articles.title: Duped on confidential funds? Prosecution spoxes say DepEd under VP Sara pulled a fast one on AFP
articles.summary: The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) was allegedly "duped" into issuing certifications that were later used by the Department of Education (DepEd) under then-secretary, Vice President Sara…

blocks.text: The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) was allegedly "duped" into issuing certifications that were later used by the Department of Education (DepEd) under then-secretary, Vice President Sara Duterte to help justify the liquidation of P15.54 million in confidential funds, House prosecutors said Tuesday.

House prosecution panel layman spokespersons Lanao del Sur 1st district Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong and Robert Ace Barbers had this to say during day 20 of Duterte’s Senate impeachment trial, which featured the testimony of Col. Manaros Boransing II.
“Isa lang po ang puwedeng ma-draw as a conclusion from the testimony of Colonel Boransing: nabudol po ang AFP,” Adiong said in no uncertain terms.
(Only one conclusion can be drawn from Colonel Boransing’s testimony: the AFP was duped.)

Boransing testified that his Jan. 1, 2024 certification to DepEd--as presented before senator-judges Tuesday--covered eight Youth Leadership Summits (YLS) and 53 Information Education Campaign (IEC) activities conducted by the 1st Infantry “Tabak” Division with other stakeholders in 2023.

He also testified that no DepEd money was released or downloaded to his division for the activities. He said he understood the document as a routine certification of participation, and only learned during an October 2024 House probe that DepEd had used it in responding to the Commission on Audit's (COA) findings on the agency’s confidential funds.
“Nabudol ang AFP dahil hiningan sila ng certification na ang paggamit noon ay i-justify nila sa COA,” Adiong said.
(The AFP was duped because they were asked for a certification that was later used to justify [the expenditure] before the COA.)

DepEd attached the Army certifications to its April 17, 2024 response to COA Audit Observation Memorandum No. 2024-015, which sought records supporting rewards totaling P15.54 million for the reported success of information-gathering or surveillance activities.
Adiong said the certifications could only establish that the activities took place, not that confidential funds were spent on them.

“The certificate only proves that there was a summit that was conducted. There was such an event that happened on that particular date. It did not prove anything as to the utilization of confidential funds. It did not prove anything that the reward was made during that event."
Likewise, Barbers underscored that the AFP certifications were obtained without the issuing officers knowing how they would eventually be used.

“The AFP was duped. Its certifications were obtained, but the officers who issued them did not even know that their documents would later be used to support the liquidation of P15 million in confidential funds,” Barbers said.

Former DepEd Undersecretary Michael Poa had acknowledged requesting then-undersecretary Nolasco Mempin to secure military certifications in connection with the liquidation of the confidential-fund expenditure.

“You cannot use an AFP certification to prove that money was spent when the AFP did not receive the money, did not spend the money, and did not know its certification would be used as proof of the expenditure,” stressed the former three-term Surigao del Norte representative.
Up to court to decide

Barbers said the impeachment court would ultimately determine whether or not the episode resulted from gross negligence or was part of a deliberate scheme to create a paper trail for the P15.54-million expenditure.
“If the AFP itself says it did not fund these activities and did not know why its certifications were being secured, then what exactly were those certifications supposed to clear?” Barbers asked.
“The documents may carry official seals and signatures, but those signatures do not magically turn an unsupported expenditure into a legitimate one,” he further said.

articles.title: Nepal flood: Death toll tops 1,000 as rescue continues
articles.summary: Nepalese authorities say 4,000 people remain unaccounted for as rescue teams with search dogs comb through mud, rocks and debris.

image.caption: Residents of the affected regions tried to save some of their belongings after the floodsImage: Sanjit Pariyar/NurPhoto/IMAGO

blocks.text: The death toll after a massive flash flood last week at the Himalayan border between Nepal and China has risen more than 1,000 people, local authorities said on Tuesday.
In Nepal, 987 deaths have already been reported, with almost 4,000 people still being unaccounted for. In China,16 deaths and 546 missing people have been reported.
The list of missing people includes some 800 foreign nationals.
Search and rescue teams are still carrying out operations despite difficult conditions and unstable terrain.
Search dogs are also taking part in the search efforts through mud, rocks and debris the flash floods left behind.
Roads were destroyed in places, cutting off access.
Efforts are also being made to locate the some 500 workers believed to be trapped inside the tunnels of twelve hydropower project tunnels, according to Nepalese authorities.
Climate change raises risk for region, PM says
The flash floods on August 28, started as a glacial collapse in the Himalayas triggered a powerful stream of rock, ice and meltwater into the valleys below.
The stream was so powerful that a seismic event of 5.2 magnitude was recorded.
Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah reacted to the disaster by emphasizing the need to fight climate change.
"This incident has indicated that the risks we face in the Himalayan region are increasing with climate change," he posted on social media.
"Therefore, this region must be alert, and at the same time, it is time for us to strongly raise the issue of disasters caused by climate change before the international community."

articles.title: Purple harvest: Safeguarding the future of the ube industry
articles.summary: As demand for ube surges worldwide, Leyte farmers call for laws that may help stop raw ube from being sold abroad

blocks.text: BAYBAY CITY, Philippines — “Hulog ng Langit.” (Unexpected blessing.)
This is how Olegario Paredes Jr., a root crop farmer from Eastern Visayas, describes the rise of ube (purple yam) in global food trends.
Ube has been steadily finding its place in the global market in recent months, earning comparisons to Japan’s matcha as a distinctly Filipino product with growing international appeal.

Transparency Market Research values the global ube market at roughly US$455 million in 2024, with projections climbing to $943 million by 2035. For farmers like Paredes, it is a chance to turn a once-ordinary crop into a reliable source of income.

One of the founders of Organikong Magsasaka at Mangingisda ng Rehiyon Otso (OMMRO), Paredes previously cultivated sweet potato and cassava at the Juanito Eco Farm School for Practical Agriculture (JEFSPA) in Kananga, Leyte.
But ube changed farming for him.
“Labing pamatuod lang, ang ube ang maoy naghatag ug maayong kita sa akoa, sa JEFSPA, ug sa uban pa nga mga farmers,” Paredes says.
(More than anything, ube has provided a good source of income for me, JEFSPA, and other farmers.)
Paredes started planting ube in 2023.
The crop that once seemed ordinary was beginning to attract an extraordinary amount of attention. Soon, the surge reached Eastern Visayas directly.

As international interest in ube spiked in 2024, the Fatima Multi-Purpose Cooperative, a cooperative that uplifts local farmers, fisherfolk, and low-income groups, began venturing into ube processing.
They reached out to Paredes for an organic supply agreement.
Soon, foreigners began visiting the region in search of ube suppliers, Paredes tells Rappler.
“Niabot sa farm, niari sa region para pagkita sa amo production area ug ang processing sa Fatima,” Paredes recalls.
(They visited the farm and came to the region to see our production area and the processing facility in Fatima.)

blocks.caption: FOREIGN INTEREST. Moroccan nationals visit Paredes’ farm to get ube supply deals. Photo Courtesy of Olegario Paredes Jr.

blocks.text: In March 2026, a Moroccan buyer who was looking for a steady source of ube powder visited Paredes. The buyer wanted 1,000 kilograms of ube every month for distribution across four countries.
That single order alone works out to roughly 80 tons of raw ube a month.
And that Moroccan buyer wasn’t an outlier.
Since he started planting ube, Paredes’ farm has fielded over 10 separate foreign inquiries.
That demand pushed him to convert more of his farmland to ube production.
As a general rule, 50 tons of ube, sold at P50 per kilo, brings in P2.5 million. However, that kind of sales, he says, is only possible with consistent monitoring and cooperative weather.
But ube farming can also be challenging.
Ube’s full production cycle—from land propagation to harvest—takes about a year, Paredes explains.
In the early days, Paredes’ crops were vulnerable to pathogens, waterlogging, and mistimed planting. All the risks are concentrated in the plant’s fragile first few months.
Starting an ube farm isn’t cheap, either. Testing and planting materials come at a cost, with each seedling running P30 to P40 which can potentially rise proportionally to the demand.

While ube is a resilient crop—which means it can handle intense weather conditions—Leyte’s frequent exposure to disruptive storms could still affect yield, particularly given that harvest season is from September to November.
To meet the demand in the long run, farmers need more than planting materials: they need proper ube production training, processing tools, and adequate funding support.

blocks.caption: RESILIENT CROP. Ube can handle intense weather conditions, but ube farmers need support to protect ube varieties and meet global demand. Photo Courtesy of JEFSPA

blocks.text: For instance, right now, farmers are having difficulties sourcing seedlings, Paredes says. To help close that gap, he started supplying planting materials beyond his own region, with buyers often offering advance payment just to reserve stock.
The Department of Agriculture’s high-value crops division also distributed over 50,000 ube seedlings to OMMRO members and other farmers in the first quarter of 2026.
Paredes and OMMRO work with various institutions, including the Department of Agriculture, Agricultural Training Institute, and other local and international agencies to address these challenges.
Among these agencies is the Philippine Root Crops Research and Training Center (PhilRootCrops), which is based at Visayas State University (VSU) in Baybay City.
Established in 1977, PhilRootCrops is the country’s national research and training center for root crops and tubers. It conducts regular cultivation workshops and crop monitoring.

The center’s director, Professor Marlon Tambis, calls ube one of the most resilient crops in the Philippines. Ube is a perennial crop with strong economic upside, he notes, yet many farmers still lack the training to make the most of it.
Tambis says the crop’s potential is outpacing the resources needed to develop it. PhilRootCrops is currently developing new cultivation technologies but the funding hasn’t kept pace.
“While we are provided by VSU of P500,000 every year, it’s still very small,” Tambis says.
“Of course, that is not enough because we are a national center. We have a national mandate. We have clients from everywhere in the Philippines. That’s just one month’s expenses,” he says.

It’s been this way for years, Tambis says. Through PhilRootCrops’ long and continued efforts, the center has managed to acquire multiple partnerships that continue to fund its operations and development, a lifeline that has kept its research going even as government funding stays thin.
Ube’s rise is an opportunity too important to let slip away, Paredes points out. Securing that opportunity starts with protecting the crop itself.

blocks.caption: SUPPORT SYSTEM. PhilRootCrops conducts regular cultivation workshops and crop monitoring to support ube farmers.

blocks.text: First, Paredes wants ube formally declared a priority crop by law, a status he believes would unlock more structured, long-term government support. He also calls for safeguarding the country’s ube varieties, beginning with a stop to raw ube from being sold abroad.
“Unta, ang gobyerno, dili nila i-allow na ibaligya sa gawas ang raw ube. Kung pwede, powder or processed product lang para maprotect nato ato mga gipananom na mga ube varieties,” says Paredes.
(Hopefully, the government will not allow raw ube to be sold abroad. If possible, only powdered or processed products should be exported so we can protect the ube varieties that we have cultivated.)

On August 22, Leyte 4th District Representative Richard Gomez filed House Bill No. 10225, known as the Philippine Ube Industry Development Act, to declare purple yam a national priority crop and boost production and exports.
Then there’s the matter of people.
Small farmer groups need to be organized and backed with real support so that big companies don’t end up monopolizing the industry and dictating prices at farmers’ expense.
Paredes says there should be a dedicated agency to help farmers navigate exports and move faster.
For years, farmers struggled with low demand for their crops. With ube, for the first time in a long while, that’s no longer the problem.
Whether Eastern Visayas farmers will be able to take full advantage of this demand depends on the support they get. – Rappler.com

Jennifer Jezreel Kaye Pading is an economics student at Visayas State University in Baybay City in Leyte. An Aries Rufo Journalism Fellow for 2026, she is also the executive editor of Amaranth and community officer of AYEJ-Leyte Panaad Ha Sinirangan.

articles.title: UK long-term borrowing costs hit 28-year high
articles.summary: Yield on 30-year government bonds jumps to 5.88%, the highest since 1998, in bond rout triggered by global factors

blocks.text: The UK government’s long-term borrowing costs jumped to their highest level since early 1998 on Tuesday as a global bond sell-off gathered pace.
The yield – in effect the interest rate – on 30-year UK government bonds, known as gilts, hit 5.89% as traders fretted about a fresh increase in oil prices driving up inflation.
Ten-year gilt yields were at 5.25%, the highest level since the global financial crisis of 2008.

Higher yields progressively increase the cost of financing the government’s debt, and if sustained these would pass through to the Office for Budget Responsibility’s forecasts for the chancellor, John Healey, when he delivers his 28 October budget.
The moves underline the tricky global backdrop facing Andy Burnham’s government as he returns to Westminster promising to help consumers with the cost of living.

The bond sell-off was driven by international factors. Japanese 10-year yields hit their highest level since the 1990s amid expectations that the Bank of Japan will have to raise interest rates to control inflation.

Investors also appeared to be responding partly to higher oil prices, which were up 1.7% at $92 after a fresh exchange of fire in the Iran conflict over the weekend. Higher energy costs drive up inflation, potentially forcing central banks to respond.
Finance ministers and central bankers from the G20 major economies are meeting in North Carolina to discuss the state of the global economy.
The US Treasury secretary Scott Bessent, who chaired the G20 meeting of his peers, hinted afterwards that Japanese policymakers could be about to raise interest rates.
“I have information that the market doesn’t have, and it’s my belief that the Japanese government and the Bank of Japan will do the things that will lead to a stronger yen,” he said.
In August the US and Japan took the rare step of intervening jointly in global foreign exchange markets in an attempt to prop up the yen, but the Japanese currency subsequently resumed its slide.
after newsletter promotion

Expectations of higher interest rates were also piqued by a speech from the US Federal Reserve chair, Kevin Warsh, on Friday warning that the central bank would still have “work to do” if inflation did not return to target.

As well as fretting about future inflation, bond investors also appear to be concerned about runaway deficits in the US, where the Trump administration has cut taxes and is having to hand back much of the revenue from swingeing trade tariffs.
Bessent, who is keen to push down on long-term US borrowing costs, has suggested the administration may have plans to cut spending, but no policy has yet been announced.

articles.title: Army official 'surprised' his certification used to justify P15-M VP Sara's confi fund
articles.summary: Army official 'surprised' his certification used to justify VP Sara's P15-M confi fund

blocks.text: Published September 1, 2026 6:44pm

Army Colonel Magtanggol Panopio on Tuesday said he was surprised that the certification he issued in December 2023 was used to justify the Department of Education (DepEd)'s P15.5 million confidential fund spending on Day 20 of the impeachment trial.

It was then DepEd Undersecretary Michael Poa who told lawmakers that he asked for such military certifications from then Education Undersecretary Nolasco Mempin to justify DepEd’s confidential fund expenses on rewards for informants during a House panel inquiry in October 2024.
As a result, it was Mempin who asked his subordinates for such certifications.

“Nalaman po namin iyan noong humarap kami sa Congress, noong nagkaroon po ng congressional hearing sa confidential intelligence fund ng Department of Education, Your Honor. Medyo nagulat po kami, kasi iyong certification po namin is only for the certification that we conducted the Youth Leadership Summit,” Panopio said.

(We became aware of it when we faced Congress for an inquiry on confidential and intelligence fund of the DepEd. We were slightly surprised, because our certification only stated that we conducted the Youth Leadership Summit.)
“Hindi po namin sine-certify anything about money or funds, Your Honor,” Panopio testified.
(We did not certifying anything that involves money.)

Before Panopio took the stand, military Colonel Maranos Boransing II also testified that the certification he issued to Poa as requested by Nolasco did not attest to the propriety of DepEd’s confidential fund spending.

“No, Maam. The certification was [for] their (DepEd) and other stakeholders' participation in the Youth Leadership Summit and the Information Education Communication Campaign,” Boransing said in response to the question of Senator judge Hontiveros if the certification was a vouch for DepEd’s proper use of its P15.5 million of confidential funds.
'In good faith'

During the October 2024 House inquiry, Poa said he asked Mempin for such military certifications “in good faith” since the Commission on Audit was asking the DepEd to respond to an audit observation memorandum (AOM) that questioned the said confidential fund spending on rewards for informants.

“To be perfectly candid, Your Honor, ang dami ko pong trabaho sa DepEd. One of them was to comply with AOM. I'm not using that as an excuse. So. kung ano pong documentation na available at that time na nasa OSEC (Office of the Secretary) or binigay sa amin, binigay sa OSEC, ‘yun fact na yun po... ‘yung impression ko na there was already coordination and information from DepEd,” Poa said.
(I have a lot of work in DepEd...I just used the documentation available in our office...I had the impression that there was already coordination and information from DepEd.) —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: ‘Survivor Philippines,’ ‘StarStruck’ director Monti Parungao dies at 58
articles.summary: Film and television director Monti Puno Parungao, known for his work on GMA Network programs “Survivor Philippines,” “StarStruck,” and “Dear Uge,” died Tuesday, September 1. He was 58. Parungao died…

blocks.text: Film and television director Monti Puno Parungao, known for his work on GMA Network programs “Survivor Philippines,” “StarStruck,” and “Dear Uge,” died Tuesday, September 1. He was 58.
Parungao died at his home in Quezon City after battling Stage 4 colon cancer, according to his brother Hardy Parungao.
The Parungao family announced his passing on social media.
“It is with great sadness that the Parungao family announces the passing of Edgardo Puno Parungao III (Direk Monti) on September 1, 2026,” the family said.
“Details of a service to celebrate and honor his life will follow. The family is grateful for your prayers, love and support,” it added.
Parungao began working at GMA in 1987 and went on to build a career spanning television, film, advertising, theater, and events.
He was among the directors of “Survivor Philippines,” the local version of the international reality competition franchise, and also worked on “StarStruck,” GMA’s long-running talent search.
He also directed episodes of “Dear Uge,” the comedy anthology series hosted by Eugene Domingo.
Beyond television, Parungao worked as a screenwriter, producer, editor, and director. He was also known for LGBTQ-themed films, including “Sagwan” and "Bayaw".
Parungao underwent several surgeries in recent months as he battled cancer.

MANILA, Philippines – The defense team of Vice President Sara Duterte maintained that there was “no irregularity” in the Department of Education‘s use of Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) certifications to support its confidential fund expenses.

“Of course, on our side, since we’re advocating for the client, there’s really no irregularity. But this is not advocating through the media. That has been our position in the answer,” defense counsel and deputy spokesperson Justin Nicol Gular told reporters on Tuesday, September 1.

The Senate impeachment trial is in the middle of hearing the prosecution’s evidence about Duterte’s alleged misuse of the confidential funds of the Office of the Vice President and the DepEd when she headed the agency.

On Tuesday, the prosecution presented witnesses from the AFP — Colonel Manaros Boransing II and Colenel Magtanggol Panopio — to prove that the Philippine Army conducted youth summits without DepEd’s confidential funds, and that Duterte and her office allegedly misrepresented the AFP certifications issued to the DepEd about these activities.

blocks.caption: ‘Nabudol ang AFP’: Prosecution accuses Sara Duterte-led DepEd of misrepresentation

blocks.text: Boransing and Panopio issued certifications proving the success of the AFP’s youth summits in partnership with agencies like DepEd. However, DepEd allegedly submitted these certifications to the Commission on Audit (COA) for the liquidation of the agency’s P15.54-million funds.

Although he said that there was nothing irregular on the use of certifications, Gular refused to belabor on that point, explaining the recent sub judice reminder from the impeachment court. Gular, however, said that the public is entitled to interpret what happened during the trial proper.

During the trial’s 20th day, defense lead counsel Sheila Sison shared the contents of the AFP’s certifications. She noted that the certifications of Panopio and Lieutenant Colonel Carlos Sangdaan Jr. stated that the projects were done in collaboration with other agencies like DepEd.
“… The certification was also issued for what legal, whatever legal purpose it may serve,” Sison added.

“But that statement, just basically means what it says — for whatever legal purpose it may be used for. And you can find this in several documents, not only in the document tackled by the impeachment court,” Gular explained.

blocks.caption: ‘No irregularity’ in use of AFP certification for DepEd confi funds liquidation – defense

blocks.text: In the trial, the DepEd’s credit notice from COA was again brought up.

On August 11, COA state auditor Xylene del Campo confirmed that COA’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Auditing Office (ICFAO) cleared DepEd’s P75-million confidential funds through a credit notice.

Presiding officer Chiz Escudero, on Tuesday, clarified with the parties if the P15 million DepEd funds in question were part of the P75-million cleared funds. Both defense counsel Lindon Miguel Bacquel and prosecution counsel Reynaldo Robles responded in the affirmative.

“I think what’s important is just to ensure that that document exists in public records. And we just want that public record or that document, the credit notice to be highlighted as well that it is included as one of the documents, as among those that senator-judges should consider during the impeachment trial,” Gular explained in a mix of Filipino and English, when asked about the credit notice’s relevance.

However, Robles reiterated Del Campo’s August remarks, stating that COA and ICFAO are still studying the possibility of referring the matter to its fraud audit unit. Meaning, COA’s credit notice is not yet conclusive.

blocks.caption: ‘No irregularity’ in use of AFP certification for DepEd confi funds liquidation – defense

blocks.text: Bacquel was the defense’s assigned lawyer for the supposed cross-examination of both Boransing and Panopio but he declined to cross-examine the AFP witnesses.
Gular explained that cross-examination is done by the defense to test the credibility of the prosecution’s witnesses.

blocks.caption: ‘No irregularity’ in use of AFP certification for DepEd confi funds liquidation – defense

blocks.text: “But if we do not see any issue as to the testimony of the witness…. Lawyers sometimes do not conduct cross-examination anymore,” Gular said in a mix of Filipino and English. “That’s the reason why we don’t conduct cross-examination.” – Rappler.com

articles.title: No budget for new flood control projects in 2027 -- JV Ejercito
articles.summary: Senate Finance Committee Chairperson Joseph Victor “JV” Ejercito said on Tuesday that no funds will be allocated in 2027 for new flood control projects, with funding instead focused on completing…

blocks.text: Published September 1, 2026 6:33pm

Senate Finance Committee Chairperson Joseph Victor “JV” Ejercito said on Tuesday that no funds will be allocated in 2027 for new flood control projects, with funding instead focused on completing unfinished infrastructure and addressing gaps in flood mitigation, particularly in Luzon.
In the 2026 national budget, funding for new flood mitigation projects was withheld following the exposure of anomalous and so-called ghost flood control projects.

However, Ejercito said funding for flood control projects would still be necessary next year, given the severe flooding the country recently experienced amid heavy rains brought by the Southwest Monsoon (Habagat).
"But we saw the impact. When the rains continue, Central Luzon—from Tarlac, Pampanga, and Bulacan to Metro Manila—is really underwater," he said.
“In my view, we have to resume funding, but only for uncompleted projects. We should complete unfinished flood control projects and address the gaps,” Ejercito added.
The senator said that projects to be continued must be aligned with a master plan, supported by a feasibility study and located in any of the country’s 10 most flood-prone provinces.

He added that if a master plan is not submitted, or if a project to be continued is not included in the plan, it may still proceed if it has the required approval from the regional or provincial development council to establish its necessity.

“(hat’s why we’re requiring Regional Development Council approval, or at least provincial council approval, so that the province itself knows that the project is needed. If the RDC or provincial council approves it, it means the project is necessary,” Ejercito said.
“No new projects, complete all the uncompleted projects and close the gaps,” he added.
The senator said resuming funding for unfinished projects would also help accelerate infrastructure spending.
He said the economic slowdown was an unintended consequence of the sharp decline in public spending in previous quarters following the exposure of the flood control scandal.
“We now have to accelerate spending, but at the same time, without, of course, sacrificing accountability. We still need to monitor it closely,” Ejercito said.
He urged civil society organizations and other watchdog groups to coordinate with authorities if they identify suspicious projects so these can be properly investigated by the concerned agencies.

Under the proposed 2027 national budget, P107.4 billion is allocated to the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) for flood control projects to maintain, repair and enhance existing infrastructure.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Philippines in running for full MCC compact after securing $60-million energy grant
articles.summary: Fresh from securing approval for a $60-million United States (US) grant for energy-sector reforms, the Philippines is now among 91 countries in the running for a full-fledged Millennium Challenge…

blocks.text: Fresh from securing approval for a $60-million United States (US) grant for energy-sector reforms, the Philippines is now among 91 countries in the running for a full-fledged Millennium Challenge Corp. (MCC) compact, potentially opening the door to a much larger development grant similar to the $434-million package it received more than a decade ago.

In its Candidate Country Report for Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 published last Monday, Aug. 31, MCC included the Philippines among countries that may be considered for its flagship compact assistance program.

The Philippines’ inclusion as a candidate, however, does not yet guarantee another compact, as MCC will still assess which countries will qualify and ultimately be selected for negotiations with the US before year-end.

In choosing eligible countries, MCC considers their commitment to just and democratic governance, economic freedom, and investments in their people, as well as their potential to reduce poverty and generate economic growth.
Candidate countries must also have gross national income (GNI) per capita of no more than $8,105 for FY 2027 and remain eligible to receive US economic assistance.

The development comes just over two months after MCC’s board approved the Philippines’ second threshold program, providing about $60 million in grant financing to address policy and institutional constraints in the energy sector.
Unlike loans, MCC grants do not have to be repaid by recipient governments.
Threshold programs are smaller grants focused on policy, regulatory, and institutional reforms, while compacts are MCC’s larger, five-year grants aimed at reducing poverty through economic growth.

Department of Finance (DOF) Secretary Frederick D. Go earlier told Manila Bulletin that the latest threshold program “serves as a critical stepping stone toward qualifying for a future MCC compact program.”

The $60-million threshold grant will finance the Energy Development Governance Efficiency Project, aimed at removing bottlenecks that delay power projects and strengthening the reliability of the country’s electricity supply.

The program will support reforms to streamline energy planning, programming, and permitting, alongside targeted investments aimed at improving energy-sector operations as well as encouraging greater private investment.
The Philippines was first selected to develop the latest threshold program in December 2023 and was reselected in December 2024 before receiving final approval from MCC’s board last June 24.

The latest grant is the Philippines’ second threshold program. Its first, implemented from 2006 to 2009 during the Arroyo administration through the now-defunct US Agency for International Development (USAID), focused on improving fiscal policy and strengthening the government’s fight against corruption.

That program provided training, technical support, as well as information technology (IT) systems to investigators, prosecutors, revenue officials, and anti-corruption agencies. More than 3,000 government personnel received specialized training, while all nine performance targets were exceeded, including those covering corruption convictions, tax administration, and anti-smuggling enforcement.
The Philippines subsequently graduated to a full-scale MCC compact worth $434 million, implemented from 2011 to 2016 during the Benigno Aquino III administration.
The five-year compact financed projects to modernize government business processes, rehabilitate roads, and support community-driven development initiatives.

During the administration of former President Rodrigo R. Duterte, however, the Philippines did not secure a second MCC compact after the US aid agency deferred its reselection in 2016 due to “significant concerns around rule of law and civil liberties,” amid human rights concerns surrounding the deadly war on drugs.

articles.title: Samar fisherman turns over two green sea turtles caught on net
articles.summary: TACLOBAN CITY — What began as an accidental catch ended with two green sea turtles safely back into the sea after a fisherman voluntarily turned them over to authorities. On Monday, August 31, at…

blocks.text: TACLOBAN CITY — What began as an accidental catch ended with two green sea turtles safely back into the sea after a fisherman voluntarily turned them over to authorities.
On Monday, August 31, at around 4:20 p.m., fisherman Rendel Amarilla of Rawis-Anibong here accidentally caught two green sea turtles in his net while fishing near Barangay Amandayehan, Basey, Samar.
Rather than keeping the turtles, Amarilla brought them to the Fishery Law Enforcement Team (FLET) office on Tuesday morning, Sept. 1.
The turtles, later named “Bea” and “Heaven,” measured approximately 46 centimeters and 44 centimeters in length, respectively.
Personnel from the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) examined both turtles and found them to be healthy and in good condition.
After the necessary information was documented, the turtles were fitted with identification tags to support monitoring and future identification.
After the assessment, documentation, and tagging were completed, Bea and Heaven were safely released back into the sea.
The incident highlights the important role that fishermen and coastal communities play in protecting marine wildlife.
Accidental capture can happen during fishing activities, but the prompt and responsible turnover of marine animals can give them a better chance of surviving and returning to their natural habitat.

Green sea turtles are marine reptiles that spend most of their lives in the ocean and play an important role in healthy marine ecosystems. Like other sea turtles, they face threats from accidental capture in fishing gear, habitat degradation, pollution, and other human activities. INQ

articles.title: Russian attack hits rail workers in new deadly strikes on Kyiv
articles.summary: Ukrainian officials say 20 people, including two children, were injured in the capital and the wider region.

blocks.text: "Every day spent in war pushes humanity back, and every step taken towards peace fills humanity with new hope and enthusiasm," Modi said at a security summit in Kyrgyzstan.
Modi, whose country's economy depends heavily on discounted oil from Moscow, has made several similar pleas to Putin since he launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
Overnight in Kyiv, eight people were killed and fires were reported in three city districts.
Another four people were killed in the nearby town of Boryspil where a residential building was hit.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Tuesday morning that nearly 350 rescue workers had been working through the night in Kyiv and the surrounding region after the latest strikes.
In a post on social media, he said Russia had fired a "significant number of jet drones and ballistic missiles".
The strikes mark the sixth day of sustained Russian drone and missile attacks on Kyiv, in what appears to be a strategy aimed at exhausting Ukrainian air defences and undermining civilian morale.
Russia's military warned over the weekend that its forces were preparing to carry out "massive" strikes on Ukrainian energy facilities.
Eight other Ukrainian regions were attacked, Zelensky said, adding that an Indian national was among the casualties.
Ukraine's Interior Minister Ivan Vyhivsky later said the Indian man - who turned 26 on Tuesday - was killed in Boryspil.
The overnight attacks come after 38 people were killed in Russian strikes on a weapons depot in the Kyiv region on Friday, causing shells, mines and drones to detonate.
Separately, a drone attack hit a major Russian Baltic Sea port in Ust-Luga, triggering a fire, Leningrad regional Governor Aleksandr Drozdenko said.
Ukraine says targets like Ust-Luga - which handles millions of tons of petroleum products each year - are legitimate as they help finance Moscow's war effort.

articles.title: Palace: Marcos spent time with wife, but not during peak of flooding
articles.summary: Malacañang has set the record straight about a video of President Marcos singing during First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos’ birthday celebration on Aug. 26, saying the event took place before heavy rains…

blocks.text: Malacañang has set the record straight about a video of President Marcos singing during First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos’ birthday celebration on Aug. 26, saying the event took place before heavy rains hit Luzon, causing severe flooding.

Palace Press Officer and Communications Undersecretary Claire Castro clarified that the event, which surfaced over the weekend, did not occur during the peak of flooding in Metro Manila and Central Luzon provinces.
Castro said there is no truth to the narrative detractors allegedly want to spread.

"Naganap po ang pagharana ng Pangulo, kay First Lady, hindi po ito iyong kasagsagan noong malakas na ulan, hindi po ito kasagsagan ng pagbaha (The President’s serenade for the First Lady did not take place at the height of the heavy rains. It was not during the height of the flooding)," Castro said in a Palace briefing on Tuesday, Sept. 1.
The Palace spokesperson alleged that it was the message circulated by those who spread the video, whom she called "detractors and obstructionists."

"So, kumalat at ang dumating na mensahe sa iba nating mga kababayan ay nangharana ang Pangulo kay First Lady noong gabing malakas ang ulan at noong gabing bumabaha ng todo-todo dito sa Central Luzon at sa Metro Manila. Hindi po iyan ang katotohanan (The message that reached some of our fellow Filipinos was that the President serenaded the First Lady on the night when heavy rains were falling and when severe flooding was occurring here in Central Luzon and Metro Manila. That is not the truth," Castro stressed.
Castro said she cannot blame the public for calling the video insensitive as they only reacted to what the detractors wanted them to see.
"So, naiintintihan po namin kayo, kasi iba po iyong kwentong naipalabas ( We understand you because a different story was being portrayed)," she said.

"Pero, sana makita rin po natin na sa buong linggo, hanggang kahapon kahit walang pasok at holiday, ang Pangulo po ay tutok hindi po nagpapabaya ang Pangulo para maibigay lahat ang pangangailangan ng ating mga kababayan, lalong-lalo na iyong mga naapektuhan (But I hope we can also see that throughout the entire week, up until yesterday, even though there were no classes and it was a holiday, the President remained focused and did not neglect his duties to provide everything our fellow Filipinos needed, especially those who were affected)," she added.
'The President gave only a little of his time'
Castro also clarified that the President serenaded the First Lady after finishing his work.
She pointed out that the President dedicated only a small portion of his time to the celebration.

"Kung nagharana man ang Pangulo, para sa kanyang asawa at mga kasama ang ilang malalapit na kamag-anak, kaunting oras lang po ang ibinigay ng Pangulo, para sa kanyang pamilya, para sa kanyang asawa para i-celebrate ang buhay (If the President did serenade his wife, in the presence of a few close relatives and companions, the President gave only a little of his time to his family and to his wife to celebrate her life)," Castro said.

"At hindi po nagpabaya ang Pangulo sa kaunting oras na ito na ibinigay para sa kanyang asawa (During that brief time he set aside for his wife, the President did not neglect his responsibilities)," Castro added.
The Palace mouthpiece further clarified that even though the President attended the event, "he continued to monitor the situation and what the weather conditions might be."
"Pero at that time, wala pong masamang panahon, iyon po ang dapat nating linawin (At that time, however, there was no bad weather. That is what we need to clarify)," Castro said.

articles.title: Man, 23, appears in court charged with murder after Teesside house fire
articles.summary:
Seven-year-old girl and aunt, 34, died and four others were injured in blaze near Middlesbrough last week

A 23-year-old man has appeared in court charged with murdering a seven-year-old girl…
articles.byline: Josh Halliday North of England editor

blocks.text: A 23-year-old man has appeared in court charged with murdering a seven-year-old girl and her aunt who died in a house fire.
Natalie McDonald, 34, and Valentina Foster died and four other people were injured in the blaze in Grangetown, near Middlesbrough, in the early hours of 26 August.
Jaden Wright, of no fixed address, appeared before Teesside magistrates court on Tuesday for a hearing that lasted less than two minutes.
Wright briefly greeted his solicitor as he was brought into the dock before he was remanded in custody to appear before Teesside crown court on Thursday.

The court clerk outlined that he faces two murder charges, two counts of grievous bodily harm with intent and two charges of attempted grievous bodily harm with intent. The charges relate to the six people who were in the house, two of whom cannot be identified by the media due to their age.
The clerk said Wright faced a separate charge of intentional strangulation over an incident said to have happened on the day before the fire.

Cleveland police said on Friday that a 48-year-old woman was in the Royal Victoria Infirmary in a “critical but stable” condition after the fire and a 27-year-old man was at James Cook university hospital receiving treatment. Two teenage girls were discharged after sustaining non-life-threatening injuries.

Katie Smith, the senior investigating officer from Northumbria police, said: “This has been a truly tragic incident and my thoughts remain with the families of all those involved. I would like to thank local residents for their support and patience during this complex investigation. Anyone who may still have information, or has any concerns, can still submit information using the major incident public portal.”

Katie Nicholson, the chief crown prosecutor for CPS North East, said: “Our prosecutors have worked closely with Cleveland police to establish that there is sufficient evidence to bring this case to court. We remind all concerned that proceedings against the defendant are active and he has the right to a fair trial. It is vital that there should be no reporting, commentary or sharing of information which could in anyway prejudice these proceedings.”
A 31-year-old man who was also arrested in connection with the case was released without charge on Sunday.

articles.title: Teen girl charged with murder over recording of San Diego mosque attack
articles.summary: Prosecutors say the 17-year-old from North Carolina also published a manifesto from the two teenage gunmen in the 18 May attack.

blocks.text: A 17-year-old girl has been charged with murder by aiding and abetting after prosecutors say she recorded a livestream of an attack on a San Diego mosque that left three people dead.
Prosecutors say the girl also published a manifesto from two teenage gunmen who carried out the attack on the Islamic Center of San Diego on 18 May.
The teenager, from North Carolina, was arrested last week and indicted by a grand jury on Monday, according to Forsyth County District Attorney Jim O'Neill.
Speaking at a news conference, O'Neill said: "The thought of her going back to school, with the weekend approaching, holy days approaching, we didn't know what she was capable of."

The teenager now faces three murder charges and one count of conspiracy. O'Neill explained that under North Carolina law, a person accused of aiding and abetting a crime can be held criminally responsible in the same way as the person who carried it out.
Authorities say the attack was carried out by two males - aged 17 and 18 - who opened fire at the mosque, before taking their own lives.
O'Neill said the pair had two aims that day: "Number one, to kill as many people as possible on that day. Secondly, they wanted this carnage and destruction recorded ... livestreamed."
A security guard at the mosque, Amin Abdullah, exchanged gunfire with the attackers and initiated a lockdown, helping protect around 140 children who were inside the building.
Abdullah and two worshippers - Mansour Kaziha and Nader Awad, who drew the attentions of the shooters in a parking lot - were fatally shot.
San Diego Police Chief Scott Wahl previously described Abdullah's actions as "heroic", saying they had "undoubtedly" saved lives.

According to investigators, the shooters recorded the attack using cameras mounted on GoPro-style helmets. O'Neill said the pair had also planned further attacks "at a local Jewish temple and finally at a predominantly African American high school".
Authorities said the teenagers had an arsenal of around 30 guns and a crossbow, which investigators say were taken from one of the shooter's parents.
The attackers also left behind writings containing racist and antisemitic views, as well as references to white supremacist ideologies.
The document, which was reviewed by the BBC's US news partner CBS News, pointed to a gunman who murdered 51 people at two mosques in Christchurch, New Zealand, in 2019, as one of their models.

MANILA, Philippines – OpenAI on Monday, August 31, denied allegations it had stolen some Apple trade secrets, adding that the iPhone maker did not show former employees had taken confidential information.

Apple’s July complaint against OpenAI and Tang Tan and Chang Liu, former Apple employees and now OpenAI workers, stems from assertions that OpenAI took on a broad effort to systematically acquire and exploit Apple’s confidential information through ex-employees.

According to a Reuters report, OpenAI said Apple’s lawsuit intends to slow down a potential competitor while also discouraging Apple employees from leaving the company, with OpenAI taking on some 400 former employees of the iPhone maker to boost its hardware initiative according to filings from both companies.

OpenAI said Monday that Apple’s encouragement of the use of personal iCloud accounts to access documents and perform work tasks makes separating personal and company information difficult, adding that Apple’s policy of immediately escorting departing employees from the premises does not give them the time to return company devices, turn over responsibilities, and move over work files to the right people within the company.

Liu said in a filing that his access to Apple documents after his departure was done to help former colleagues within the company to locate files or answer work-related queries, and adding Apple employees kept contacting him for help after his departure. Meanwhile, Tan said he only kept non-confidential documents, like an employee departure checklist, after he left the company.
OpenAI on August 3 also denied wrongdoing and published messages and email correspondences on their website that support what Liu has said — that he was helping his former coworkers.
OpenAI said that employees “can leave a company like Apple that has struggled to ⁠adopt ​AI and move to an exciting startup that builds innovative products.”
“Apple may not like those choices. But it cannot claim those choices are unlawful, and it cannot use its own sloppy ​procedures to blame others for its own mess,” OpenAI added. – Rappler.com

articles.title: No prosecutor resignations as panel adjusts to sub judice rule
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — For the first time since the Senate Impeachment Court issued a ruling for a stricter sub judice rule implementation last Aug. 26, a member of the prosecution team — Manila Rep.…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — For the first time since the Senate Impeachment Court issued a ruling for a stricter sub judice rule implementation last Aug. 26, a member of the prosecution team — Manila Rep. Joel Chua — appeared before an official press conference.

However, during the briefing after Vice President Sara Duterte’s trial on Tuesday, Chua’s answers seemed to be measured and calculated — often pausing several times before replying to questions, earning laughs from the crowd.

“Ang mahal ng penalty (The penalty is expensive),” Chua said after being asked about the testimonies of Col. Manaros Boransing II and Col. Magtanggol Panopio, two Philippine Army (PA) officials who issued certifications on Army-funded youth summits which were used by Vice President Sara Duterte’s office used to justify confidential expenses.

It appears this will be the way forward for the prosecution, as Chua said no one will resign and be appointed as a full-time spokesperson, contrary to the panel’s initial plans.“Well we have decided na wala na lang munang magre-resign and kasi no’ng una isa ‘yan sa mga naging discussions kung ganoon ang mangyayari, kaya nga po nasabi ni Congressman Zia (Alonto Adiong), kasi ‘yon ang talagang unang option,” Chua said.

(Well we have decided that no one will resign, because one of the initial considerations was that we will adopt such a measure, which is why Congressman Zia (Alonto Adiong) mentioned this because it was one of the first options.)

“In fact may mga sinasabi, suggestions ‘yong mga private prosecutor at public prosecutor na may ilan na pagre-resignin para maging spokesperson. Pero after considering everything — tutal, isang buwan na lang kung masusunod ‘yong ating target, eh siguro susubukan na lang namin to explain in a way na hindi tayo magta-touch sa merit,” he added.

(In fact, there were suggestions that some of the private prosecutors and public prosecutors will resign to become spokespersons. But after considering everything — since we have a few months left on our target, maybe we will just try to explain in a way that we will not touch on the merit.)

The prosecution’s setup, Chua said, is that they will have a member of the prosecution panel to sit during press briefings and another spokesperson or House member to explain matters that may be considered sub judice.
After all, Chua said that not every question asked during press briefings are related to the merits of the case.

“Kaya kung makikita ninyo may isang public (prosecutor) at may isang spokes(person) […] kasi too late na kung magbabawas tayo tapos magdadagdag pa, sino pa ba naman ang idadagdag natin to maintain ‘yon 11(-person) prosecution team?” he said.

(If you will see our setup now, there is a public (prosecutor) and one spokes(person) […] because it is too late already, if we will cut and add prosecutors, who will we add now to maintain that 11(-person) prosecution team?)

“Well hindi naman sa comfortable pero baka mamaya may magtatanong tungkol sa procedure aspect outside the merit of the case, so I can answer that. Kasi hindi naman lahat puro merito ang tanong, so may mga iba tinatanong — kagaya po ng tinanong kanina, na ano na ‘yong susunod,” he added.

(Well it’s not a state of being comfortable but we were anticipating that some people may ask about the procedural aspect outside the merit of the case, so I can answer that. Because not all questions are about merits, so there may be other questions — like what was asked earlier, as to what is the next issue.)

Discussions on the sub judice rule came after a manifestation from lead counsel for respondent Sheila Sison last August 12, when she questioned counsel for prosecution Amando Virgil Ligutan over a Facebook post where he said that a “principle all lawyers and law students know by heart” is that “misleading questions are not allowed even on cross-examination.”

Sison said Ligutan did not name anyone, but he was clearly referring to counsel for respondent Kristine Ferrer — particularly the exchange between her and another prosecution counsel. Atty. Lorna Kapunan.
LINK TO POST:

Sison was pointing to a tense moment during the cross-examination of state auditor Xylene Mae del Campo, where Kapunan strongly objected to Ferrer’s habit of cutting the witness off before she was even able to provide an answer to the questions.

As she insisted that Ferrer is mistaken in stating that she can throw questions answerable by yes or no only, Kapunan said that “misleading questions are not allowed.” After this, Ferrer responded by saying that “it is allowed.”

But Sison said that Ferrer’s “it is allowed” quip was not a reply to Kapunan’s “misleading questions are not allowed” even on cross-examination statement — making Ligutan’s social media post as something done in “bad faith.”

In response to this manifestation, Presiding Officer and Senator-judge Francis Escudero said last Wednesday that while they would no longer punish previous violations, the ruling will apply to all parties moving forward.

For senator-judges, Escudero clarified that they may still ask questions during trial where they usually do their interjections but must do so with “cold neutrality”. Escudero reminded them that they must not only be impartial but must also appear impartial.

For lawyers representing the prosecution and defense, public reprimand with admonition awaits sub judice rule violators on their first strike, while a monetary fine of P30,000 with the possibility of being restricted from speaking, objecting, or examining witnesses on the floor may be imposed upon them on their subsequent violations.

The ruling prompted the prosecution to reconsider sending out prosecutors to press briefings. Alonto Adiong, a spokesperson for the panel, said there are still ongoing discussions on whether there will be changes to the composition of the prosecution panel.

Last Friday, prosecution member and Bicol Saro party-list Rep. Terry Ridon clarified that none of the public and private prosecutors for Duterte’s impeachment trial will resign, as the panel is moving towards adding more spokespersons who will not be bound by the court’s sub judice rule. /mr

articles.title: BIR destroys illicit vape products with P1.54-M tax liability
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) Revenue Region No. 6, which covers the City of Manila and Palawan, destroyed 240,550 illicit vape products with an estimated tax liability…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) Revenue Region No. 6, which covers the City of Manila and Palawan, destroyed 240,550 illicit vape products with an estimated tax liability of P1.539 billion on Aug. 24 at the Digama Waste Management Facility in Porac, Pampanga.

“Enforcement does not end with seizure. We must permanently remove illicit vape products from the market and hold accountable those behind their illegal manufacture, importation, distribution, and sale,” BIR Commissioner Charlito Martin R. Mendoza said in a statement on Tuesday.
According to Revenue Region No. 6 Regional Director Remir Macatangay, BIR Manila has expanded its enforcement operations from individual retail establishments to warehouses.

“We started with retail stores and expanded to warehouses. This led to our operation against Tap Fog Philippines, the largest single illicit vape enforcement operation conducted by the BIR to date. Some of the products seized in that operation were among those destroyed today,” Macatangay said.

The destruction, the BIR statement said, should send a clear message: “Neither unlawful traders nor unfavorable weather conditions can hinder the BIR’s commitment to safeguarding government revenue, protecting compliant businesses, and keeping illicit vape products out of the market.” /atm

articles.title: Mayon sulfur emissions spike raises eruption concern
articles.summary: LEGAZPI CITY — Sulfur emissions from Mayon Volcano have surged to more than twice their average level since Aug. 5, prompting the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs) to warn…

blocks.text: LEGAZPI CITY — Sulfur emissions from Mayon Volcano have surged to more than twice their average level since Aug. 5, prompting the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs) to warn of possible renewed eruptive activity.

In its bulletin on Tuesday, Sept. 1, the agency said Mayon released 7,115 tons of sulfur dioxide on Aug. 31, the second-highest emission recorded since volcanic gas concentrations began declining on July 16.
Since Mayon was placed under Alert Level 2, or moderate unrest, on Aug. 5, its sulfur emissions have averaged 3,844 tons a day, Phivolcs said.

The surge in gas emissions coincided with a slight increase in low-frequency volcanic earthquakes, with 12 recorded as of midnight Tuesday. Phivolcs attributed the earthquakes to volcanic degassing, while real-time seismic energy release remained at background levels.
The agency also detected short-term swelling or pressurization in Mayon’s northern and eastern flanks based on electronic tilt monitoring.
“Elevated volcanic sulfur dioxide emissions could forewarn of a potential shift to renewed eruptive activity at the summit crater,” it said.
A renewed eruption could generate pyroclastic density currents or uson, rockfall, ballistic fragments, and widespread ashfall, it added.

Phivolcs said Mayon remained under Alert Level 2 but urged residents and local governments to prepare for a possible escalation to Alert Level 3, particularly those in areas vulnerable to pyroclastic density currents.

It reiterated that entry into the six-kilometerPermanent Danger Zone is prohibited and warned of possible lahars and sediment-laden streamflows along channels draining Mayon, particularly during prolonged heavy rains or a simultaneous explosive eruption.
Pilots were also advised to avoid flying near the summit, as ash and ballistic fragments from a sudden eruption could endanger aircraft. /mcm

articles.title: US irks Germany, Europe with Russian G20 invite, press bans
articles.summary: Russia's finance minister is at the G20 meeting in Asheville but some key US press corps members are not. The mood was already tense amid the lengthy Iran war and Trump's renewed beef with neighbor…

image.caption: The two-day summit in North Carolina come as Donald Trump has Iran, but also his nearest neighbor Canada, in his economic crosshairsImage: Allison Joyce/AFP

blocks.text: G20 finance ministers and central bank heads gathered in Asheville, North Carolina for two days of talks.

The session is being overshadowed by dissatisfaction over the White House welcoming Russia to the meeting but not some critical reporters, the war with Iran and its economic fallout, and Donald Trump's latest trade dispute with Canada.
Who is representing Russia at the meeting?
Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov made an unexpected appearance as talks opened late on Monday. He held a bilateral meeting with US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.
"We like getting along with everybody," Trump told reporters when asked about the first in-person Russian invite since the 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
The US currently holds the rotating G20 presidency and so is hosting the session.

The US government told several news agencies on condition of anonymity that Bessent used the meeting to tell Siluanov that the US would not give Russia economic relief until it brings its four-and-a-half-year invasion to a close.

blocks.caption: Anton Siluanov appeared at the summit but not in the 'family photo' amid European resistanceImage: Bernd von Jutrczenka/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: How did European delegates respond?
"Receiving the Russian finance minsiter here sends a troubling signal," German Finance Minsiter Lars Klingbeil said.
He said he and his European colleagues made clear that they would not appear in the traditional "family photo" alongside the Russian media, saying this was a common EU position.
The photo was ultimately taken without Siluanov and away from the media.
Polish Finance Minister Andrzej Domanski told the Reuters news agency that he recognized the right of the G20 hosts to invite guests, but that he was unhappy to see Moscow represented.

"We do not trust Russia. They lie constantly and you need to be really, really cautious while discussing with them," he said. "So for me it would be very difficult to have any kind of conversation with Russia."

blocks.caption: Klingbeil was critical both of inviting Russia and of excluding reportersImage: Amrei Schulz/BMF/photothek.de/picture alliance

blocks.text: Which reporters and outlets were excluded?
As leaders gathered in Asheville, three giants of the US media landscape complained of either no or limited access toe the meeting.

The business-focused Bloomberg News said that its team was not allowed access, while the Wall Street Journal and the New York Times both complained that certain journalists who would typically cover such events were refused media credentials.
Following a challenge from the DJV German journalists' union on Monday, Klingbeil was critical on the matter.

"I believe the press has a completely legitimate interest in reporting openly and freely on this G20 summit," he said. "I consider it unacceptable for journalists or entire editorial teams to be excluded."

blocks.caption: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has the unenviable task of trying to sell Donald Trump's trade and economic policies to allies Image: Bernd von Jutrczenka/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Intractable Iran war weighing down global economy

Klingbeil had also said in a German political podcast last week that he would bring a simple message to the US regarding what he called Donald Trump's "irresponsible" war in Iran — that it needed to come to an end.

Host Bessent, however, was trying to drum up support among allies for the US plans for what it calls "Operation Economic Outcast," an intensified sanction regime against Iran reliant in no small part on third parties outside the US who still do business with Tehran.

Iran has withstood decades of extensive Iranian and western sanctions, but Bessent tried to argue when asked by reporters that it could swiftly be made to collapse if its remaining trading partners joined in.
"I think it could be within weeks or months — and the economy doesn't have to collapse, we just have to have the regime come to their senses," he said.
Why Canada rejected Trump's terms despite economic risks
Trump's latest Canada meltdown unsettles allies
The other major source of strain at the meeting was last week's sudden deterioration in trade talks between the US and Canada.

This quickly descended into the tit-for-tat imposition of tariffs, and President Trump launching various social media jabs before unilaterally redesignating Lake Ontario as Lake America, at least on the books in the US.
Canada's Finance Minister Francois-Philippe Champagne sought to stress that even the recent friction did not impact his participation.
"Canada has always been at the table and constructive, ready to discuss," he told reporters, stressing the need to ensure continued economic growth and "bring back some stability in trade."

articles.title: Palace says public service seen not in clothes after officials draw flak for branded garb
articles.summary: Government officials should be gauged by their performance and service, not by the clothes they wear, Malacañang said on Tuesday.

blocks.text: Published September 1, 2026 6:19pm
Government officials should be gauged by their performance and service, not by the clothes they wear, Malacañang said on Tuesday.

Palace Press Officer Usec. Claire Castro said this when asked about local executives who were seen wearing expensive designer clothes while conducting relief efforts amid the flood and rain caused by the Southwest Monsoon or Habagat.

Castro didn't name names, but the issue came to the fore after Pampanga Governor Lilia Pineda and her son Vice Governor Dennis Pineda were seen wearing branded rainwear while leading disaster response operations in the province, and drew criticism online.
The governor has since been quoted in media reports as having said sorry if they made a mistake with the clothes they wore amid the rain and flood.
“Ang pagseserbisyo po ay hindi po nakikita sa damit, nakikita po ito sa gawa. Nakikita po ito kung visible ba iyong mga leaders at nandidiyan sila para tumulong,” Castro told reporters.
(Public service is not observed in the clothes one wears, but by their actions. It is seen in whether leaders are visible and present to help.)

“Hindi po nakikita ang pagtulong, ang serbisyong totoo sa damit ng isang lider. Mayroon pong mga iba, napakasimple ng dating, t-shirt, pants, iyong iba nagpapaulan pa, pero wala namang natutulong. So mas maganda po na tingnan ang lider sa trabaho, sa gawa, hindi po sa damit,” she added.

(Help and genuine public service are not measured by the clothes a leader wears. There are some who may look very simple, wearing just a T-shirt and pants, and even braving the rain, but they are not helping. So, it is better to judge a leader by their work and actions, not by their clothes.)
Castro reminded government officials to be “sensitive,” especially during disasters, despite their usual lifestyle.
“Siguro kailangan din maging sensitive kasi lalong-lalo na, kung iyong mga kababayan natin ay nakakaramdam ng hirap, trauma at kalungkutan,” she said.
(Perhaps we also need to be sensitive, especially when our fellow Filipinos are experiencing hardship, trauma, and sadness.)
On Monday, around 17,300 residents in Pampanga moved to 270 evacuation centers as severe, prolonged flooding continues to affect the province.
A man also died after falling into an open manhole that was submerged in floodwaters in Barangay Cutcut, Angeles City, Pampanga.
The victim’s body was found an hour later, far from the drainage where he fell.
The governor described the flooding as unprecedented for some areas in Pampanga, noting that even places that normally do not experience flooding have now been affected.
Due to the flooding and rising water levels in the Pampanga River, several portions of the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) have been experiencing heavy traffic since Sunday. —NB, GMA News

articles.title: Affidavit of desistance cannot be used as basis to dismiss trafficking case -- SC
articles.summary: The Supreme Court (SC) has said that an affidavit of desistance, or a sworn statement withdrawing a complaint, from a victim is “highly suspect” and cannot be used as a basis to dismiss a trafficking…

blocks.text: Published September 1, 2026 6:18pm

The Supreme Court (SC) has said that an affidavit of desistance, or a sworn statement withdrawing a complaint, from a victim is “highly suspect” and cannot be used as a basis to dismiss a trafficking case.
SC Third Division, in a 16-page decision, affirmed the conviction of a woman for trafficking a minor.

The SC cited Section 8 of the Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003, which states that cases involving trafficking should not be dismissed based on the affidavit of desistance executed by the victims, their parents, or legal guardians.
“We take this opportunity to emphasize that affidavits of desistance are highly suspect when the person executing the same is a victim of exploitation,” it said.
“This is especially true when the victim is a child or a person who cannot be expected to know the full consequences of the retraction of a testimony,” it added.
According to the court, it cannot disregard the possibility that the decision was a result of coercion, influence, or other forces that may make the retraction involuntary or untrue.
The SC said the woman recruited the minor to provide sexual services to a man in exchange for money.
It said the minor received P15,000 from the man, but the woman later took the money. The woman bought her a cellphone and gave her P3,000.
Following this, the child’s mother discovered the incident and filed a complaint.
According to the SC, the victim later revealed that she signed the affidavit of desistance in exchange for P30,000 from the woman’s counsel.
Meanwhile, the High Court reiterated that the State is the party affected by the dismissal of the criminal action and not the private complainant.
Due to this, the court said it is up to the State to determine if the case should proceed while the complainant’s role is limited to that of a witness.
“Furthermore, by itself, an affidavit of desistance or pardon is not a ground for the dismissal of an action once the case has been instituted in court,” it said.
“This springs from the rule that in a criminal action already filed in court, the private complainant loses the right or absolute privilege to decide whether the charge should proceed,” it added.
Aside from this, the SC said that all elements of qualified trafficking in persons are present. The court declared the woman guilty and sentenced her to suffer the penalty of life imprisonment.
The decision, penned by Associate Justice Samuel Gaerlan, was promulgated in February and made public in September. — BAP, GMA News

articles.title: More than 1,000 dead from catastrophic Nepal-China floods as rescuers search for survivors
articles.summary: The death toll from catastrophic flooding in Nepal and China passed 1,000 on Tuesday, authorities said, as rescue teams worked to reach communities cut off by the disaster.

image.caption: A health-care worker holds his colleague's head during a break after handing the bodies of victims who perished in the flash floods and a mudslide, in Trishuli, Nuwakot district, Nepal, on Tuesday. (Francis Mascarenhas/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New
The death toll from catastrophic flooding in Nepal and China passed 1,000 on Tuesday, authorities said, as rescue teams worked to reach communities cut off by the disaster.
Thousands still missing, including hundreds believed trapped in tunnels
Nepal evacuees return to inspect flash flooding damage

Nepal's disaster agency said Tuesday that 987 deaths had been counted there, with 3,916 people missing, including 583 foreigners. Chinese authorities, in their latest update on Sunday, reported 16 deaths and 546 people still missing.

At least 11,814 people have been rescued so far, according to Nepalese authorities. Emergency crews have been using helicopters and other aircraft to reach stranded communities in areas where roads and bridges have been destroyed by the flooding and landslides.
The disaster began Wednesday with a chain of events high in the Himalayas. A glacial collapse sent large amounts of rock, ice and meltwater into valleys below, triggering powerful floods downstream.

Scientists studying satellite imagery said the collapse appears to have involved the failure of bedrock beneath a glacier in the Himalayan region. The rockfall was powerful enough to register as a magnitude 5.2 seismic event.

The resulting surge of water and debris entered rivers that flow through valleys in Tibet and Nepal, causing them to rise rapidly. Floodwaters swept away homes, buildings, roads and bridges and carried mud and rocks downstream.

Authorities are still searching for thousands of people who remain unaccounted for on Tuesday. Rescue teams are also working to provide assistance to survivors in areas where roads and other transportation routes have been damaged or cut off.

items: Rescuers search for thousands following deadly Nepal-China flood
Hundreds feared stuck in hydropower tunnels in Nepal

blocks.text: For rescuers, the immediate priority remains finding at least 900 workers who are missing from 12 hydropower projects damaged by the flash floods, about 500 of whom are believed to be trapped inside tunnels.
Visuals released by Nepal's army showed rescue teams entering dark, debris-filled tunnels, wading through mud and water and climbing over rocks as they searched for signs of life.

Bimal Sharma, a helicopter pilot who has been flying rescue missions since the disaster began, said he was shocked to see the devastation in Timure, a border town close to Tibet that he has known for years.
"It felt like I was flying over an entirely different landscape," he said.
Sharma said he has had little opportunity to speak with the people he rescued, but their expressions told him how deeply the disaster had affected them.
"I can see the pain in their eyes. It's heartbreaking," he said.

articles.title: Cop killed while trying to arrest robbery suspect in Batangas
articles.summary: BALAYAN, Batangas - A police officer was killed by a robbery suspect in a follow-up operation in Barangay Sampaga here on Saturday afternoon, Aug. 30. The report identified the fatality as Police…

blocks.text: BALAYAN, Batangas - A police officer was killed by a robbery suspect in a follow-up operation in Barangay Sampaga here on Saturday afternoon, Aug. 30.
The report identified the fatality as Police Staff Sergeant Von Rico Macuha, a member of Sta. Teresita, Batangas Municipal Police Station (MPS).
He was shot in the head by the suspect who was allegedly involved in robbery incident and was identified as Carlo Arcilla Sape, a resident of Sta. Rita town.

According to the report police team went to the temporary residence of the suspect in the said village but he sensed the presence of the police and fled, prompting the police team to pursue him at about 4 p.m.
During the pursuit, the suspect proceeded to an elevated area and allegedly fired at the pursuing police operatives, hitting Macuha in the head.
Macuha was immediately taken to a medical facility in Calaca City and was transferred to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) in s hospital in Balayan town where he died.

The Provincial Police Intelligence Unit, Batangas Police Provincial Office (PIU-BPPO), and Provincial Mobile Force Company (PMFC) were immediately deployed to augment Sta. Teresita MPS in the ongoing hot-pursuit operation against the fleeing suspect.

articles.title: First Thing: Duane Keith Davis found guilty of 1996 murder of Tupac Shakur
articles.summary:
Jury took about three hours to reach verdict in case that relied heavily on confessions from the defendant. Plus, the woman who lived with and loved Freddie Mercury as her fiance

Good…

blocks.text: Good morning. A Las Vegas jury has found the former South Side Compton Crips gang leader Duane Keith Davis guilty of the murder of Tupac Shakur, bringing the case to a close nearly 30 years after the rapper was gunned down. The jury took about three hours to reach a guilty verdict in a case that relied heavily on multiple confessions from Davis himself.

The 63-year-old, who was accused of instigating the deadly shooting but not pulling the trigger himself, had spent years telling investigators and interviewers alike of his direct involvement before he was arrested in 2023.

items: Who was Tupac Shakur? Shakur was born in 1971 in East Harlem, New York, and rose to fame in the early 90s with lyrics that doubled as a sharp commentary on social injustice, including systemic racism and police brutality. He was 25 when he died and is regarded among the greatest rappers to ever live, and continues to be celebrated around the world years after his life was cut short.

How have his family reacted to the trial? “We’ve been waiting 30 years to grieve properly,” Zayd Akinyela, Shakur’s cousin, told reporters outside the courtroom when the trial was under way. “A lot of people don’t get to grieve until they understand what happened to their loved one and how it happened.”

Why have authorities been so heavily criticised over the case? Las Vegas police faced criticism that they had bungled the investigation and failed to pursue crucial leads, including from a member of Shakur’s entourage who claimed he could identify the shooters. That witness died weeks later in a separate shooting.

With more than 40 bridges destroyed, rescuers are relying on helicopters, while India and China are sending prefabricated truss bridges to help restore access. items: What role had Driscoll been playing? An Iraq war veteran, tech investor and former adviser to JD Vance, Driscoll was tapped for the unusual role of key negotiator to try to end the war between Russia and Ukraine. He was also a major force behind trying to cut the red tape for military contractors to quickly develop more drones and counter-drone capabilities as warfare rapidly changes around the world.
