articles.title: Cotabato leaders call for unity in public service
articles.summary: DAVAO CITY – North Cotabato provincial leaders urged residents to uphold unity, faith, and dedication to public service during the 112th Founding Anniversary and the culmination of the Kalivungan…

blocks.text: DAVAO CITY – North Cotabato provincial leaders urged residents to uphold unity, faith, and dedication to public service during the 112th Founding Anniversary and the culmination of the Kalivungan Festival 2026 at the Provincial Capitol on Tuesday, Sept 1.

Cotabato Governor Emmylou Taliño-Mendoza, Vice Governor Rochella Marie Taliño-Taray, and Rep. Maria Alana Samantha Taliño-Santos highlighted the province's commitment to peace, progress, and unity during the program at The Basket.

blocks.caption: The Provincial Government of Cotabato, led by Governor Emmylou Taliño-Mendoza, vows to strengthen partnerships with government agencies and other stakeholders to advance peace, progress, and unity in the province as it culminates the 112th Founding Anniversary and Kalivungan Festival 2026 on Tues…

blocks.text: The Provincial Government of Cotabato, led by Governor Emmylou Taliño-Mendoza, vows to strengthen partnerships with government agencies and other stakeholders to advance peace, progress, and unity in the province as it culminates the 112th Founding Anniversary and Kalivungan Festival 2026 on Tuesday, September 1, at the Provincial Capitol Grounds in Amas, Kidapawan City. (Photo via Ivy Tejano / MB)

In a speech, Mendoza urged government workers and officials to perform their duties to the best of their ability, regardless of their positions, saying every contribution matters in advancing the province. "No matter how small or big your role is."

Mendoza emphasized that public service is a public trust. She said 112 years is such a long number and that they are blessed to have the presence and prayers of their priests and elders as they celebrate this milestone.

"Amid these crises, our faith in God can help us remain strong," she said, thanking local officials, national agencies, partnered organizations, and other stakeholders for their endless support to the province's development.

The governor welcomed the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) Undersecretary, Fatima Aliah Dimaporo, who represented DSWD Secretary Rex Gatchalian as the guest of honor and speaker during the celebration.

Gatchalian, in a speech read by Dimaporo, congratulated the provincial government and its people on the province's 112th founding anniversary, highlighting everyone's role in building a legacy of peace, progress, and unity.

"Cotabato's 112-year history is shaped by the contributions of its farmers, workers, entrepreneurs, and communities, whose cooperation has helped build a stronger, more peaceful, and prosperous province," Gatchalian said.

Taray described the event as a celebration of Cotabato's diverse cultures, traditions, talents, and local products. She said their diverse languages, municipalities, and cultures should not divide their people, but bring them together as one community.

Santos said the anniversary should be measured not only by the scale of the festivities but also by the province's ability to bring its people together, remember its roots, and honor those who helped build its peace and progress.

Officials credited the collaborative efforts of the provincial government, district offices, local chief executives, national government partners, and other stakeholders in pursuing development and ensuring that families are not left behind.

The province's 112th Founding Anniversary and Kalivungan Festival 2026, dubbed "A Legacy of Peace, Progress, and Unity," underscores the province's ongoing efforts to build on its gains and strengthen solidarity among its communities.

Makilala emerges as champion of the Drum and Lyre Corps Competition and takes home the P300,000 cash prize during the culmination of the festival at the Provincial Capitol Grounds in Amas, Kidapawan City, on Tuesday morning.

They also won the special awards for Best in Street Parade, Best in Choreography, and Best in Musicality. Meanwhile, Mlang placed first runner-up and received P200,000, while Tulunan National High School finished second runner-up with P150,000.

articles.title: House to vote on stopgap funding bill as lawmakers scramble to avoid government shutdown – US politics live
articles.summary:
Speaker Mike Johnson to launch a floor vote designed to prevent any federal shutdown before the November midterms

Generational ⁠change is on the ballot ⁠in Massachusetts on ​Tuesday…

blocks.text: House to vote on stopgap funding bill as lawmakers scramble to avoid government shutdown
Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.

House speaker Mike Johnson will launch a floor vote to pass the stopgap funding bill designed to keep the federal government fully funded through early December, removing the possibility of a shutdown before the midterm elections.
“The first thing is we’ve got to make sure this government gets funded and we don’t have another Democratic shutdown,” he told reporters as he prepared to open the chamber for business.
The short-term funding bill underwent some significant changes in the Senate, which made it more palatable for Democrats.

It delays a proposed rule from the Office of Management and Budget that would give political appointees more power over the distribution of federal grants. It also includes language to ensure the administration cannot transfer funds to the Border Patrol.
But a provision that delays for one month a federal ban on intoxicating hemp THC products has prompted criticism from many GOP lawmakers.
As a result, GOP leaders will probably place the bill on a fast-track process that avoids a separate procedural vote, bypassing any Republican efforts to block or stall the legislation.

Suspension bills require a two-thirds vote to pass, meaning a significant number from both parties need to support the measure for it to pass and advance to Trump’s desk. The funding vote will most likely take place later today.
In other developments:

items: The Supreme Court allowed Donald Trump to continue building his $400m White House ballroom project. In a 5-4 decision along political lines, the justices found that a group issuing a legal challenge against the ballroom did not have standing to bring their case. Trump celebrated with a post on his Truth Social platform while Democrats criticized the decision.

Army Secretary Dan Driscoll is stepping down from his role after 18 months on the job, leaving another top military position vacant. Driscoll and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had reportedly butted heads for some time.
Trump vowed further strikes on Iran and called it a “failed nation”. The remarks came as Washington and Tehran exchanged their first military strikes in a month.

blocks.text: Massachusetts primaries test Democratic appetite for generational change

Generational ⁠change is on the ballot ⁠in Massachusetts on ​Tuesday as Democratic voters choose whether to renominate 80-year-old progressive senator Ed Markey or replace him on the ballot with 47-year-old representative Seth ⁠Moulton.

Markey, who has served in Congress for nearly 50 years, is backed by leading progressives such as senator Bernie Sanders and representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, as well ⁠as most members of the state’s congressional delegation, including senator Elizabeth Warren.

No members of the delegation have ​endorsed Moulton, a moderate US Marine Corps veteran ‌whose supporters include New Jersey ‌Governor Mikie Sherrill and the Democratic organization VoteVets, Reuters reported.
The Boston Globe’s editorial board is also behind Moulton, casting ‌him as a necessary agent of change with “proven leadership skills” and positions on key issues that align with most voters.
Markey has a nearly $2m fundraising advantage over Moulton, and Markey has led in recent polls by a double-digit margin. The primary winner is heavily favored to win in November.
Democrat Kamala Harris carried the state by nearly 25 percentage points in 2024.
A similar generational challenge is playing out in the Boston area, where moderate representative Stephen Lynch, 71, is facing progressive attorney Patrick Roath, 39.

articles.title: Six killed, several injured in Dumalinao road crash
articles.summary: ZAMBOANGA CITY- Six persons were killed while several others were injured when a passenger van crashed into a parked wing van truck in Dumalinao, Zamboanga del Sur on Tuesday, September 1. Witnesses…

blocks.text: (Photo via Liza Jocson)
ZAMBOANGA CITY- Six persons were killed while several others were injured when a passenger van crashed into a parked wing van truck in Dumalinao, Zamboanga del Sur on Tuesday, September 1.
Witnesses said the van was travelling from Ipil, Zamboanga Sibugay when it collided with the other van that was parked along the road.
The impact was so severe that five persons were immediately killed. One expired while undergoing treatment at a medical facility.
Several persons were also treated at the hospital for injuries.
Investigation showed that a passenger van was travelling from Ipil, Zamboanga Sibugay toward Pagadian City when the driver lost control of the vehicle.
The passenger van crashed into a wing van parked along the highway before colliding with other vehicles along the road.
Police are investigating other circumstances behind the road mishap.

articles.title: Boomers, Tall Blacks sharpen Gilas for Asian Qualifiers second round
articles.summary: Iron sharpens iron. And for Gilas Pilipinas, its experience in the first round of the 2027 FIBA World Cup Asian Qualifiers against New Zealand and Australia certainly came in handy for the Nationals…

blocks.text: Iron sharpens iron.

And for Gilas Pilipinas, its experience in the first round of the 2027 FIBA World Cup Asian Qualifiers against New Zealand and Australia certainly came in handy for the Nationals in their 2-0 sweep of the fourth window.

The Filipinos may have come out with a 2-4 record at the end of the first round of the qualifiers but Gilas believes playing to such a high level of competition allowed them to be ready for what was in store for them against Jordan and Iran in the second round.
“It was a lot of learning experience out there. I mean, those are the top two teams in the pool,” said Gilas star Dwight Ramos.
“We had tough opponents Australia and New Zealand but they made us better. We were able to come back from slow starts and we’re just very happy for the guys,” he added.

Before the August window, Gilas came in on a four-game losing skid in the qualifiers — all of those came at the hands of the two Oceania teams. The only victories Gilas had in the first round was against Guam.
The Boomers gave Gilas a beating in their two meetings, winning 93-66 on the road and then 96-42 at their home turf.
Against the Tall Blacks, it was more competitive with the Kiwis escaping 96-93 in the first meeting and then avoiding a homecourt upset with a 106-104 double-overtime win against Gilas.

As tough as the matches were, Ramos said the losses built Gilas character which finally paid off when they recovered from double-digit deficits in the 82-81 win over Jordan and the grindout 68-56 victory over Iran.

“We all believe in each other so whoever's out there on the court, looks like they're playing with confidence. Make or miss, it doesn't matter 'cause you know as teammates we're here behind them and we're always making up and picking each other up,” explained Ramos.
“It feels good 'cause it's been a while since we did that. It feels good. You know, (we) start winning games again. We gotta tough windows and feels like we're getting our groove,” he added.

articles.title: Germany news: Explosive device found near power plant
articles.summary: Police say they found an "unconventional explosive and incendiary device" near the Jänschwalde power plant in Brandenburg. Meanwhile, Germany's top diplomat says Algeria could become an important…

image.caption: Authorities said there was no danger to the publicImage: Patrick Pleul/dpa-Zentralbild/picture alliance

blocks.text: September 1, 2026
Explosive device discovered at substation in eastern Germany

blocks.caption: The Jänschwalde coal-fired power plant was built between 1976 and 1989Image: Andreas Franke/IMAGO

blocks.text: Police have found an explosive device near the Jänschwalde power station in the eastern German state of Brandenburg, according to media reports on Tuesday.
The device was discovered at an electrical substation in Turnow-Preilack, southeast of Berlin, after potential damage to a power line was detected, Germany news agency dpa reported.
"Evidence is being secured," the agency quoted a police spokeswoman as saying. "Bomb disposal experts are on site."
Police added that there was no immediate danger to the public and that no one was hurt.
Further details were not immediately available.
The apparent attempted attack comes after several incidents targeting power supply in the greater Berlin area.
In January, suspected far-left extremists set fire to high-voltage power lines near a power station in southwest Berlin, causing power cuts to 45,000 homes.
In March 2024, a group set fire to a large electricity pylon needed to supply the Tesla factory in Grünheide near Berlin. That caused a halt in production for several days.

articles.title: Nepal-Tibet flood deaths pass 1,000 as police ask relatives for DNA to identify victims
articles.summary: Relatives of missing tourists asked for blood samples and photos, as efforts continue to rescue trapped hydropower workers
articles.byline: Cait Kelly in Kathmandu and agencies

blocks.text: Nepali rescuers have built temporary bridges to reach remote areas and dug through the ruins of hydropower projects in the Himalayas to rescue hundreds of trapped workers, as the death toll passed 1,000 nearly ⁠a week after devastating ​floods left a trail of destruction across the country’s towns and valleys.

About 600 people remain stuck in several devastated hydropower stations that have become the focus of rescue efforts. The prime ⁠minister, Balendra Shah, said more than 11,000 people had been rescued across the affected region, and power and communication lines had been restored in some areas.
“Thousands of citizens have lost their homes, families, loved ones and property,” Shah said.

Six days after the catastrophe struck the Himalayan border region, 4,400 people were still missing in Nepal and Tibet. Police in Kathmandu have urged relatives of missing tourists to provide DNA samples to assist identification efforts.

In a statement posted to social media, Nepal police on Monday asked relatives of those missing to “provide a fresh blood sample for DNA profiling and two passport-sized photographs” to the pathology laboratory at the Nepal police hospital in Kathmandu, or the nearest district police office.

Among Nepal’s list of the missing are 592 foreigners, including tourists who had come for mountain trekking and Hindu pilgrims seeking spiritual peace at Tibet’s sacred Mount Kailash, from countries such as India, the US, UK, Australia and Canada.
Relatives abroad have been requested to undergo DNA profiling at an authorised laboratory and to “send a soft copy of the DNA profile to Nepal police’s official email address”.
In some of Nepal’s flood-affected areas, hundreds of unidentified bodies have already been buried because they are decomposing and there is no room left in hospitals or morgues.

blocks.caption: People search posters of those missing in Nepal flood

blocks.text: At the police hospital in Kathmandu on Tuesday, more than 100 people were waiting to have their blood sampled.

Among them was Prakaiti Jurnj. Her mother was still missing, but the family had been able to identify her father’s body from a photograph on the wall outside the teaching hospital, where images of the deceased have been posted in an effort to identify the victims.

“Both my father and mother, they were in the village in Nukawot. They were both swept away by the flood,” she said. “We haven’t heard from them since Wednesday. We found my father’s body; my brother saw the photo on the wall.”

She was waiting for her two other siblings, who live in the UK, to arrive on Tuesday so they could all try to get up to the village. She said she wanted to contact her grandmother or sister-in-law, who she thinks both survived the flood because their house is further up the mountain. Their village was still in a blackout, and making contact was impossible.
“I can’t go there; the situation is very bad,” she said. “I can’t go up there alone. I am not sure if we’ll be able to get them.”

The disaster was triggered by a glacier collapse that sent a deluge of ice, rock and mud through Nepal’s border region with China, posing a massive challenge for the country’s six-month-old government.

The region is vulnerable to flooding and landslides, and extreme weather events such as intense monsoons and melting glaciers have become more common because of warming due to human-caused climate change.

In a late-night social media post, Shah said aid worth more than $42m had poured into the country, but that Nepalis were reeling. “The government understands the ​immense pain they are enduring. The path ahead is to ‌support them through this suffering and help ‌them return to normal life through rehabilitation,” the prime minister said.

Shah also said that 279 workers had so far been rescued from hydropower projects, where authorities estimated close to 1,000 people had been trapped. Days after the disaster, hope was rapidly diminisging that any of those trapped in a series of tunnels could be alive.

Pictures and videos shared by rescue teams showed earth-moving equipment digging and shovelling mud and rocks under lights in the dark of the night. Soldiers used torchlight in a big pit they had created to look for space to get into one tunnel.

Chinese state media coverage has focused largely on the official response, highlighting the deployment of firefighters, the People’s Liberation Army and instructions from top leaders. Little is known about victims on the Chinese side.
The flood was “caused by glacier instability under the long-term effects of global warming”, China’s state broadcaster said on Monday.

Shah said the ​catastrophic event signalled the growing risks that the Himalayan region faces. “The region must therefore remain vigilant. The time has come for us to strongly raise before the international community the disasters we are experiencing as a consequence of climate change,” he wrote in his post.

articles.title: ‘It is Lake Ontario and it won’t change,’ business owners in Niagara region respond to Trump renaming lake

image.caption: Richard Carpenter, right, and Jonathon Olszewsky own Carson's Pizzeria in Niagara Falls, Ont., where they've playfully renamed their American menu items to Canadian towns and cities. (Diona Macalinga/CBC)

blocks.text: Hamilton

From Chicago deep dish to 'Thorold-style Deep Dish Pizza,' businesses in the Niagara region react to the U.S. president's move to rename Lake Ontario to Lake America amid escalating tensions and a brewing trade war.
Some businesses say American customers have apologized for U.S. President Donald Trump’s new executive order
Now that Google Maps has changed the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America for users based in the U.S., the owners of one Niagara Falls restaurant decided to take a similar approach to their menu.
The move comes after U.S. President Donald Trump signed an executive order to change the name of the lake, amid escalating tensions and a brewing trade war.
“If you can rename whatever you want for your country, well then, we can do the same thing over here,” said Richard Carpenter, co-owner of Carson’s Pizzeria.
What was once their Buffalo chicken sandwich is now listed as their "Ontario wing sauce chicken sandwich."
“Also, the same thing with the Chicago Deep Dish, he named it the Thorold-style Deep Dish Pizza,” said co-owner Jonathon Olszewsky.

The pizzeria's Facebook post, announcing their “little name change,” has gathered concurring reactions from Canadians across the country, though Carpenter said the menu change is temporary and more “humour-based.”
Carson's Pizzeria is just one business in the region using small gestures like this to respond to the name change.
Katherine McMichael, owner of the shop Lady Lou Collective in Niagara-on-the-Lake, Ont., said “it is Lake Ontario and it won’t change.”

items: Google updates maps to show Lake America in the U.S. — but Canadians are now seeing it, too

blocks.text: “It’s quite silly that somebody thinks they can change the name of the lake, especially when it was made way beyond any of us were ever here,” McMichael told CBC Niagara.
McMichael owns and curates Canadian-made art work and gift items for her store Lady Lou Collective.
She keeps a sign in her shop's door thanking her customers for supporting Canadian businesses and Canadian-made goods.

She said while the impact of the Canada-U.S. trade war on her own business pales in comparison to those in many other industries, particularly the automotive sector, she's still affected, as she no longer ships orders to the U.S.

items: What went wrong with U.S. trade talks, according to Canada's chief negotiator

blocks.text: “It’s sad that we can’t do that anymore,” said McMichael, fearing that her American customers would get hit with duties. “I used to say that we’re two countries that support each other … We’re all just trying to make ends meet.”
Across the street, Shauna Dickson, owner of mom-and-pop shop Irish Design said she often uses Lake Ontario as a landmark to help customers and businesses overseas find her boutique.
Dickson, who was born and raised in Niagara-on-the-Lake, said the move to change the name of Lake Ontario “felt really close to home.”

Over the years, she said she felt a shift in her interactions with customers visiting from across the border, she told CBC News. But, despite the growing tensions between the two countries she wants to make sure her American customers still feel welcome in her store.
“We had a lot of customers come in and apologize when the conversation gets brought up about where they’re from,” Dickson said.
“It feels like we’re trying to comfort people a lot to make sure they know they're welcome here,” Dickson added. “We’re not blanketing you with one bully.”
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Diona Macalinga is a St. Catharines-based CBC reporter covering communities in the Niagara region. Before that, she was a video journalist reporting on Quebec legislature, culture and community news in Montreal. You can email story ideas and tips to her at diona.macalinga@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Escudero: Burden of proof lies with the prosecution
articles.summary: Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero on Tuesday emphasized during the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte that the burden of proof never shifts from the…

blocks.text: Published September 1, 2026 6:01pm

Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero on Tuesday emphasized during the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte that the burden of proof never shifts from the prosecution.

Escudero said this after Senator-Judge Alan Peter Cayetano made an interjection, asking prosecution counsel Rey Robles whether there was any irregularity or fraud if the special disbursing officer transferred confidential funds to another person.

“For a senator-judge like me, it is important to know whether it was an irregularity wherein we should caution or reprimand, or whether it is automatically fraud. And also for non-lawyers, it would be good to know, at some point, whether there's a presumption that shifts,” Cayetano said.

“For example, the prosecution made it very clear at one point earlier on na kapagka hindi ma-account, nag si-shift na ‘yung burden. So that's very clear, di ba? So, halimbawa hindi na ma-account nag-shift ngayon sa prosecution. It's not a conclusive presumption, meaning they can show na hindi na-account,” he added.

(For example, the prosecution made it very clear at one point earlier that when it is not accounted for, the burden would shift. So that's very clear, right? So, for example, when it is not accounted for, the burden shifted now from the prosecution. It's not a conclusive presumption, meaning they can show that it is not accounted for.)
Escudero, however, clarified that the burden of proof never shifts from the prosecution.

“For the record, to clarify, the burden of proof never shifts. The burden of evidence may shift, but the burden of proof does not. The burden of proof still lies with the prosecution, but depending on how the issue is presented, the burden of evidence may shift, but the burden of proof never shifts,” the presiding officer said.

Robles maintained that under the joint circular governing confidential funds, the special disbursing officer is responsible for disbursing the funds and should not transfer it to another person who is not an accountable officer. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: Tropical storm maintains strength off N. Luzon, LPA dissipates – Pagasa
articles.summary: (Satellite image from Pagasa) MANILA, Philippines — The low-pressure area (LPA) off Itbayat, Batanes has dissipated, while Tropical storm Pilandok (international name: Krovanh) maintained its…

blocks.text: (Satellite image from Pagasa)

MANILA, Philippines — The low-pressure area (LPA) off Itbayat, Batanes has dissipated, while Tropical storm Pilandok (international name: Krovanh) maintained its strength inside the Philippine area of responsibility (PAR) on Tuesday afternoon, the state weather bureau said.

In a weather advisory issued at 4 p.m., the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) reported that Pilandok was estimated 1,015 kilometers (km) east of extreme Northern Luzon.
Pilandok has a maximum sustained wind speed of 65 kilometers per hour (kph) near the center and gustiness of up to 80 kph while moving west-northwest at 10 kph.
According to Pagasa, Pilandok may exit the country on Thursday, Sep. 3, while maintaining its strength.
The weather bureau previously reported that the weather disturbance will remain far from the Philippine landmass and is less likely to make landfall.
Pagasa also reported that it continues to monitor Tropical storm Saudel, formerly Obet west of Calayan, Cagayan, and another LPA off southeastern Luzon and outside the PAR.
The second LPA remained to have a medium chance of developing into a tropical depression within the next 24 hours, Pagasa said. /gsg

articles.title: Marcos pushes stricter enforcement of ‘no-build zones’ amid floods
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is calling for stricter enforcement of “no-build zone” policies and other measures aimed at reducing flooding and protecting communities from the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is calling for stricter enforcement of “no-build zone” policies and other measures aimed at reducing flooding and protecting communities from the effects of climate change, Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said Tuesday.
He issued the directive during a Central Luzon and Metro Manila Response Meeting with key Cabinet officials and local chief executives on Monday in Malacañang.

“According to the president, the law must be enforced, including the “no-build zone” policy. Let us stop politicizing the issue. Enforce the law. It must be explained to everyone that stricter enforcement of the law is necessary for our safety,” Castro said during a briefing.

“For LGUs, enforce the “no-build zones.” Ensure that your respective jurisdictions are properly maintained, work together to clear obstructions from waterways, and make sure that garbage is collected and disposed of at proper disposal sites,” she added.
In the same briefing, Castro said Marcos wants greater focus on climate change mitigation and adaptation.
“There is no need for us to blame one another. Whatever shortcomings may have occurred under the previous administration will not be tolerated by the president,” she said.
“The president is particularly focused on the effects of climate change, as we are increasingly witnessing and experiencing the full force of nature’s fury,” she added.

She said the government will also strengthen coordination with the Climate Change Commission, which is chaired by Marcos, to identify gaps in the implementation of climate policies and ensure that its recommendations reach the president. /mcm

articles.title: Ex-DPWH chief Manuel Bonoan says Marcos asked him to resign
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Former Public Works and Highways Secretary Manuel Bonoan explained that it was President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. who asked him to resign from his post a year ago amid public…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Former Public Works and Highways Secretary Manuel Bonoan explained that it was President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. who asked him to resign from his post a year ago amid public outrage over the flood control corruption scandal.

Bonoan was testifying before the Sandiganbayan Fourth Division on Tuesday in the graft trial of former Sen. Ramon “Bong” Revilla Jr. when Chairperson Associate Justice Michael Frederick Musngi noted the timing of the ex-secretary’s appearance and asked why he had resigned.
“Your Honor, I was asked to submit a courtesy resignation,” Bonoan answered.
Musngi pressed on who had made the request for the then-DPWH chief to leave his post.
“It was relayed to me, Your Honor,” Bonoan replied.
Asked by Musngi whether the request had come in the form of a “message from the president,” Bonoan answered in the affirmative.

In August 2025, a month after Marcos launched the government’s anti-corruption drive in infrastructure projects, Bonoan maintained that he would remain at his post, saying to resign would be to “turn [his] back to the problem.”
Days later, Malacañang confirmed that Bonoan had resigned from his post, with Marcos explaining that it was due to “command responsibility.”
Bonoan was ultimately charged alongside Sen. Jinggoy Estrada over a purported scheme involving P573 million in kickbacks.
‘Nothing wrong with leadership fund’
The former DPWH was called to testify in the Revilla graft case.
Revilla is accused of involvement in a P76.91-million flood control project in Pandi, Bulacan, which state prosecutors claimed to be “non-existent.”
Bonoan previously testified in the malversation case against the former senator before the Sandiganbayan Third Division.

The ex-secretary claimed that his department created a “leadership fund” availed by “all senators” in 2024—including Revilla, who then chaired the chamber’s public works committee—in a bid to address budget cuts to the agency.

“There’s nothing wrong for senators to avail of the leadership fund as long as they are consistent with the core programs of the department. It is actually embedded in the criteria for the selection of projects,” Bonoan maintained.
“In fact, all the projects submitted by the proponent senators are vetted and conform with the programs of the department,” he added.
“What would be wrong is actually in the implementation of the projects. That’s another area of concern,” he further said.

He explained that, in implementing the projects between fiscal years 2023 and 2025, the DPWH had supposedly not been given the adequate budget to conduct feasibility studies and preliminary engineering.

Bonoan likewise confirmed that he had met with Revilla on several occasions but only to “discuss the status of pending bills pertaining to the DPWH,” particularly on the declaration of national roads and additional engineering districts.

Further, upon cross-examination by Revilla’s legal counsel, Bonoan said he had no personal knowledge of Revilla’s requested projects since the list had been supplied to him via Undersecretary Roberto Bernardo.
At the end of the hearing, the prosecution said it will present 20 more witnesses in the Revilla case, with DPWH Assistant Secretary Alex Bote up next on Sept. 8. /mr

articles.title: Speaker Dy: We can build a ‘Bagong Kongreso’
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — House Speaker Faustino “Bojie” G. Dy III rallied members and employees of the lower chamber on Tuesday to continue working together to build a “Bagong Kongreso,” a better…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — House Speaker Faustino “Bojie” G. Dy III rallied members and employees of the lower chamber on Tuesday to continue working together to build a “Bagong Kongreso,” a better Congress that would restore public trust in the institution.
Dy made the statement during a surprise birthday activity organized by House leaders, officials, and employees.
“Mapalad po ako sapagkat ang mga naging kasama ko ay hindi tayo sumuko — lumaban tayo. Lumaban tayo ibangon ang Kongreso. Salamat sa tiwala,” Dy said.
(“I’m lucky for having you with me, and we did not surrender — we fought. We fought to lift Congress. Thank you for your trust.”)
The speaker, who turned 65 on Aug. 31, stressed that much work remained to be done and urged everyone in the House to remain committed to doing what is right and rebuilding confidence in Congress.
“Mahaba pa ang laban natin. Nakakapag-umpisa pa lang tayo. Pero dapat lalo nating ipaglaban ang tama at ipaglaban natin na ibangon ang Kongreso sa tulong ng bawat isa,” said the House chief.
(“We have a long battle ahead. We have just started. But we have to fight more for what is right, and we have to help each other fight to raise Congress.”)
“Palakasin pa natin yung ating paniniwala na kayang-kaya nating ibangon ang Bagong Kongreso,” he said.
(“Let’s strengthen our trust in each other that we can raise the New Congress.”)
Since assuming the speakership, Dy has pushed for a “Bagong Kongreso” anchored on transparency, accountability, institutional reform, and concrete results for the Filipino people.

He has consistently stressed collective responsibility for strengthening Congress, calling for members and employees to put public service and the welfare of the people above political and personal differences. /atm

articles.title: Burnham Lake reopens to boaters on 117th Baguio Charter Day
articles.summary: BAGUIO CITY — A renovated Burnham Lake welcomed visitors and residents who had missed its traditional boat rides on Tuesday, Sept. 1, after nearly a year behind construction barriers for a…

blocks.text: BAGUIO CITY — A renovated Burnham Lake welcomed visitors and residents who had missed its traditional boat rides on Tuesday, Sept. 1, after nearly a year behind construction barriers for a P480-million rehabilitation project.

People scampered down new boardwalks surrounding the century-old man-made lake following a ribbon-cutting ceremony led by Mayor Benjamin Magalong, Tourism Infrastructure and Enterprise Zone Authority (Tieza) head Mark Lapid, and Baguio Rep. Mauricio Domogan.
Built alongside Baguio 117 years ago by the American colonial government, the lake had been closed since October 2025 for a rehabilitation and improvement project.
The nearly four-hectare lake forms part of the 33-hectare Burnham Park, which was part of Baguio’s original design drawn up in 1903 by Chicago architect Daniel Burnham.
The rehabilitation included a new wooden boardwalk, reinforced lake embankments, improvements to the view deck, and new boats for returning concessionaires.
The city government said the lake’s reopening does not mean all areas of Burnham Park have reopened, as some facilities remain subject to safety assessments.
The next phase of rehabilitation will cover the Children’s Park, Skating Rink, and Rose Garden. /mcm

articles.title: EMB haze watch: Koronadal air quality recorded ‘fair’ to ‘good’
articles.summary: KORONADAL CITY, South Cotabato — Air quality in Koronadal City was recorded from “fair” to “good” on Tuesday morning, Sept. 1, as the Environmental Management Bureau (EMB) Region 12 continued to…

blocks.text: KORONADAL CITY, South Cotabato — Air quality in Koronadal City was recorded from “fair” to “good” on Tuesday morning, Sept. 1, as the Environmental Management Bureau (EMB) Region 12 continued to monitor the city under its haze watch following forest fires reported in Kalimantan, indonesia.
Based on EMB’s Sept. 1 hourly PM2.5 monitoring, the city’s Air Quality Index (AQI) was at 62 at 9 a.m. and 52 at 10 a.m., both classified as “fair.”
Readings improved to the “Good” category beginning at 1 a.m., when the AQI dropped to 31.
The AQI remained within the “Good” range through 10 a.m., with hourly readings ranging from 25 to 50.
The latest figures also showed an improvement from the 24-hour average recorded as of Aug. 31, when Koronadal’s PM2.5 AQI stood at 69.8, or within the yellow “fair” category.

Under EMB’s air quality guide, readings from zero to 50 are classified as “Good,” meaning air quality is considered satisfactory with little or no health risk. Readings from 51 to 100 fall under the “Fair” category, during which sensitive individuals may experience respiratory symptoms such as coughing.
EMB advised the public that regular outdoor activities may continue but urged residents to remain updated on air quality conditions.
The monitoring comes amid reports of forest fires in parts of Indonesia, which lies south of the Philippines and relatively close to Mindanao.
EMB- 12, however, has yet to confirm whether the air conditions being monitored in Koronadal are linked to the haze from Indonesia.
Koronadal is the capital of South Cotabato and seat of government of Region 12 or Soccsksargen. /mr

articles.title: Bohol folk urged to take precautions as haze blankets parts of province
articles.summary: TAGBILARAN CITY, Bohol — Haze blanketed parts of Bohol province on Tuesday, obscuring views of Panglao Island and the mountains of Maribojoc town as authorities warned residents to take precautions.…

blocks.text: TAGBILARAN CITY, Bohol — Haze blanketed parts of Bohol province on Tuesday, obscuring views of Panglao Island and the mountains of Maribojoc town as authorities warned residents to take precautions.
Residents in Tagbilaran City and nearby towns woke up to hazy skies, with some reporting that the haze had already been visible since Monday.
Mel Micayabas, 34, of Dauis town, said Panglao Island appeared to be covered in smoke when viewed from a distance.
“The haze was already visible on Monday,” Micayabas recalled.
From Tagbilaran, neighboring Cebu Island, which is usually visible across the Bohol Strait, was also barely visible because of the thick haze.
The mountains of Maribojoc were likewise completely obscured.

The Environmental Management Bureau (EMB) of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) in Central Visayas confirmed the presence of haze in Bohol and other parts of the region, saying it was likely caused by smoke from forest fires in Indonesia.

As of 6 a.m. Tuesday, PM2.5 levels recorded at the Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Station (CAAQMS) in Talisay City, Cebu reached an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 152, classified as “Very Unhealthy.”
Bohol Gov. Erico Aristotle Aumentado urged residents to wear masks when outdoors and avoid unnecessary exposure to the haze.
“If possible, wear a mask when going outside and avoid staying outdoors unnecessarily,” Aumentado said in a social media post. /gsg

Upon receiving Ibas’ credentials, Marcos said he looks forward to the opportunities that would benefit both countries and to exploring matters they could develop together.

“The Philippines and Nigeria have significant potential to expand cooperation, especially in energy security, trade and investment, and pursue initiatives that would mutually benefit our peoples and our countries,” the President said.
“…We look forward to working with you to promote and deepen our collaboration and cooperation, which has spanned 64 years,” he added after welcoming the new Nigerian envoy to the country.
Meanwhile, Ibas said he would work to enhance the friendly and strong bilateral relations between the Philippines and Nigeria. (Martina Nieyandra Calica, INQUIRER.net trainee)

articles.title: House Republicans ramp up labor union investigations ahead of midterms
articles.summary:
Inquiry come after conservative thinktanks claim unions are using member dues to support Democratic causes

House Republicans are investigating several US labor unions based on claims…

blocks.text: House Republicans are investigating several US labor unions based on claims from far-right nonprofits alleging union dues are being used for illegal political funding.

Republicans on the House’s education and workforce committee opened the investigation this summer after multiple reports from the conservative thinktanks targeted unions and their spending, claiming that unions are using member dues to support Democratic causes.

While unions are allowed to advocate for political causes, they are prohibited from using union dues to directly fund specific candidates or political action committees (Pacs). Union members can voluntary donate to labor union’s political action committees.

The unions under investigation include the American Federation of Teachers (AFT), United Auto Workers, United Steelworkers, Smart Transportation Division (Smart-TD), Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen (BLET), and the Brotherhood of Maintenance of Way Employees Division (BMWED).

The allegations come from research reports by the American Accountability Foundation (AAF), a “dark money” nonprofit that counts Project 2025 architect the Heritage Foundation as a donor, and the Freedom Foundation, a conservative thinktank whose chairman once protested against Labor Day, claiming “I can’t think of a problem in society that can’t be traced in some way back to the abuses of organized labor.”

Among the AAF’s allegations toward labor unions include complaining that the BLET supported a lawsuit filed by the UAW to halt the Trump administration’s attempt to end collective bargaining. It also highlighted the BLET’s criticism of Project 2025, which advocates for several policies that would weaken labor unions and collective bargaining rights.

“The industrial unions the [House] committee is investigating have become glorified political arms of the Democrat Party,” said Tom Jones, President of the American Accountability Foundation in a statement. “When these unions care more about their friends in Congress than their members in the factories and railroads, it becomes clear they’re not serving the working men and women of America!”
In a statement, a spokesperson for United Steelworkers said the group is “working diligently on fully addressing the committee’s request”.
“Our union values transparency and annually reports our spending with the Department of Labor,” the spokesperson said.

As a part of their union probes, House Republicans are also investigating AFT president Randi Weingarten after the Freedom Foundation claimed, using speculation around the union’s annual financial filing, that union member dues funded her 2025 book, Why Fascists Fear Teachers: Public Education and the Future of Democracy.
“Perhaps Weingarten’s next book should be entitled, Why Teachers Fear Teachers Unions,” the analysis claimed.

In a letter responding to the allegations, Michael Bromwich, an attorney representing Weingarten and AFT, called the Freedom Foundation’s report “a partisan attack masquerading as investigative journalism”.

“Its claims are premised on factual inaccuracies, misleading characterizations, and a willful disregard for the complete record,” Bromwich wrote. “The documents produced to the House committee refute these allegations and demonstrate that the book project was lawfully and ethically undertaken to advance AFT’s mission, with appropriate oversight and transparent financial arrangements.”
The Freedom Foundation and House Republicans on the investigating committee did not respond to multiple requests for comment.

The House investigations follow reports that the Trump administration conducted surveillance of labor unions in Minnesota during a mass anti-immigration enforcement operation earlier this year, including the CWA and the SEIU.

Cathy Creighton, director of Cornell University’s sSchool of Industrial and Labor Relations Buffalo Co-Lab, said that union finances are strictly controlled, with disclosure requirements on how money is spent – which is how the conservative groups got the information for their reports.
Most union members vote Democrat, because the party “has a platform that supports the labor movement, the right to organize [and] the right to bargain”, Creighton said.

“The labor movement is allowed to spend money on political actions, and they do,” she said, noting that the motivation behind the reports seem political. “The Trump administration has been trying to eliminate bargaining rights and unions, full stop.”
A 2024 poll by Gallup found 62% of Americans say the Democratic party best serves the interest of union members compared to 27% who said the same about the Republican party.

US labor unions have historically supported Democrats over Republicans since Franklin Delano Roosevelt’s administration passed the National Labor Relations Act in 1935. But Republican presidents, up until Ronald Reagan in the 1980s, refrained from taking hostile positions toward labor unions and collective bargaining.
In 1976, Republican Gerald Ford’s presidential campaign stated “free collective bargaining remains the best way to insure that American workers receive a fair price for their labors.”
But under Reagan, the Republican party began to emphasize so-called “right to work” laws over collective bargaining and adopted more hostile, pro-business stances toward labor unions.

Under Trump’s second term, he issued an executive order to rescind collective bargaining rights from more than 1 million federal workers and made cuts to federal agencies tasked with enforcing labor laws.

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Post uses AI-generated news report to falsely claim Duterte is back in PH
articles.summary: Former president Rodrigo Duterte remains detained; he was not released from detention to attend his daughter’s impeachment trial, contrary to the claim

blocks.text: Claim: Former president Rodrigo Duterte is coming home to the Philippines to attend the impeachment trial of his daughter, Vice President Sara Duterte, as shown in a news report.

Why we fact-checked this: The Facebook reel showing the supposed news report was posted on August 10. It has already received 179,000 views, 7,300 reactions, 1,100 comments, and 1,100 shares as of writing.

The graphic shows the former president waving while a plane is seen in the background. The text on the graphic reads, “Breaking news: Rodrigo Duterte comes home to the Philippines to attend the hearing of Sara Duterte.”

The caption of the post emphasized the claim that Duterte has been released from International Criminal Court (ICC) detention: “[Confirm] nakalabas na po mahal natin [presidente] na magaling Digong Duterte.”
(It is confirmed that our beloved and excellent president, Digong Duterte, has been released.)
Some Facebook users believed the claim, leaving comments in support of the former president.
The facts: Duterte remains detained at the ICC facility in The Hague, Netherlands. The ICC website lists his current status as “In ICC custody.”

The supposed news report was generated using artificial intelligence (AI). AI image detector Sight Engine flagged the image as 99% likely to be AI-generated. Hive Detect also labeled the same image as 99.1% likely to contain AI-generated content.

Reverse image search did not show any credible news report similar to the one being shown in the Facebook reel. There are also no official announcements from the ICC stating that Duterte was released from detention to attend his daughter’s impeachment trial.

Still detained: Duterte’s counsel had repeatedly appealed for an interim release citing health reasons, but this has been denied by the ICC. The court’s latest decision was issued in May 2026, when the Trial Chamber III said the former leader is still not eligible for temporary liberty.

Under the Rome Statute, a suspect cannot be released if they present risk factors, which include the danger of fleeing, obstructing justice by intimidating witnesses, or recommitting the same alleged crimes. Article 60(3) notes that the court may modify its ruling on a person’s detention or release if circumstances have changed.
In its ruling, the chamber said, “The Chamber therefore finds no notable change in circumstances [of Duterte] that warrants the release of the accused, with or without conditions.”

Duterte was arrested in March 2025 for crimes against humanity linked to killings in his brutal war on drugs. In April 2026, the ICC’s pre-trial chamber confirmed all the charges against him, including three counts of murder, covering 49 incidents of killings and 78 victims. His full trial is scheduled to begin in November.

Impeachment: Meanwhile, Duterte’s daughter is facing an impeachment trial for her alleged misuse of confidential funds, unexplained wealth, bribery, and threats to assassinate President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta Marcos, and former House speaker Martin Romualdez. (LIVE UPDATES: Impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte)
Previous fact checks: Rappler has previously fact-checked similar false claims about Duterte:

items: FACT CHECK: 2025 photo of Duterte in Hong Kong used to falsely claim he’s back in PH
FACT CHECK: Video saying Duterte will be released in July 2026 is fake, AI-generated
FACT CHECK: ICC did not junk Duterte’s case; post misrepresents old VP Sara statement
FACT CHECK: Video of ICC judge saying Duterte should be released is AI-generated
FACT CHECK: Photos of Duterte being assisted in ICC courtroom are AI-generated
FACT CHECK: No ICC admission of being ‘paid’ by Marcos gov’t in Duterte case

blocks.text: – Angelee Kaye Abelinde/Rappler.com
Angelee Kaye Abelinde is a student journalist based in Naga City, and an alumna of Rappler’s Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship 2024.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.title: Russia kills at least 12 on sixth night of drone attacks on Kyiv
articles.summary: Zelenskyy says Moscow is capitalising on shortage of US-made Patriot interceptors to lower morale in capital

blocks.text: At least 12 people have been killed in and around Kyiv overnight as Ukraine’s capital endured a sixth consecutive night of Russian drone and missile attacks aimed at shattering infrastructure and lowering the morale of the city.

Eight of the dead were reported killed in Kyiv, including seven at a railway depot on the city’s left bank, and four more in the surrounding region, after hours of air alerts culminating in a wave of strikes at about 2.30am.

Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Ukraine’s president, said “a significant number of jet-powered drones and ballistic missiles were used in the attack” and that Russia was taking advantage of a shortage of US-made Patriot interceptors.

blocks.caption: A woman collects belongings from her apartment damaged by a Russian missile strike in the town of Boryspil in the Kyiv region. Photograph: Valentyn Ogirenko/Reuters

blocks.text: In a morning post on social media, Zelenskyy said: “Russia always plans its strikes specifically to cause as much destruction to people’s lives as possible, and it succeeds only when air defence capabilities are insufficient.”

Kyiv and the surrounding towns and villages have come under sustained attack in the past few days. Thirty-eight people were killed after a Russian drone struck an ammunition store in Myla, 15 miles west of Kyiv on Thursday, the hit causing hours of secondary explosions and damaging nearby homes.
after newsletter promotion

Ukraine’s air force said Russia had attacked 28 locations, focusing on the cities of Kyiv, Odesa and their surroundings. Air defence shot down five Iskander ballistic missiles, two Banderol and five Kalibr cruise missiles and 187 out of 218 drones. Officials no longer reveal the total numbers of missiles fired.

Oleksandr Pertsovskyi, the chief executive of Ukrainian Railways, said six of the seven people killed in and around the depot were employees of the network. Another rail worker had been hospitalised, he added.

Kyiv has been chronically short of air defence systems since the supply of US made Patriot interceptors dried up. The Patriots are the only weapon that can effectively stop high-speed Russian ballistic missiles, made at the rate of about 60 a month.

Lockheed Martin, the US company that makes the most capable Pac-3 interceptors, produces about 600 a year, but US military supplies have been depleted during the US war with Iran. Ukraine is trying to secure a stockpile of about 300 for the winter, paid for by European allies, in a supply deal agreed with the US.

Moscow appears to be trying to take advantage of an absence of air defence capability before winter, in an escalation of a conflict nearly deadlocked on the frontline. Ukraine has been responding by attacking oil refineries, warehouses and other military facilities deep inside Russia, aiming to hurt the country’s economy.

articles.title: Iran says it will return to ceasefire if US does
articles.summary: Speaking on the sidelines of the SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan, Iran's president Pezeshkian called on the US to return to a ceasefire deal.

image.caption: President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran is interested in keeping the ceasefire agreement with the USImage: Vyacheslav Prokofyev/Sputnik/REUTERS

blocks.text: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Tuesday said Tehran would reciprocate any US move that signals a return to the collapsed interim ceasefire deal.

"I state explicitly that if the United States returns to its commitments under the ... memorandum of understanding, the Islamic Republic of Iran will immediately take reciprocal action," Pezeshkian said on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan.
Pezeshkian accused the US of "reneging on its commitments" under the agreement, which fell apart in June, with both sides accusing the other of violating the agreement's terms.

At the time, the US carried out strikes on Iranian targets after what it called "continued aggression" against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, with an Iranian drone striking a Panama-flagged tanker.
Tehran has repeatedly said it ⁠will ​allow free navigation through the Strait, but on its terms. A diplomatic solution to the conflict remains elusive.

Pezeshkian's comments come shortly after the US and Iran traded fire for the first time in over a month. The US said it struck Iranian minelaying forces on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday and Iran targeted US forces in the Middle East in response.
US President Donald Trump told reporters in the Oval Office on Monday that there will be a "response" to the Iranian attacks, but said the latest strikes did not mean a return to full-scale war.
Putin and Xi meet at SCO summit
Pezeshkian is due to have talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin later Tuesday.
The meeting takes place as Russia's full-scale invasion into Ukraine continues to rumble on for more than four years.
Earlier, Putin met Chinese President Xi Jinping, who has provided Russia with implicit economic backing during the Ukraine war.
According to Xi, the China-Russia pact has become "more solid" and that its "prospects will be even brighter."
On his side, Putin said the two countries' cooperation was "successfully developing on all fronts."

blocks.caption: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping met and discussed relations between the two countriesImage: Kristina Solovyova/Sputnik/REUTERS

blocks.text: The SCO is a bloc promoted by Russia and China as an alternative to Western power, which has in the past mostly served for economic discussions, with Moscow and Beijing pushing its significance in recent years.
Its 10 members also include India and Pakistan, while its 15 "dialogue partners" being Turkey and Qatar, amongst others.

articles.title: Palace respects Pineda's 'let us pray' remarks, but says gov't still there
articles.summary: After Pampanga Governor Lilia Pineda drew flak for her statements urging citizens to pray to God amid all these calamities, Malacañang said that it respected such statements but emphasized the…

blocks.text: Published September 1, 2026 5:52pm

After Pampanga Governor Lilia Pineda drew flak for her statements urging citizens to pray to God amid all these calamities, Malacañang said that it respected such statements but emphasized the government still has responsibilities to its people.
In an interview with GMA News’ Unang Balita, Pineda said that there was no one who could stop severe floods except for God, adding that the government could not do it all.

“Igagalang po natin kung anong mensahe mismo ni Governor Pineda dahil siya po ang nakakaramdam nito. Wala naman po sigurong masama kung talagang sama-sama rin tayong mananalangin dahil sabi nga po natin isa sa mga dahilan ng ganitong klaseng unos ay climate change— isa lamang ito maraming factors,” Castro said in a press conference on Tuesday.

(We respect Governor Pineda’s message because she herself experienced it. There is nothing wrong if we pray together because these types of calamities are a result of climate change—this is one of the factors.)
The Palace said that it would be difficult to dictate how officials relay their messages to their constituents, so it is up to the people how they receive these types of statements.

Castro also agreed with Pineda that it was difficult for the government to do it all alone, as it needed collaboration with citizens. For example, in areas prone to disaster, the public should follow the “no-build zone” rule, she said. It is up to the local government unit to implement these rules however, added Castro.

The Palace official reassured the public that they will not be left behind by the government, but stressed that the government also needs the people’s collaboration and compliance to get through calamities.

“Ang gobyerno po ay laging nandidiyan, ang pagbibigay ng ayuda ay nandidiyan. Pero kailangan din po kayo ng gobyerno para mas gumaan ang nararanasan nating mga delubyo, kasi kayo rin po ay may responsibilidad para sa ating pamahalaan,” Castro said.

(The government is always there, the giving of aid is there. But the government also needs you to lighten the effects of these hazards, because you also have a responsibility to the government.) —RF, GMA News

articles.title: Questions abound for Djokovic after US Open loss, 3 years without Grand Slam title
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic waved goodbye, made a heart shape with his hands and blew kisses to the crowd as he walked off the court inside Arthur Ashe Stadium to a standing ovation. Among those applauding in…

blocks.text: Novak Djokovic waved goodbye, made a heart shape with his hands and blew kisses to the crowd as he walked off the court inside Arthur Ashe Stadium to a standing ovation.

Among those applauding in return were Djokovic’s 11-year-old son Stefan, while his 8-year-old daughter Tara covered her eyes and loaded her floppy-eared stuffed animal into a bag that went around her shoulder.
Back down on the court, Djokovic had his two black bags — one containing his rackets and the other more equipment — hanging from his shoulders.

After his first-round loss to Mariano Navone at the U.S. Open on Sunday night, it remains to be seen whether the 39-year-old Djokovic will ever bring those bags out on a court again for a professional match.

The 7-6 (5), 5-7, 4-6, 6-2, 6-1 loss marked Djokovic’s earliest Grand Slam exit in two decades — dating back to the 2006 Australian Open — and the first time ever that he lost his opener at the U.S. Open.
The holder of a men's record 24 Grand Slam singles titles, Djokovic has now gone three straight years without winning a major.
Physical issues

Perhaps even more concerning than his record — which has otherwise still been fairly competitive since his last Grand Slam title at the 2023 U.S. Open — is that Djokovic has consistently struggled with physical issues this year.

After a run to the Australian Open final to start the year, Djokovic played little because of an injured right shoulder. Then he appeared weakened by a Paris heat wave in a five-set loss to Brazilian teenager Joao Fonseca in the third round of the French Open.
“I was barely standing on my legs toward the end of the match,” Djokovic said after getting beaten by Fonseca.

Djokovic revived himself for a run to the semifinals at Wimbledon and then struggled again at the Cincinnati Open this month when he was beaten by 50th-ranked Thiago Agustin Tirante in his opening match.
After the loss to Tirante, Djokovic said an unspecified health condition made it difficult for him to play in hot and humid weather.

“It’s just a condition that I have, health-wise, that has been bothering me for the past couple of years,” Djokovic said. “A lot of issues, especially when it is humid and it is hot. … Nerves and everything involved that make it worse.”

Djokovic’s issues against Navone began midway through the first set when he appeared to be struggling with the heat and humidity. Djokovic led early on in the first set but Navone got back on serve before the match was briefly halted for the roof to be closed because of light rain.
As Djokovic sat in his chair during the break, he kept moving an ice pack around his face, head and neck.

Navone won the first in a tiebreaker and things eventually got much worse for Djokovic, who threw up at least once and later appeared to be cramping when he grabbed at his left foot. Djokovic swallowed pills brought to him by a doctor and had his lower back massaged during a medical timeout between the fourth and fifth sets, and he grimaced after several shots.
Djokovic made 70 unforced errors in a painful performance that ended a few minutes before midnight.

“It’s something that I’ve been carrying, unfortunately, pretty much every match this year: vomiting, throwing up, a serious issue there,” Djokovic said. “Then my whole body starts to collapse, basically cramping and pain. Yeah, the back just gave up in the end and shoulder, and I couldn’t close it out.”
What's next?

Where does Djokovic go from here? While he hasn’t openly discussed an imminent retirement, one final hurrah at the Australian Open — the Grand Slam tournament he’s won a record 10 times — in January would be a fitting setting for a final send-off.
Or he could continue competing into his 40s.
After all, Djokovic has reached two Grand Slam finals and six semifinals over the last three years.
“I feel when I’m healthy, I’m still able to play as a top-five player, still able to compete at the highest level,” Djokovic said after his semifinal loss to Jannik Sinner at Wimbledon this year.
Roger Federer and Rafael Nadal's physical issues
Djokovic is the last man still competing among the Big Three players who dominated the game over the last two decades.
Roger Federer (knee) and Rafael Nadal (hip) also struggled with physical issues before they retired in 2022 and 2024, respectively. Federer was 41 when he stopped and Nadal was 38.
Djokovic’s 24 major titles are two more than Nadal’s 22 and four more than Federer’s 20. Those numbers prompt some to consider Djokovic tennis' GOAT.

“That’s OK. He has done incredible,” Federer said last week. “It’s amazing what he has been able to do and still now. I would have thought that maybe he was getting to a place where all of a sudden we would see a much bigger decline.”
Now — perhaps — Djokovic is declining more severely.

articles.title: Marcos tells agencies: No room for complacency on climate change
articles.summary: Palace Press Officer Claire Castro told reporters on Tuesday that Marcos had called for a meeting with various government agencies in light of the flooding that occurred across Luzon.

blocks.text: Published September 1, 2026 5:50pm

In the aftermath of the devastating impact of successive cyclones and the Southwest Monsoon, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. urged government agencies to remain vigilant and avoid complacency in addressing the threats posed by climate change.
Palace Press Officer Claire Castro told reporters on Tuesday that Marcos had called for a meeting with various government agencies in light of the flooding that occurred across Luzon.
Castro said several countries across the world have been impacted by storms, monsoons, and floods, including Nepal, China, Laos, Pakistan, India and Kenya.
“Ang utos ni Pangulong Marcos Jr., huwag tayong magpakampante,” Castro said. (President Marcos Jr. said not to be complacent.)

“Seryosohin natin ang banta ng climate change. Kahandaan ang susi para malampasan natin ang panganib nito,” she added. (Let us take the threat of climate change seriously. Readiness is the key to overcoming its danger.)
The Department of Education has been instructed to instill in children the effects of climate change.

The continuous rains and floods destroyed several houses and several infrastructures. A bridge in Tarlac City collapsed, killing at least one person. Some riverside houses in Lubao, Pampanga also collapsed into strong currents.

For local government units, Castro cited two master plans that could have prevented people from building structures in dangerous areas: a 1941 master plan in Metro Manila, as well as a 1936 plan in Cebu.

“Ayon sa Pangulo, dapat ipatupad ang batas pati ang ‘no-build zone’. Huwag nang mamulitika, ipatupad ang batas at dapat ipaliwanag sa lahat na kailangang mas maging istrikto sa pag-implementa ng batas para sa ating kaligtasan,” Castro said.

(The President said that the law should be enforced, including a ‘no build zone’. Let us not be political and implement the law, and it should be explained to everyone to be stricter when it comes to enforcing environmental laws.)
Castro did not name a personality or agency responsible for the non-implementation of these plans.
However, Commissioner Albert dela Cruz of the Climate Change Commission had previously lamented that the other agencies do not listen to them—even though Marcos himself is the chair of the body.
Castro said that this will not happen again, saying that the required policies and projects that could mitigate the effects of climate change must be implemented.
She admitted, however, that not all of them will be accomplished before Marcos’ term ends. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Apple's new CEO John Ternus makes AI top priority
articles.summary: John Ternus is just the third Apple CEO in 30 years. His primary challenge is to correct the company's faltering AI strategy to preserve its position as a big tech leader.

image.caption: John Ternus (left) has big shoes to fill as he takes over from former Apple CEO Tim CookImage: Apple

blocks.text: On September 1, a new era begins at Apple as John Ternus becomes just the third man to hold the CEO role at the tech giant since 1997.

Ternus was announced as Tim Cook's successor back in April, bringing Cook's 15 years at the helm of one of the world's biggest companies to an end. Since then, Ternus, a leading hardware engineer at the company, has been working closely alongside Cook in preparation for the big job.

Just as Cook had when he took over from the iconic Steve Jobs, Ternus has big shoes to fill. Apple's share price has increased by more than 2,000% since Cook took over in 2011 and the company has sold more than 3.1 billion iPhones in that time.
Ternus faces a range of challenges at Apple, but his ability to keep the company at the top will hinge on how he reshapes its AI strategy.
Apple has struggled to successfully embrace the technology so far, with critics saying it has fallen far behind its rivals.
September 9: John Ternus makes public debut

Ternus will make his public debut as CEO at Apple's Autumn product launch event on September 9. Dubbed "Surprise and Shine," Ternus is expected to announce the company's first foldable iPhone as well as a new version of an AI-powered Siri, Apple's virtual assistant.

blocks.caption: John Ternus made his name as a key engineer at AppleImage: Mason Trinca/REUTERS

blocks.text: Francisco Jeronimo, VP for Data and Analytics at tech research group IDC, says Apple's forthcoming announcements were planned during Cook's time in charge and that it will be 2027 before the direction Ternus wants to take the company in becomes apparent.
"Of course, September 9 will be quite an important milestone for the company around foldables and around innovation," he told DW.
"But I don't think we have seen anything that could indicate that Apple is behaving in a different way or is showing a different kind of strategy because Tim Cook is not in the job anymore — yet."
Apple's huge AI challenge
What observers will be looking out for from Ternus on September 9 is the extent to which he focuses his remarks on AI.

While it was already patently clear when he was announced in April that the artificial intelligence boom would be pivotal to his time at the helm, it has become even clearer in the five months since the unveiling that the AI revolution is here to stay.

"It's becoming clear that AI is not a fad, is not something that will go away in the next two or three years," says Jeronimo. "It's something that will dictate the future of most tech companies and indeed all companies."
He reckons AI could be "the most consequential technology" for Apple because it could either help it maintain its lofty position or create a set of daunting challenges.
The biggest challenge he sees is that Apple doesn't "control" AI infrastructure the way it could previously in terms of designing and controlling both the hardware and software for its key products.

"Maybe that will be what John Ternus will be doing differently from Tim Cook, because at the moment, even if Apple built their own AI technology, the reality is that they still depend on someone else," he says.

Apple's reliance on other companies in the AI realm has led it into unfamiliar territory. It struck a deal with OpenAI in 2024 to integrate ChatGPT into the iPhone but it has led to a bitter dispute between the companies. Apple sued OpenAI earlier this year, alleging that the AI company stole its trade secrets.
Earlier this year, it announced a deal with Google, whereby the search giant's Gemini models would be used for Apple's own AI models and its new AI-powered version of Siri.

"The risk for Apple is to become less relevant in a world where companies like OpenAI and Anthropic are leading in terms of technology, in terms of awareness, in terms of services and potentially in terms of hardware," says Jeronimo.
For decades, Apple's success has been built on its physical products, from the iPad to the iPhone.

"If devices from OpenAI become available, that could be very, very risky for Apple. They could completely disrupt the experience and the way we interact with technology. And if Apple is not on the front of that innovation, that is a big risk," he says.
A combination of Jobs and Cook?

Ternus' background as an engineer who worked on Apple's core products, as well as innovations such as the Apple Watch and AirPods, means he will be expected to lead the way on new AI-driven products for the company.

He also played a central role championing Apple's shift to designing its own chips instead of relying on external suppliers like Intel — precisely the kind of independence Apple would like to achieve when it comes to AI.

Jeronimo thinks Apple still has big advantages, givenits massive volume of users as well as the company culture of having dominated innovation in tech for decades. He thinks if Apple can get to grips with AI under Ternus, it could lead to huge success.

blocks.caption: The role of Apple CEO is in itself iconic, in part due to Steve Jobs' tenureImage: Kristy Macdonald/picture alliance/AP

blocks.text: "What we will see in the next years will dictate whether Apple is on the right track or if they are really struggling," he says.

For Ternus, the first task will be to simply fit smoothly and convincingly into a role that both Jobs and Cook undeniably made their own. "Steve Jobs was the guru of innovation and disruption and Tim Cook was the guru of execution," says Jeronimo.
"I think John Ternus can be a combination of both."
The Apple story

articles.title: DA still assessing Pax Silica's impact on agriculture
articles.summary: The Department of Agriculture (DA) said Tuesday that it is still assessing the possible impact of the controversial Pax Silica initiative on the country"s agriculture sector.

blocks.text: Published September 1, 2026 5:48pm
The Department of Agriculture (DA) said Tuesday that it is still assessing the possible impact of the controversial Pax Silica initiative on the country’s agriculture sector.

During the House budget briefing on the DA’s proposed P198.45-billion budget for 2027, Gabriela Women’s Party-list Representative Sarah Elago asked the department about its actions regarding the project, which has raised concerns over its potential impact on farmers in Tarlac province.

“Has the DA conducted an assessment of its potential effects, especially given reports that around 15,000 farmers and up to 20,000 Aeta people could lose their livelihoods and ancestral lands because of this project?” she asked in Filipino.
In response, Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu-Laurel Jr. said the assessment was still ongoing.

"Right now, we are still thoroughly assessing the full effects of Pax Silica. The initial reports I have seen indicate that not that many people will be affected. But our assessment is not yet finished," he said.

“From what I understand from what I see on TV, within the 1,600-hectare Clark area, it doesn't seem like there are that many directly affected farmers. I really cannot say as of now until our study comes out on what the effects will be on agriculture," Tiu-Laurel added.
Asked when the assessment would be completed, Tiu-Laurel said, “Perhaps, in another 30 days.”

Pax Silica is the US Department of State’s flagship initiative on artificial intelligence and supply chain security, aimed at advancing a new economic security framework among allies and trusted partners.
Under the initiative, the Philippines and the United States are working to establish a 4,000-acre industrial hub envisioned as a model for AI-focused investment within the Luzon Economic Corridor.
The Department of Environment and Natural Resources earlier confirmed that no environmental impact assessment (EIA) had yet been processed for the proposed hub in New Clark City.
Progressive and environmental groups have raised concerns over the project’s potential environmental and social impacts.
Malacañang, however, has assured that no farmers will be displaced, saying the 3,500-hectare area allotted for buildable zones includes the site identified for the Pax Silica project.
Around 6,000 hectares have been reserved for green spaces, forest reserves and planned agricultural areas, it said.— MCG, GMA News
