articles.title: MMDA GM Torre explains viral Marikina ‘flood control’ video
articles.summary: Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) General Manager Nicolas Torre III explained a viral video showing a Marikina City skid-steer loader apparently scooping water from the river and…

blocks.text: Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) General Manager Nicolas Torre III explained a viral video showing a Marikina City skid-steer loader apparently scooping water from the river and dumping it back.

The clip, posted by former Rep. Kiko Barzaga on Aug. 30 with the caption “Meow Meow Vlog: Marikina flood control,” has drawn 6.3 million views and 122,000 reactions on Facebook as of Tuesday, Sept. 1.

In the video, Barzaga appears alongside footage of the loader, quipping: “Galing talaga ng flood control ng Marikina City. Lipat na ako d’yan sa 2028 (Marikina City’s flood control is really something. I’ll move there in 2028).”
Some netizens criticized the deployment of the machine, calling it a waste of public funds and suggesting the driver was simply playing around.
On Aug. 31, Torre clarified in a Facebook post that the loader was not scooping river water for flood control. Instead, it was cleaning its bucket after clearing mud during post flood operations.
He added that the water served a dual purpose -- washing the bucket and flushing mud and sediment along the riverbank.
Several commenters echoed Torre’s explanation, noting the operator was washing off mud from clearing the opposite side of the river.
Others stressed the bucket was simply being rinsed, not used to push back floodwaters.
Torre also criticized those mocking the workers, urging the public to understand the situation before commenting.
He called on netizens to avoid ridiculing cleanup crews, who he said were working in muddy conditions to help restore the area. (Freya Gan)

articles.title: Palace urges public to do its part in solving nation’s problems
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang on Tuesday urged the public to do their part in keeping their communities safe, saying the government cannot solve the country’s problems alone. Palace Press Officer…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang on Tuesday urged the public to do their part in keeping their communities safe, saying the government cannot solve the country’s problems alone.

Palace Press Officer Claire Castro made the statement after Pampanga Governor Lilia Pineda urged residents in a Monday interview with GMA News to pray, heed government warnings, prepare for emergencies, and prioritize their families’ safety amid heavy rains and flooding.
“Hindi ninyo puwede pong iasa sa gobyerno ang lahat dahil sa kadami po natin lahat. Kailangan may plano rin kayo sa pamilya ninyo para ligtas po ang mga pamilya ninyo,” she added.
(You cannot rely solely on the government because there are so many of us. You need to have a plan to keep your family safe.)
Pineda’s remarks that drew criticism from the public. Castro, on one hand, explained the government’s position.

“Let’s be real: the government is always there, and assistance is always available. But the government also needs you to help lessen the impact of the disasters we experience because you, too, have a responsibility to our government,” Castro said at a media briefing.

“The president’s message is that no one will be left behind. We will all rise together and eventually feel relief. Perhaps what we really need is to work together because the government cannot do it alone,” she added.
Castro also said she respects Pineda’s statement, noting that the governor knows the situation in her province.

“There’s probably nothing wrong with all of us praying together, especially since, as we’ve said, one of the reasons for this kind of severe weather is climate change—although that is just one factor; there are many factors involved,” the palace official said. /mcm

articles.title: Pampanga gov: Disaster response takes priority over outfit backlash
articles.summary: CITY OF SAN FERNANDO, Pampanga — Pampanga Gov. Lilia Pineda asserted that she is “focused on disaster response” instead of minding criticisms over her wearing a branded raincoat while inspecting a…

blocks.text: CITY OF SAN FERNANDO, Pampanga — Pampanga Gov. Lilia Pineda asserted that she is “focused on disaster response” instead of minding criticisms over her wearing a branded raincoat while inspecting a damaged dike in Lubao town.
She made known her priority after apologizing in a television interview on Monday night.
“Kung nagkamali kami sa ganoong attire namin, sorry,” the governor said, referring to herself and her son, Vice Gov. Dennis Pineda.
(If we made a mistake in wearing such attire, sorry.)
She said she respected her critics’ opinions, adding that their comments were a “wake-up call to me.” She added that she and her son do not wear branded clothes every day.
On social media, several netizens accused the Pinedas of being insensitive to the poverty around them. Some comments were disrespectful and below the belt.
Supporters of Pineda, called by locals “Governor Nanay,” took to social media to defend her, citing her programs on health, education, agriculture and job creation.

“It is my mandate to focus now on disaster response. I cannot be distracted. I need to prioritize the delivery of services to 296 flooded villages in 19 local towns and the capital and 1.2 million people,” the governor told the Inquirer in a phone interview.
The Pampanga Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office reported P1.3 billion in losses to crops, fisheries, machinery and facilities.

Paul Pangilinan Corpus, an educator who finished his degree under the Capitol’s scholarship program, posted his observation that “trolls were at work” against the Pinedas because they had “almost uniform content,” referring to a common pubmat (card) and captions. “Some showed to be valid remarks,” Corpus said.
Reached by phone in San Simon, where a flood retention wall was breached, Vice Gov. Pineda declined to comment on the criticisms.
“Nagseserbisyo po kami ni Governor Nanay sa mga Kapampangan. Sana yun po ang makita nila,” he said.
(Governor Nanay and I are serving our fellow Kapampanga. I hope that’s what they see.)

Pampanga was the “hardest hit” province by the monsoon rains and recent typhoons, according to Office of Civil Defense Administrator Undersecretary Harold Cabreros, who conducted an aerial inspection on Monday./coa

articles.title: Olongapo City under state of calamity due to severe flooding
articles.summary: SAN ANTONIO, Zambales — The Olongapo City government on Tuesday has declared the city under a state of calamity after weeks of intense rainfall that triggered widespread flooding, landslides, damage…

blocks.text: SAN ANTONIO, Zambales — The Olongapo City government on Tuesday has declared the city under a state of calamity after weeks of intense rainfall that triggered widespread flooding, landslides, damage to properties and infrastructure, and the displacement of residents.

The city council approved Resolution No. 196, Series of 2026, during its regular session on Tuesday based on the recommendation of the Olongapo City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (OCDRRMC), which adopted Resolution No. 2026-04 during an emergency meeting on Monday.

In his endorsement to the city council, Mayor Rolen C. Paulino Jr. said Olongapo recorded 2,900.5 millimeters of cumulative rainfall throughout August, about 3.47 times the normal August rainfall of 835.7 mm.
He said 569.5 mm of rain fell from August 28 to 29 alone, equivalent to about 68 percent of the city’s normal rainfall for the entire month.

The prolonged, heavy rains resulted in flooding, landslides, damage to properties and infrastructure, environmental degradation, disruption of transportation and public services, and the displacement of residents, according to the resolution.

The city government also said the successive weather disturbances had significantly disrupted normal social and economic activities and placed considerable strain on its disaster response, recovery, and public service capabilities.

In an earlier interview, Jeffrey Lapid, head of the Olongapo City Disaster Risk Reduction Management Office, said that 13 out of 17 villages in the city were flooded during intense rainfall as of Saturday, Aug. 29.

At least 730 families, or 2,530 individuals, evacuated from their flooded homes. The city also recorded one fatality, a 3-year-old boy in Barangay Old Cabalan who was swept by rushing floodwaters when a wall above their house suddenly collapsed.

The declaration is expected to facilitate the immediate mobilization and use of available resources for response, relief, recovery, and rehabilitation efforts for affected residents, communities, properties, and infrastructure.
The city and other parts of Zambales continue to recover from repeated flooding and other impacts of heavy rains in recent weeks./coa

articles.title: Mass Russian barrage kills 12 in Kyiv
articles.summary: KYIV, Ukraine – Russia launched a barrage of drones and ballistic missiles at Kyiv and its surrounding region overnight, killing at least 12 people and wounding 21, Ukraine said Tuesday,…

blocks.text: KYIV, Ukraine – Russia launched a barrage of drones and ballistic missiles at Kyiv and its surrounding region overnight, killing at least 12 people and wounding 21, Ukraine said Tuesday, hitting the capital as children were set to return to school after the summer.

Moscow has intensified its strikes on Kyiv this summer, more than four-and-a-half years into its invasion, with US-brokered talks frozen and the Kremlin not dropping its maximalist demands to end the war.
Kyiv has tightened security following weeks of attacks and AFP journalists in the capital heard around a dozen loud explosions and saw flashes in the sky early Tuesday.
President Volodymyr Zelensky denounced “Russian terror” and said an Indian citizen was among the dead, calling on allies to boost Ukraine’s air defence this autumn.
Authorities said eight of the victims were killed within Kyiv and that most of them were railway workers who died after a ballistic missile hit a rail depot.
Oleksandr Pertsovskyi, chief executive of Ukrainian Railways, said six of the company’s employees were killed.
He said the attack caused “extensive destruction”, including the complete devastation of a workshop, while fires continued to burn at some sites.
Another four people were killed in the Kyiv region, Ukrainian prosecutors announced, saying a residential building was damaged in the suburb of Boryspil.
‘As much destruction as possible’
Zelensky said 50 people were evacuated from the building in Boryspil.

“Russia always plans its strikes specifically to cause as much destruction to people’s lives as possible, and it succeeds only when air defence capabilities are insufficient,” he said on social media.
He said it was “very important” that deliveries boosting Kyiv’s air defence “increase this fall”.
EU defence and foreign ministers are due to gather in Ireland from Tuesday to grapple with how to bolster Kyiv, as the Kremlin escalates its air campaign.
Ukraine’s border service also announced that Moscow had hit the Orlivka ferry checkpoint on the frontier with NATO-member Romania with “Shahed-type attack drones”.
Romania has shot down Russian drones entering its airspace twice this year.
Ukrainian officials also said Moscow had struck a “fire and rescue vehicle” in Zaporizhzhia, wounding four people, and attacked the southern Odesa region.
‘Massive strike’
In Moscow, Russia’s defence ministry said its forces had carried out a “massive strike” using long-range weapons and attack drones.
It said the attack targeted military-industrial and fuel and energy facilities in Kyiv and the surrounding region.
The ministry also said it had struck infrastructure in the Odesa region and the ports of Odesa and Chornomorsk.
The Ukrainian air force had warned that the threat of “ballistic weapons and other means of attack against Kyiv and the region remains in effect”, and urged residents to remain in shelters.
Ukrainian children return to school on Tuesday, and the Kyiv regional military administration has warned there must be no large events in high-risk areas.

Kyiv and its surrounding areas have come under sustained pressure from Russian attacks in recent weeks, with jet-powered drones adding to the threat and triggering as many as a dozen air-raid alerts a day.
One weekend attack on an ammunition depot killed 38 people in the capital’s suburbs.
Both sides have escalated long-range strikes in recent months, targeting infrastructure such as warehouses, businesses and oil and port facilities, as well as ships, increasing civilian casualties.
Ukraine faces a shortage of interceptor missiles, particularly US-made Patriot systems for use against ballistic threats.

articles.title: 'Mama cat' is here: Jenny Barzaga takes oath in House as Kiko Barzaga's replacement
articles.summary: Newly-elected Cavite 4th district Rep. Jennifer "Jenny" Barzaga took her oath of office on Tuesday afternoon, Sept. 1, as she offically filled the House seat left by her controversial son, expelled…

blocks.text: Newly-elected Cavite 4th district Rep. Jennifer "Jenny" Barzaga took her oath of office on Tuesday afternoon, Sept. 1, as she offically filled the House seat left by her controversial son, expelled "congressmeow" Francisco "Kiko" Barzaga.
Rep. Barzaga, a former Dasmariñas City mayor, was allowed to take her oath during plenary session upon a motion by Majority Leader Ilocos Norte 1st district Rep. Sandro Marcos.
Marcos noted that Rep. Barzaga garnered the most votes during April 29 special elections held to determine the empty seat.
Deputy Speaker Iloilo 1st district Rep. Janette Garin, the presiding officer at that time, carried the presidential son's motion.
The district’s Board of Canvassers the elder Barzaga as the winner of the special election early morning Sunday morning, Aug. 30.
The ex-mayor garnered 201,893 votes--more than six times the total of the second-placer.

The landslide victory proved that Dasmariñas City remained a Barzaga bailiwick in spite of the controversial acts of the Gen Z solon, Kiko, who was essentially kicked out by his own colleagues in the House of Representatives last June.
His mother was also his predecessor in the district.
Raul Rex Mangubat finished a distant second in the congressional race with 30,361 votes, followed by Jacinto Frani Jr. (24,350), Marvin Dupal-Ag (1,184), and Lysander Ordenes (561).
There were 258,361 vote-casters out of the district's 447,387 registered voters, resulting to a turnout of 57.75 percent.
Commission on Elections (Comelec) Chairman George Garcia earlier said that the turnout target was 50 percent.

articles.title: Army officials testify they were surprised DepEd used certification to account for confidential funds
articles.summary: Two senior officials of the Philippine Army on Tuesday, September 1, testified before the Senate Impeachment Court that the certifications they issued to the Department of Education (DepEd) under…

blocks.text: Two senior officials of the Philippine Army on Tuesday, September 1, testified before the Senate Impeachment Court that the certifications they issued to the Department of Education (DepEd) under Vice President Sara Duterte merely confirmed that anti-insurgency activities for the youth took place but cannot validate, justify or prove the lawful disbursement of P112.5-million in confidential funds.

On Day 20 of the impeachment trial, Assistant Chiefs of Staff for Civil-Military Operations Col. Manaros Boransing and Col. Magtanggol Panopio, witnesses presented by the House prosecution panel, testified that their certifications only covered activity attendance and contained zero validation of financial liquidation or reward payouts to informants.

Panopio said he was surprised to know that the certification he issued under orders from retired Maj. Gen. Gabriel Viray III—which was based on the request of DepEd Undersecretary Nolasco Mempin—were used to justify their use of its confidential funds before the Commission on Audit (COA).
“We were a bit surprised because our certification is only for the conduct of the Youth Leadership Summit (YLS). We didn’t certify anything about money or funds, Your Honor,” Panopio told the court.
Upon Senator-judge Risa Hontiveros’ questioning, both Panopio and Boransing disavowed DepEd’s use of their certifications to justify their expenditures during COA’s scrutiny.
“The certification was theirs, DepEd and other stakeholders’ participation in the YLS and the Information Education Communication (IEC),” he said.
When Hontiveros further asked: “So you did not certify that they spent funds, whether regular or confidential and intellgence funds (CIFs), for the activities of the Philippine Army?”
Boransing replied: “Yes, Maam.”

When Hontiveros asked if they indeed have no knowledge on how the DepEd spent their CIFs for YLS and IEC campaign activities of the Philippine Army, Boransing said “Yes, your honor. I do not have any personal knowledge.”

Panopio also stated that the army only conducted the YLS in their area of operation.Boransing also clarified that summits are community leadership programs and therefore, “There is no intelligence operations when we do the specific activities.”
Panopio similarly told Senator-judge Erwin Tulfo that the summits focus merely on community relations rather than gathering intelligence.
“There was no mention of any funds in the certifications that we issued,” Panopio said.
Boransing in his response, also to Tulfo, explained that coordination and other expenses of the Army participants to the YLS is programmed by the Army through its budget.
“There were no funds released from any government agencies, specifically from DepEd, sir, to the 1st Infantry Tabak Division,” Boransing said.
He also said they were also never informed that his certifications would be used to justify DepEd’s use of confidential funds before the COA.

Meanwhile, upon questioning by Presiding Officer and Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero, Boransing, who supervised and monitored the two anti-communist recruitment initiatives, said it is possible that the vice president might have utilized the DepEd’s own budget allocation for its youth training programs but unaware it was from the agency’s confidential funds.
“Yes, sir. What I know is they arrived there. They were there during the YSL and traveling, as I know in the government, entails expenses and permission to leave the post,” he said.
Currently, Duterte is being tried over alleged systematic misuse of confidential funds of the DepEd and the Office of the Vice President amounting to P612.5-million.
Based on the timeline, the vice president allegedly spent P112.5-million confidential funds which were withdrawn in three separate single-day withdrawals amounting to P37.5-million each in 2023.

The camp of the vice president earlier sought to justify the use of aliases and releasing acknowledgment receipts (ARs) instead of the official receipts (ORs) in order to protect the identities of the informants who supposedly benefitted from the confidential funds.
ARs submitted by the OVP to the COA included names such as “Mary Grace Piattos,” “Ralph Josh Bacon,” “Antonio Pagong,” “Timon Andrew Pusa,” and “Xuniso Belat.”

Senator-judge Vicente “Tito” Sotto III, for his part, said there is a clear distinction between an alias and a fabricated identity, refuting in part, Senator-judge Robin Padilla’s earlier argument and moves to justify the use of aliases by the vice president.
“If there is a person behind the alias, then it is an alias. If there is no person behind the name, it is a fictitious name or a fake name,” Sotto said citing provisions under Republic Act No. 6085.

articles.title: Sydney records warmest winter on record as Melbourne equals previous hottest temperatures
articles.summary:
New South Wales, Victoria and Tasmania just experienced their warmest-ever winters – and BoM says above-average temperatures expected to continue

Australia’s two biggest cities had their…

blocks.text: Australia’s two biggest cities had their hottest and equal hottest winters on record, with three eastern states also breaking temperature records.

The Bureau of Meteorology’s (BoM) spring outlook shows above average daytime and nighttime temperatures are expected to continue for much of the country, with an increased chance of unusually high maximums.

Dr Simon Grainger, a senior climatologist at the bureau, said Sydney had its warmest winter on record, with the mean temperature of 15.3C at Observatory Hill breaking the previous record of 15.0C set in 2013. Average maximum and minimum temperatures at the same site were also the warmest on record.
Melbourne equalled its 2005 record for winter mean temperature of 12.2C, while Canberra recorded its warmest winter maximum, with an average maximum temperature of 14.7C.

New South Wales, Victoria and Tasmania had their warmest winters on record, and all other states and territories except the Northern Territory were in their top 10 warmest winters on record since 1910.
Australia’s mean temperature was 1.45C above the 1961–1990 average for winter, the equal third-highest on record since national observations began in 1910.
Grainger said much of the south-east’s experience was driven by “relatively warm nights and a lot fewer cold nights”, with several factors at play.
“The local weather patterns certainly assisted. For large parts of this winter we had high pressure systems sitting in the Tasman sea,” he said.
“That allowed a lot of warmer air to come down from the tropics over eastern Australia – places like Sydney, Canberra, Melbourne – with fewer outbreaks of cold air getting in.”
Grainger said the developing strong El Niño had also set up weather patterns that tended to be favourable for high daytime temperatures across southeastern Australia.
“Finally of course, all of this is occurring against the background of a globally warmer climate,” he said.
“Daily [global] land temperatures and daily ocean temperatures during August have been close to or above the historical records that were set only in 2024.”

Australia’s national annual average temperature is about 1.5C higher than in 1910, according to the BoM, and the climate crisis, driven by the burning of fossil fuels, has increased the frequency and severity of extreme weather events.

The record-breaking winter data was released as federal resources minister Madeleine King and Northern Territory chief minister Lia Finocchiaro celebrated turning on the tap that will feed the first fracked gas from the Beetaloo Basin into the territory’s power grid.
It follows a horror northern hemisphere summer of record-breaking heatwaves, drought and wildfires in Europe and North America, and intense rain and typhoons in Asia.
after newsletter promotion

The national average rainfall for winter was 8% above the 1961–1990 average, driven by high rainfall in southern inland Australia. Grainger said parts of inland NSW, Victoria, South Australia and parts of the Northern Territory had above average rainfall, with parts of far-western NSW near the SA border experiencing their wettest winter on record.
SA recorded its sixth wettest winter on record. In contrast, rainfall was below average in parts of the east coast and south-western Australia.

The BoM’s long-range forecast shows below average rainfall is expected to continue through parts of southern and eastern Australia through spring, while above average rainfall is expected in large parts of the west from October.

Grainger said a continuation of above average daytime and nighttime temperatures was likely for much of the country “and with that there’s [a] chance of unusually high maximum and minimum temperatures”.
He said the BoM’s models showed the El Niño in the Pacific Ocean would continue to strengthen through spring, likely peaking in late spring or in summer.

Prof Sarah Perkins-Kirkpatrick, a climate scientist from the Australian National University, said while some people might enjoy the idea of a warmer winter, it had negative consequences for the environment.
“We need to consider what’s happening to our natural ecosystems,” she said.
“A lot of our ecosystems need cooler temperatures, a lot of our animals are used to it, and if we start taking that out of the picture, then things aren’t looking so healthy.”
She pointed to the recent snow season, where low falls had also affected the tourism industry, with resorts in Victoria and NSW forced to close early.
“Snowfall in Australia is pretty rare, and just notching the temperature up to a couple of degrees during winter basically puts us above freezing point most of the time,” she said.

articles.title: Nartatez orders protection of cops deployed in flood-hit areas amid leptospirosis risk
articles.summary: Police General Jose Melencio C. Nartatez Jr., chief of the Philippine National Police (PNP), directed police commanders to provide health protection and other safeguards to personnel carrying out…

blocks.text: Police General Jose Melencio C. Nartatez Jr., chief of the Philippine National Police (PNP), directed police commanders to provide health protection and other safeguards to personnel carrying out disaster response operations in flooded areas as leptospirosis cases continue to rise.

Nartatez ordered chiefs of police and unit commanders to ensure that their personnel have the necessary gear, equipment, and medicines to protect them from health risks linked to prolonged exposure to floodwaters.

“Those who provide service and protection in this time of serious weather challenge must also be taken care of. The protection and welfare of every police personnel should always be considered in every deployment order,” Nartatez said in a statement on Monday, Aug. 31.

The country continues to experience strong rains due to the effects of the enhanced southwest monsoon (habagat), causing widespread flooding in several areas and increasing the exposure of police personnel involved in rescue and other emergency operations.
Nartatez said the safety of police personnel must be considered alongside their duty to assist communities affected by the bad weather.
More than 2,000 PNP personnel and 12,000 Reactionary Standby Support Force personnel were deployed to sustain emergency response and public safety operations across 600 flood-hit areas nationwide.

Police personnel were also deployed in 948 occupied evacuation centers sheltering 31,800 families or 138,325 evacuees. Their duties included search and rescue operations, securing vital installations, clearing roads, and protecting vulnerable groups.
Nartatez praised local police officers for continuing to assist communities despite the difficult conditions.
“We commend the swift mobilization of manpower and resources to help citizens, especially those who need rescue from the floods,” he said.
“Setting aside their personal safety, our police officers braved the torrential rains and strong winds to fulfill their sworn mandate to serve and protect the public,” he added.

The Department of Health (DOH) has been monitoring leptospirosis cases amid the continuing rains and flooding. The disease can be contracted through contact with water or soil contaminated with the urine of infected animals.
The DOH recorded 5,486 leptospirosis cases nationwide from Jan. 4 to Aug. 26, warning that infections could continue to increase over the next two weeks following the recent rains and flooding.

articles.title: Footage of police officer boasting about punching Sydney anti-Herzog protester raises questions about conduct
articles.summary:
Male police officer caught on camera during 9 February protest against visit of Israeli president Isaac Herzog

  • Get our

blocks.text: Video footage has emerged capturing a New South Wales police officer boasting about “punching” a protester in the head “when he was down”, before the protester was charged with assaulting police.

Police body-worn camera footage, which was leaked to a social media account and widely shared over the weekend, reveals a male police officer telling his colleagues during the 9 February protest at Sydney town hall against a visit by the Israeli president, Isaac Herzog: “I fucking pumped that cunt.”
A female officer can be heard replying, “So funny,” before the male officer says: “Then I punched him in the head when he was down.”

Guardian Australia understands the video relates to legal proceedings from a protester who was charged with assaulting police. They were one of three protesters who on Friday had the charges against them dropped.

Police have now withdrawn charges against four of the 30 protesters charged in the wake of the protest. The three protesters who had their charges withdrawn on Friday were scheduled to face a joint hearing alongside 22 others in July 2027.

The premier, Chris Minns, had previously urged the public “to not look at a 10-second clip without the full context” after a number of videos went viral showing police allegedly punching protesters and dragging Muslim worshippers away while they were praying.
The new video of the police bragging about punching the protester is understood to be the first bodycam footage to be widely shared publicly.
In February, the independent police watchdog – the Law Enforcement Conduct Commission (Lecc) – launched Operation Makalu to investigate allegations of police brutality at the protest.
On Tuesday, the NSW Greens MP and spokesperson for justice, Sue Higginson, referred the leaked body-worn camera footage to the watchdog, alleging it was evidence of police misconduct.

“The police misconduct that I personally witnessed on 9 February at town hall was obscene, the impunity was something I have not ever seen before and I have no doubt it was the result of the Minns Labor government suppressing protest with invalidly made laws,” Higginson said in a statement.
“This footage shows the attitude of the police that night and should result in an immediate suspension and investigation of the officers involved.
“The Lecc is already investigating the actions of the police that night, but this evidence warrants immediate action by the NSW police.”
A spokesperson for NSW police said they were aware of the video, but were unable to comment due to the ongoing Lecc investigation.
after newsletter promotion
Guardian Australia approached the premier, Chris Minns, for comment.

The day after the protest, he said that the police were “put in an impossible situation” after protesters attempted to defy the public assembly restriction declaration (Pard) law, which police enforced during the protest.
In April, the court of appeal found that law unconstitutional, ruling in favour of the Palestine Action Group and Blak Caucus who brought a challenge against it.

Majed Kheir, a lawyer who represented two of the three protesters whose charges were on Friday withdrawn, said: “The withdrawal of a further three cases simply reflects recognition of the reality that these cases were doomed to fail.

“The brutal conduct of police on 9 February plainly went so beyond the pale. All charges should be immediately dropped as a first step to restore some level of confidence in the NSW police force that our law enforcement institution can be accountable and acknowledge their wrongdoing.”
A petition launched in June by the NSW Council for Civil Liberties calling for the charges against all the anti-Herzog protesters to be dropped has almost 3,000 signatures.

articles.title: Alphaland temporarily closes Baguio Mountain Lodges amid Itogon landslides
articles.summary: Alphaland Baguio Mountain Lodges (ABML), an ultra-exclusive resort in Benguet province owned by the Ongpin family’s Alphaland Corp., reported that it has temporarily closed its premises amid…

blocks.text: Alphaland Baguio Mountain Lodges (ABML), an ultra-exclusive resort in Benguet province owned by the Ongpin family’s Alphaland Corp., reported that it has temporarily closed its premises amid landslides in the municipality of Itogon.

“As a precautionary measure to protect homeowners, visitors, employees, and contractors, ABML is closed to all homeowners and visitors until further notice. The restriction allows response teams to remove debris and assess affected areas without obstruction,” the company said in a statement on Tuesday, Sept. 1.

Alphaland said it recognizes that homeowners are concerned about their properties and may wish to inspect them, but given the continuing rainfall and unstable ground conditions, the closure will remain in effect until the property has been assessed and clearance has been given.
Homeowners have been advised separately and will be notified directly when access can resume.

ABML said it is working with the local government and neighboring communities in Itogon following one month of sustained rainfall that has triggered landslides and disrupted several areas of the municipality.
Benguet has been placed under a state of calamity as a result of the prolonged severe weather and its impact on communities and infrastructure across the province.

Landslides have affected properties and families in the barangays surrounding ABML and have also occurred within portions of the ABML property. Based on information available at this time, no casualties have been reported in the affected barangays or within ABML.
Alphaland is coordinating with local authorities to assist affected families in the surrounding communities and to support ongoing relief and safety efforts.

“Our neighbors in Itogon are going through a very difficult time, and we are doing what we can alongside the local government to help. Within our own property, we are taking no chances with anyone’s safety,” said Alphaland President Dennis O. Valdes.

Alphaland has engaged independent engineering specialists to evaluate the condition of roads, slopes, structures, and other infrastructure within ABML. Their findings will guide the stabilization, repair, and restoration work that follows and will determine when the property can safely reopen.
The firm added that it will continue to share verified information as it becomes available, covering community assistance, site conditions, access restrictions, and recovery progress.

“The company extends its concern to all families and communities affected by the prolonged rains and landslides, and stands ready to work alongside the local government and its neighbors throughout the response and recovery,” Valdes said. - James A. Loyola

articles.title: Thai resort prepares to host USS Abraham Lincoln sailors after more than 270 days at sea
articles.summary:
Security stepped up in Pattaya before arrival of thousands of sailors and marines, whose deployment was extended due to US war in Iran

Authorities in the Thai resort city of Pattaya have…
articles.byline: Guardian staff and agencies in Pattaya

blocks.text: Authorities in the Thai resort city of Pattaya have stepped up security as they prepare to welcome thousands of sailors and marines from the USS Abraham Lincoln after more than 270 consecutive days at sea.
“About 600 officials will provide security and other necessary assistance,” the provincial governor, Narit Niramaiwong, told AFP.
The nuclear-powered aircraft carrier sailed past Singapore over the weekend on its way back to the US after a lengthy deployment in the Middle East as part of the US war against Iran.
It left California in November 2025 for duty in the South China Sea and was rerouted to the Middle East before the US-Israeli attacks on Iran that began six months ago.
Reports of deteriorating living conditions and poor mental health on board, including attempted suicides, have made headlines in the US, provoking criticism of Donald Trump’s war against Iran.

Pattaya’s mayor, Poramase Ngampiches, said the carrier would dock just after midnight on Wednesday (about 5pm GMT on Tuesday) at Laem Chabang port. About 40 buses have been laid on to transport the sailors to Pattaya and back in staggered groups before the carrier departs on Sunday.

After meeting US officials on Monday, Poramase said that service members would be banned from certain recreational activities such as parasailing and marijuana use. Medical cannabis was legalised in Thailand in 2022 and dispensaries have become common in Thai cities.
Once a sleepy fishing village, Pattaya was transformed by the Vietnam war in the 1960s, when US soldiers on leave began coming for rest and recreation.
The city has since become hugely popular with foreign tourists, known for its beaches and a nightlife scene that has long drawn scrutiny over sex tourism.
Poramase told AFP there had been a recent crackdown on sex workers but denied this was linked to the US arrivals.

Government officials are warning local businesses not to overcharge US sailors, and there would be a greater police presence in popular areas along Pattaya Beach and the city’s Walking Street, Poramase said.

The city’s police chief, Anek Srathongyoo, said law enforcements agencies had been ordered to step up security measures to prevent undesirable situations. He said that if any US service members broke Thai law, they would be prosecuted accordingly.

Local business owners feeling the tourism slump from the Iran war are eager for the new arrivals. A banner hung over a local bar near a beach reading: “Welcome all US military personnel. Thank you for your service.”

Bualuang Ponok, a bar employee, said she had seen US service members during past visits, but she didn’t expect many of them would be spending. “They said 5,000 people will come here, but how many will reach us?” she said.
Earlier in August, the usually Asia-based USS George Washington relieved the long-deployed Lincoln in the Middle East.
The Lincoln, one of the US Navy’s largest warships, was part of American efforts in the Iran war, which flared back up over the weekend for the first time in a month.

This deployment included a record-setting uninterrupted time at sea of more than 250 days, which caused concerns after reports of deteriorating mental health among the crew and shortages of supplies including food and hygiene products.
Trump later downplayed these concerns and said that the deployment was “not nearly long enough”.
Thai officials have said the Lincoln will return to the US after its port call in Thailand.
Associated Press and Agence France-Press contributed reporting

articles.title: Lakeshore communities warned as Laguna de Bay water level rises
articles.summary: LUCENA CITY — The Laguna Lake Development Authority (LLDA) on Tuesday urged residents along the shores of Laguna de Bay to remain vigilant as the lake’s water level continued to rise above its…

blocks.text: LUCENA CITY — The Laguna Lake Development Authority (LLDA) on Tuesday urged residents along the shores of Laguna de Bay to remain vigilant as the lake’s water level continued to rise above its critical high-water mark amid persistent rains brought by the enhanced southwest monsoon and a low-pressure area (LPA).

“Due to persistent torrential rains brought by the southwest monsoon and a Low Pressure Area, the water level of Laguna de Bay has exceeded its critical high mark of 12.50 meters, reaching 12.67 meters,” the LLDA said in an advisory issued at 10:15 a.m.
The agency said the recorded 12.67-meter water level was at 10 a.m. The LLDA considers 10.50 meters as the lake’s critical low-water level and 12.50 meters as its critical high-water level.
According to the LLDA, Laguna de Bay reached the critical high-water level of 12.50 meters last week before rising further to 12.58 meters on Saturday, August 29.
“Residents living along the shores of Laguna de Bay are strongly advised to remain vigilant and closely monitor official public announcements,” the agency said.
The LLDA also urged lakeshore residents to prepare for possible flooding and strictly follow local evacuation protocols if heavy rainfall persists.

The agency noted that Laguna de Bay serves as a natural catch basin for water from watersheds in Laguna and Rizal provinces, as well as parts of Metro Manila. Rising lake levels therefore increase the risk of flooding in low-lying communities along its shores.

The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) said heavy rainfall was expected in parts of Luzon from Monday afternoon through Tuesday afternoon due to the southwest monsoon, which in turn was being enhanced by Tropical Storm Pilandok.
Meanwhile, the weather bureau monitored three other weather disturbances outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR).
The LLDA urged local governments and residents in vulnerable areas to remain prepared and closely monitor weather developments.
Authorities were also advised to keep drainage systems and tributary rivers leading to the lake free of obstruction to help minimize flood risks.

Located between Laguna province to the south and Rizal province to the north, Laguna de Bay is the Philippines’ largest lake and one of Southeast Asia’s largest freshwater lakes by surface area, covering approximately 911 to 949 square kilometers./coa

articles.title: 697 fugitives nabbed, as drugs, smuggled goods seized in Mimaropa
articles.summary: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — Police units across Mimaropa arrested 697 fugitives and seized about P45.7 million worth of illegal drugs and smuggled goods as the Police Regional Office in Mimaropa…

blocks.text: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — Police units across Mimaropa arrested 697 fugitives and seized about P45.7 million worth of illegal drugs and smuggled goods as the Police Regional Office in Mimaropa intensified its anti-criminality campaign from May 8 to Aug. 31.
The arrests included 204 Most Wanted Persons and 493 other wanted individuals, the MIMAROPA police said.

Police also conducted 139 anti-illegal drug operations that resulted in 157 arrests and the seizure of 680.82 grams of shabu, 80.53 grams of marijuana leaves, 5.4353 grams of marijuana kush, and 2,015.90 grams of cocaine. The drugs were estimated to be worth P15,330,062.12.
Meanwhile, 8 anti-smuggling operations resulted in the arrest of 22 suspects and the seizure of smuggled goods valued at about P30.4 million.
Combined, the two operations accounted for approximately P45.7 million worth of illegal drugs and smuggled goods seized during the period.

Mimaropa police also stepped up its campaign against loose firearms, conducting 171 operations and accounting for 177 firearms. Of these, 148 were voluntarily surrendered, 29 were confiscated, and one was captured.
Authorities turned over 89 firearms for safekeeping while two cases were filed in court, police said.

The campaign against illegal logging yielded 21,347 board feet of lumber and other forest products valued at about P1.47 million. Police conducted 46 operations, arrested 49 suspects, and filed 11 cases in court.
In its campaign against illegal gambling, PRO Mimaropa conducted 27 operations that led to the arrest of 97 people and the confiscation of cash and other items valued at P63,303.

“Our personnel have to remain focused on the ground. We have to act on information, go after those involved in criminal activities, and prevent these threats from reaching our communities,” said Police Brig. Gen. Dela Cruz, Mimaropa police regional director./coa

articles.title: OCD urges public to limit outdoor exposure as Indonesia haze reaches PH
articles.summary: The Office of Civil Defense (OCD) urged the public on Tuesday, Sept. 1, to limit outdoor exposure and take precautions as haze associated with forest fires in Indonesia continued to affect parts of…

blocks.text: The Office of Civil Defense (OCD) urged the public on Tuesday, Sept. 1, to limit outdoor exposure and take precautions as haze associated with forest fires in Indonesia continued to affect parts of the country.

OCD Deputy Administrator for Administration, Asst. Sec. Bernardo Rafaelito Alejandro IV said the agency was closely coordinating with the Department of Environment and Natural Resources-Environmental Management Bureau (DENR-EMB) to monitor the air quality situation in several areas, particularly the National Capital Region (NCR), Calabarzon (Region 4A), and Mimaropa (Region 4B).

“As observed, the haze is possibly associated with smoke and transboundary haze from the ongoing fires in Indonesia which may have been transported towards the Philippines by prevailing winds,” Alejandro said in a video message.
“So we are continuously monitoring the air quality, our EMB, through its network of air quality monitoring stations to assess the extent and potential impact of the haze,” he added.
Alejandro warned that exposure to haze could cause health problems, particularly among vulnerable individuals.

Persons sensitive to air pollution, including children, older persons and those with respiratory and cardiovascular conditions, were advised to limit their outdoor exposure and take necessary precautions.
“The haze may cause difficulty in breathing, coughing, chest pain, watery eyes, itchy nose, and worsening of respiratory diseases such as asthma,” he said.

“Wear a well-fitting mask, preferably N95 or equivalent, when going outdoors in areas with noticeable haze, and stay updated through official advisories issued by DENR and EMB, and your Office of Civil Defense together with the Department of Health,” he added.
He also urged residents to stay indoors as much as possible and close doors and windows. He advised the public to use a wet cloth to cover gaps where smoke or particles could enter their homes.
Those who need to travel were likewise reminded to exercise caution, particularly when visibility is reduced.
“Wear an N95 mask if you leave the house, and use headlights or foglights when traveling at night or in areas with poor visibility,” Alejandro said.

PAGASA earlier said the haze over parts of the country was linked to particles from forest fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia, which were being transported by the relatively strong southwest monsoon or “habagat.”

PAGASA said forest fires in Indonesia are a recurring phenomenon during strong El Niño events, citing similar episodes in 2015 as an example. Previous episodes also affected parts of the Visayas and Mindanao, where reduced visibility became a concern for airport operations.

articles.title: Inadequate cell service is 'jeopardizing people’s lives' in emergencies, N.L. woman says
articles.summary: First responders and residents across Newfoundland and Labrador say better cellular connectivity is needed for emergency situations.

image.caption: Amanda Howse still remembers being stranded on the road and being unable to call 911 because there was no cell service. (Submitted by Amanda Howse)

blocks.text: Nfld. & Labrador·New
First responders and residents across Newfoundland and Labrador say better cellular connectivity is needed for emergency situations.
Across the province people and first responders want to see connectivity improved
Even a decade removed from the event, Amanda Howse remembers Jan. 20, 2016 clearly.

After hitting a snow drift and veering off the road, she managed to pull herself out of her wrecked car — alone, hurt and stuck down the side of the highway near Charles Brook in central Newfoundland. She reached for her phone, ready to dial 911 but couldn’t. There was no cell service.
“It’s jeopardizing people's lives by not having adequate cell service across this province,” Howse told CBC News.

The issue of connectivity and access to emergency services was raised last week, after a fisherman died off Westport on the Baie Verte Peninsula. A firefighter in the community told CBC News connectivity issues are a problem in emergencies.
Howse received help when another driver saw tire marks lead off the embankment, and with the help of another resident's two-way radio, they were eventually able to contact emergency services.
She’s since been diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder from the experience. However, Howse considers herself to be one of the "lucky ones.”
Cellular coverage, or lack thereof, raises concerns about ability to reach emergency services in N.L.
Connectivity struggles feel like ‘déjà vu’
On the other end of the line, first responders say connectivity is a problem that needs to be solved.
“It seems like we're repeating ourselves, déjà vu, every couple of years,” said Deer Lake Fire Rescue fire chief Stephen Rowsell.
“I’ve talked to other chiefs around the province. They seem to have the same concerns,” he said.

More than a 600-kilometre drive from Deer Lake, in Marystown, Marystown Volunteer Fire Department fire chief Justin Bolt said there are some parts of his area where service is “inadequate” or not available at all.

Though Bolt’s department has purchased additional resources to try to stay connected —including three cell phone boosters — sometimes it’s not enough and his crew has to go to a nearby home to connect.
“It could be in another community where they [firefighters] have to actually go in and use a resident's phone in order to make that call,” said Bolt.
The fire chief hopes to see improvements in his community’s connectivity in the future.
“We're in an age of technology, but technology is not advancing to keep us connected. But all the tools are there,” Bolt said.
Work ongoing to 'close gaps'
In a statement to CBC News, Buckley Belanger, federal Secretary of State for Rural Development, said the federal government is “working to close gaps in mobile coverage in several ways.”

These include the Universal Broadband Fund, where up to $50 million is available to improve cell service in rural areas and along roads. The federal government has also asked provinces and territories to identify “shovel-ready” projects that could expand cell coverage.

items: PCs and NDP promise millions in funding during weekend election campaigns
Residents of C.B.N. say wildfires show need for improved rural cell coverage

blocks.text: The province's Department of Jobs, Growth and Rural Development said it’s looking to “identify potential partners and solutions to improve mobile connectivity throughout the province.”
The province also said it is continuing to advocate to both the federal government and telecommunications companies to increase coverage.
During last year’s election, the PCs promised it would spend an extra $3 million a year to increase cellular coverage in the province.

In a statement, telecommunications giant Bell spokesperson David Marcille said improving connectivity in rural and remote areas remains a “shared challenge,” that often requires collaboration between industry and governments, and that it “remains committed to working with partners to help address remaining coverage gaps.”

articles.title: Every fiesta has room for one more
articles.summary: When fiesta season arrives in Bacolod, celebrations extend beyond the streets and into homes. During fiesta season, families open their doors to relatives, neighbors, friends and visitors, with food…

blocks.text: Lifestyle | Food
Mountain Dew's 'Dew It sa Pista: Sugod-Fiesta Edition' follows a house-to-house celebration in Bacolod
When fiesta season arrives in Bacolod, celebrations extend beyond the streets and into homes.

During fiesta season, families open their doors to relatives, neighbors, friends and visitors, with food and drinks shared around the table. This tradition is the focus of Mountain Dew’s latest creator campaign, “Dew It sa Pista: Sugod-Fiesta Edition.”
Set during the Bacolod Chicken Inasal Festival, the campaign features food creator Ninong Ry alongside Nisa Nuggets, River Joseph and Dustin Yu, collectively known as the "Tropang Dewds."
Instead of following the usual festival route, the group visited Bacolod homes, where they shared home-cooked meals with Negrense families and heard the stories behind each handaan.

The meals included grilled inasal and other home-cooked dishes, with bottles of Mountain Dew served alongside the food. The campaign centers on the house-to-house aspect of the celebration and the role of food in bringing families, friends and neighbors together.

blocks.caption: (Photo: Mountain Dew)

blocks.text: (Photo: Mountain Dew)

“Iba talaga ang fiesta ng Pilipino. Diyan nagsasama-sama ang pamilya, tropa, at buong barangay sa isang handaan. Diyan nabubuo ang samahan! At siyempre, mas masarap ang kwentuhan at kainan kapag may ice-cold Mountain Dew na kasama,” said Ninong Ry.

The Bacolod Chicken Inasal Festival was first launched in 2018 and returned in 2023 after the pandemic. It has since grown into one of the city’s major celebrations, with cook-offs, performances and other street festivities alongside its focus on food and community.
For Mountain Dew PH Carbonated Soft Drink Lead Katrina Suarez, the campaign was inspired by the festival and the homes visited by the group.
“The energy of the Inasal Festival, the warmth of every home that opened its doors to us, and the meals shared around every table are what inspired this campaign,” Suarez said.
“DEW It sa Pista: Sugod-Fiesta Edition” is available on Mountain Dew Philippines’ official social media channels.

articles.title: Sara Duterte trial recap, Sept. 1: Military men, DepEd's P15.5-million confidential funds
articles.summary: The impeachment court on Tuesday, September 1, heard the testimonies of two military officials whose signatures are on documents the Department of Education, under then-Secretary Sara Duterte, used…

blocks.text: September 1, 2026 | 4:26pm

MANILA, Philippines — The impeachment court on Tuesday, September 1, heard the testimonies of two military officials whose signatures are on documents the Department of Education, under then-Secretary Sara Duterte, used to liquidate its confidential funds in 2023.

Duterte's trial entered its ninth week today with the prosecution's relatively brief presentation of witnesses Col. Manaros Boransing II and Col. Magtangol Panopio, as the defense chose not to cross-examine both military men.
Boransing and Panopio signed certifications that attested to the "successful" conduct of youth leadership summits and information campaigns that their Army units ran in 2023.

Tuesday's session is still on Article I, which accuses Duterte of misusing P612.5 million in confidential funds across the Office of the Vice President and DepEd; the P15.54 million tied to today's witnesses is one slice of that larger figure.
Here are the three highlights from today's proceedings:
1. DepEd didn't "release" funds to the Army, though used its summits as proof its confidential spending worked

Both Boransing and Panopio testified their units, the Army's 1st Infantry Division and 7th Infanty Division, respectively, received no funds from DepEd, the Office of the Vice President, or the Vice Presidential Security and Protection Group for their divisions' conduct of 2023 Youth Leadership Summits and information campaigns.

Sen. Bam Aquino got Boransing to confirm the Army's total operational spending across all eight summits, through a rough on-the-spot computation, likely stayed under P500,000, with local governments covering most youth participants' costs and other agencies shouldering their own expenses.

DepEd nonetheless submitted Boransing's certification to the Commission on Audit as what the agency called proof of success of an information-gathering or surveillance activity, one of its bases for P15.54 million in confidential funds it claimed went to rewards payments for informants.

Private prosecutor Reynaldo Robles, who led the prosecution's direct examination today, said the amount covered a large number of individual payments, roughly P100,000 to P200,000 each, some listed under names he described as unusual, and that the figure covered only the first two quarters of 2023.

The certificates signed by Boransing and Panopio, however, both make no mention of any amount. Under questioning from Presiding Officer Chiz Escudero, Boransing acknowledged the certificate did more than state the successful conduct of activities, as there was a sentence that the Army "successfully collaborated with the Department of Education," resulting in "zero reported [communist terrorist] recruitment." Boransing agreed that it amounted to a claim of success.

Sen. Joel Villanueva pressed the same point and argued that a certificate stating an activity was "successfully conducted" doesn't establish any link between a specific informant, the information that informant supplied, and a reward paid for it. Boransing said he had no opinion on how his certificate was used and is not qualified to weigh in, since he isn't an intelligence officer.

Boransing and Panopio both said they had only learned their certificates were submitted by DepEd to justify its confidential spending during the 2024 House good government committee hearings that sought to probe Duterte's use of secret funds.
2. DepEd's "confidential" information about student matters, which partly shaped where the Army held its summits

Boransing, under questioning from Escudero, said he could not characterize DepEd's inputs as confidential in nature. What DepEd provided, he said, was information on school schedules and permission to speak with students — details he distinguished from anything resembling intelligence work.

Later, under questioning from Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian, Boransing went further and said DepEd gave his division no confidential or surveillance information at all. What DepEd contributed, he said, was "open-source information," including which students showed leadership potential, and so could be pulled in to be participants in the leadership summits, and which schools made suitable venues.

Panopio, under questioning from Gatchalian, gave a similar account but with an added detail. He said his certification's claim that DepEd information had "enabled" the Army's civil-military and intelligence operations referred to input from teachers on the ground, not DepEd officials at higher levels. Asked what kind of information this was, Panopio said it covered matters happening in the community — including communism, terrorism, drug abuse and family issues — and that he could not say definitively whether any of it counted as confidential.

Pressed by Gatchalian to specify what, if anything, DepEd shared that he would call confidential, Panopio said: "Siguro po 'yung mga... I can speculate only... Maybe the personal circumstances like teenage pregnancies or other personal information na maging confidential because it is their personal life."
Panopio said this kind of community-level information factored into how the Army unit picked where to hold its summits and campaigns, depending on the "needs" of the communities.
3. No substantial stipulations

Before Panopio took the stand, the prosecution tried to speed up the trial by asking the defense to stipulate — agree without live testimony — that three more AFP officers (Panopio, Maj. Gen. Adonis Bahau, and Lt. Col. Carlos Sangdaan) would testify essentially the same as Boransing had.

Lead defense counsel Sheila Sison, however, refused to go that far, and the defense agreed only that the officers issued the certifications and that no confidential funds were transferred from DepEd to their units.

She would not stipulate that the officers were unaware their certifications would be used in DepEd's liquidation, arguing each certificate closes with the line "for whatever legal purpose it may serve" — language she said shows the officers signed knowing the documents could be put to legal use.

articles.title: Poa temporarily ‘steps aside’ as VP Sara’s defense spokesperson ahead of testimony
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense team said Atty. Michael Poa has temporarily stepped aside as the team’s spokesperson as he is expected to testify in the impeachment proceedings. “For the…

blocks.text: Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense team said Atty. Michael Poa has temporarily stepped aside as the team’s spokesperson as he is expected to testify in the impeachment proceedings.

“For the defense team, it is only proper that Atty. Poa, na isasalang sa (who will be presented to the) impeachment court, common etiquette and proper decorum dictate that we respect the impeachment court and he needs to, at the moment, step aside from serving as the Defense Team Spokesperson. Kaya ako, bilang deputy lang muna (That is why, for now, I will act only as deputy),” Defense team deputy spokesperson Atty. Justin Nicol Gular said in a press briefing on Tuesday, September 1.
Gular said the move was made to respect the impeachment court and preserve the integrity of the proceedings, noting that Poa is “on deck” to be presented as a witness by the prosecution.

“He is on deck. He will possibly be the witness. Out of respect of the impeachment proceeding and to ensure the integrity of the proceedings, we, Atty. Poa, saw it fit that hindi muna siyang magsasalita for the defense (deemed it appropriate for him not to speak for the defense for the meantime),” Gular said.
Gular said the defense team is currently considering who will take over the role permanently.
“The new spokesperson is still being considered and being talked about between the defense team and the client, the Vice President,” he said.
Gular added that once a decision is made, either Poa or Duterte herself will inform the media and the public.
Defense team observes sub judice rule

Gular also said the defense team has relayed to Duterte the impeachment court’s directives regarding the sub judice rule, which limits public statements that could affect matters under consideration in the proceedings.

“Yes, I would assume. This was mentioned by the Presiding Officer, and the defense team listens to the directives, suggestions of the impeachment court because we really respect the process,” Gular said.
He said Duterte was also expected to comply with the court’s directives.
“I think in one of the statements of Atty. Poa, she [Duterte] said she will try her best, of course, to comply with the directives of the impeachment court,” he said.
Gular stressed that the defense team, including Duterte, respects the sub judice rule and has been careful to comply with Rule 18 of the Senate Rules on Impeachment.
“I don’t want to engage in speculation. I also cannot speak for the Vice President herself, that’s her own decision,” he said.

“But again, the defense team, including the Vice President, respects the ruling on the sub judice issue and, as you have seen, we have been very conscious in complying with that section, the Rule 18, of the Senate rules on impeachment,” he added.

According to Gular, statements concerning evidence presented during the trial—including those that characterize, describe, or assess the weight of evidence—fall under the restrictions of the sub judice rule.
Public can form its own views
Gular acknowledged that the public may interpret what happens during the impeachment trial since the proceedings are open to the public.

“The public is entitled to interpret what happened to the trial. Available ito sa (This is available to the) public and everyone, including the senator-judges, is entitled to interpret or consider that statement of the witness,” he said.
Defense says it is not trying to make proceedings ‘boring’
Gular also addressed comments from some members of the public who may find portions of the impeachment proceedings less engaging.

“I think the defense has to be clarified that we’re just doing our jobs and whatever the proceedings bring on a certain day, ginagawa lang po namin ang kailangan naming gawin (we’re just doing what we need to do),” Gular said.
He also rejected the idea that the defense deliberately tries to make the proceedings either dull or dramatic.
“It has never been our strategy to make the impeachment, you know, boring or, on the other hand, theatrical,” he said.
“We’re not thinking, for today, gawin nating (let’s make it) boring, bukas dapat gawin nating masaya (tomorrow, let’s make it happy). Wala pong ganoon,” he added.
Gular said he understood the public’s desire to remain engaged, particularly because the impeachment case involves a sitting vice president.
“I understand the sentiment coming from the public. Of course, the public, as much as possible, would want to have their attention on this proceeding as this is important,” he said.
But he urged the public to be patient and allow the impeachment process to take its course.

“Just be patient. Ganito talaga yung proseso (This is really how the process works). Minsan may mga araw na for others, gagamitin ko lang yung quote mo, ‘boring,’ minsan mainit (Sometimes there are days that, for others, I’ll just use your quote, ‘boring,’ sometimes it’s heated). This is part of a proceeding,” Gular said.
Poa no longer in defense holding room
Gular also clarified that Poa is no longer staying in the defense holding room because he may be called as a witness.

“Atty. Poa is no longer, as of the moment, as for now, considering that he will be presented as a witness, actually staying in the defense holding room. He is staying in the holding room for the subpoenaed witnesses,” he said.
Gular said he last spoke with Poa the previous week and has not communicated with him since.
Asked whether the defense would cross-examine Poa if he takes the witness stand, Gular said the matter would depend on how the proceedings unfold.
“Antayin na lang natin (Let’s wait for it). Remember, it’s the prosecution who will be presenting him,” he said.
Public urged to observe proceedings
Gular ultimately appealed to the public to continue following the impeachment trial while allowing the proceedings to unfold according to established rules.

“To the public, given that this is an important constitutional proceeding, especially for the Vice President who is the accused, let’s just stay patient. Let’s listen and just observe the proceedings and understand as much as we can,” he said.
He also encouraged the public to listen to legal experts who are not bound by sub judice restrictions and to use their analysis when forming their own opinions.

articles.title: Bregente leads charge: Team PH trails by 2
articles.summary: Team Philippines put itself in championship mix of the 31st Nomura Cup, as Rolando Bregente and Jet Hernandez combined for a two-under-par 142 aggregate to be tied with powerhouse Japan, just two…

blocks.text: Team Philippines put itself in championship mix of the 31st Nomura Cup, as Rolando Bregente and Jet Hernandez combined for a two-under-par 142 aggregate to be tied with powerhouse Japan, just two shots behind surprise first round leader Hong Kong China at Bayhood No. 9 Golf Club in Beijing, China.

Having the reputation to start out fast and shoot low, Bregente gunned down four birdies in shooting a three-under-par 69 and was left to rue Hernandez' struggles on the greens on the way to a respectable 73, even as Shin Suzuki failed to count after firing a 75 as the Filipinos moved ahead of the leaderboard against traditional powers China, Australia, Thailand and defending champion Vietnam.

"This only confirms the thoughts of the team that we really have a solid shot at winning this," the 24-year-old Bregente said in Filipino. His only bogey came on the 16th, when he three-putted from about 25 feet. "The greens are the main defense of the course, and I saw Jet (Hernandez) struggle with his putting."

Jeffrey Shen and Markus Zachary Lam returned 70s to comprise scoring for HK-China, while Taisei Nagasaki and Mao Matsuyama fired 71s to make up the Japanese score as they threw away the 73 of Kaito Sato. Ethan Tian's 73 for HK-China also did not count.

"Yeah, I had a rough putting day," Hernandez, the National Strokeplay chapmpion back home, said. "I thought I committed and visualized really well and was starting (my putts) on line and rolling really good. Bit they just didn't drop today."
He remained confident that things will be better from the second round onwards, especially after playing the course with all the pressure.
"Am not too worried about it, though," the incoming psychology senior at University of Denver added. "They'll eventually drop."
The Philippines, which helped start this event together with Japan and Chinese Taipei in 1963, has not won the Nomura Cup. It has two second place finishes.
But this team looks to be the best prepared trio that the country has sent in years.

"He was in the flight behind me and I basically saw his entire round," Bregente went on. "He was hitting it dead straight on the fairways but just wasn't able to hole putts. But I know that he will bounce back."
China is three shots behind the joint second placers at 145 after getting a 72 from Jing Guo Chi and a 73 from Hao Yi wang, to tie the Vietnamese, who won this event in upset style at home in 2024.
Tuan Anh Nguyen fired a 72 and Huy Anh Ho accounted for a 73, Thailand is another shot back with New Zealand seven strokes off the pace.

articles.title: 90-day license suspension for drivers in Marikina road rage
articles.summary: The Land Transportation Office (LTO) suspended the licenses of two drivers for 90 days after a road rage incident in Marikina City. According to the LTO, the incident involved a jeepney and a private…

blocks.text: A jeepney and private vehicle involved in a road rage incident along A. Bonifacio Road in Marikina City. (Screengrab from Stan D Cruz/Facebook)

blocks.caption: A jeepney and private vehicle involved in a road rage incident along A. Bonifacio Road in Marikina City. (Screengrab from Stan D Cruz/Facebook)

blocks.text: The Land Transportation Office (LTO) suspended the licenses of two drivers for 90 days after a road rage incident in Marikina City.
According to the LTO, the incident involved a jeepney and a private vehicle traveling along A. Bonifacio Road toward C-5.

A video circulating on social media showed the two vehicles traveling close to each other before the drivers and some passengers got out and got involved in a physical confrontation in the middle of the road.
Following the incident, the LTO issued show cause orders to the registered owners and drivers of both vehicles.
They were ordered to appear before the agency’s Intelligence and Investigation Division and submit sworn explanations.
The LTO said possible violations include reckless driving, obstruction of traffic, and being an improper person to operate a motor vehicle.
The drivers were also ordered to surrender their licenses, while the two vehicles were placed under alarm status pending the investigation.
LTO Chief Assistant Secretary Markus Lacanilao said violence and disorder on the road will not be tolerated, adding that those involved may face appropriate sanctions.

“Hindi lisensya ang galit para bumaba ng sasakyan at makipagsagutan o makipagsuntukan sa gitna ng kalsada, lalo na kung nalalagay sa panganib ang ibang motorista. Ang mga sangkot sa insidenteng ito ay haharap sa kaukulang pananagutan (Anger is not a license to get out of a vehicle and engage in an argument or a fistfight in the middle of the road, especially when other motorists are put at risk. Those involved in this incident will be held accountable),” Lacanilao added.

blocks.text: Jericho Rosales as Manuel Quezon (TBA Studios)
To mark another year of recognizing the best of Philippine Cinema, the Manunuri ng Pelikulang Pilipino has released this year's nominees for the 49th Gawad Urian Awards.
Jerrold Tarog's last installment in his bayaniverse series of films, "Quezon," leads this year's nominees with 10 nods, including Best Film, Best Director, and Best Actor.
Meanwhile, newbie Krystel Go ("I’mPerfect") competes for the Best Actress plum against Odette Khan ("Bar Boys: After School") and Maris Racal ("Sunshine").

articles.title: Burnham to say he wants to unlock ‘positivity’ in first statement to MPs since becoming PM – UK politics live
articles.summary:
Prime minister will bring upbeat message to adversarial Commons after a summer of policy announcements and improved poll ratings

Good morning. Andy Burnham became prime…

blocks.text: Burnham to say he wants to unlock ‘positivity’ in first statement to MPs since becoming PM

Good morning. Andy Burnham became prime minister six weeks ago, but today will be the first time he addresses MPs in the Commons. It will also be the first time he has spoken as a minister from the dispatch box in more than 16 years. As MPs return to Westminster, they will be telling each other about how they spent the summer holiday and, for Burnham, it has undoubtedly gone well. He has unveiled a blitz of announcements which, broadly, have had a good reception and he has delivered the kiss of life to Labour’s poll ratings.

Today Burnham will chair cabinet in the morning and then make a ministerial statement in the Commons after 3.30pm. Normally a prime ministerial statement has a specific focus; it will be about a major policy decision, or a foreign affairs crisis. From the briefing that we have had so far, it sounds as if Burnham’s will be more of a wide-ranging rehash of all the things that he has been talking about this summer. In her preview, Jessica Elgot says he will talk about his intention to bring more essential services back into public control.
According to the BBC’s preview, Burnham will say he wants to “unlock a feeling of positivity and possibility” in every part of the country.

For the past six weeks, Burnham’s tone has been relentlessly positive. He repeatedly says he wants to focus on “problem-solving, not point-scoring”, and he clearly means it. Labour MPs chose Burnham as leader because they thought Keir Starmer would not be able to stop Nigel Farage becoming PM, but over the summer Burnham has said very little in public critical about Farage, or Reform UK, or the Tories. He views partisan mud-slinging as part of the old politics that he would like to reject.

But can he do that when he has to perform politics in the House of Commons? It sounds as if Burnham will not have much new to announce in his statement and so journalists will probably focus instead on what Labour and opposition MPs say to him, and how he responds. Burnham may not approve of “point-scoring”, but in the Commons, tradition, culture and even the architecture (front benches supposedly two swords’ length apart) prioritise conflict and it will interesting to see if he can get through the afternoon without resorting to the usual aggressive ding-dong. This will be an even bigger challenge for him at PMQs tomorrow.

And even if Burnham can remain upbeat for two hours in the Commons chamber, he will soon find that there are some places in the country particularly resistant to “positivity” – like the newsrooms at the Mail and GB News.
Still, it is probably worth a try. Here is the agenda for the day.
9.30am: Andy Burnham chairs cabinet.
Noon: Downing Street holds a lobby briefing.
2.30pm: Nigel Farage, the Reform UK leader, takes his seat as an MP after winning the Clacton byelection during the summer recess.
2.30pm: Ed Miliband, the foreign secretary, takes questions in the Commons.
After 3.30pm: Burnham gives a statement to MPs.
Late afternoon: Alex Norris, the justice secretary, gives a statement to MPs about changes to the prisoner early release scheme.

I’m afraid we are no longer able to have comments open below the line every day on this blog. If you want to contact me, please email politics.live@theguardian.com. You can use this email to flag up corrections, comments for publication, questions or complaints.

items: nowSmall boat crossings during summer months have fallen to seven-year low, Home Office says
