articles.title: How young Cameroonians end up fighting in Russia’s war
articles.summary: Cameroon has emerged as one of the leading sources of African recruits for the Russian military, with young men lured to Europe by false promises of jobs and fast-tracked Russian citizenship, only to…

blocks.text: Cameroon has emerged as one of the leading sources of African recruits for the Russian military, with young men lured to Europe by false promises of jobs and fast-tracked Russian citizenship, only to find themselves on the front lines of the war in Ukraine.

As of May this year, Ukrainian officials say that nearly 3,000 citizens from various African countries were known to have fought — or to still be fighting — for Russia : Cameroon, Ghana, Egypt, Kenya and Uganda were identified as significant.
In April, the Cameroonian government confirmed that Russia had reported the deaths of 16 Cameroonian nationals, seven of whom had died in military action in Ukraine.

blocks.caption: Charles Ojiambo Mutoka, 72, shows a picture of his son Oscar, who he learned was killed while fighting for Russia in Ukraine Image: Tony Karumba/AFP

blocks.text: Poverty driving youths into Russia’s duplicitous schemes
The actual death toll is likely higher according to DW correspondent Dorcas Ekupe, reporting from Bamenda in northwestern Cameroon.

“When you look at other publications and see what is happening — even seeing families who are grieving their loved ones — the number is really much higher than what the government had earlier said,” Ekupe told DW’s AfricaLink program.
She described two forces causing this worrying phenomenon: economic desperation and deliberate deception.
Many recruits, she said, travelled to Russia believing they had secured jobs in construction or as security guards, or that they were participating in study programs.
“Once in Russia, they then end up on the battlefield,” Ekupe said.
Russia’s perceived appeal meanwhile is also being amplified by well-organized campaigns.

Banjo Herman, a lecturer and political analyst at the University of Bamenda, pointed to the key role of the the Russian paramilitary Wagner Group as well as its successor, the Africa Corps, as Moscow’s primary instrument for expanding its presence and reputation across Africa.
Military recruitment dressed up as ‘cultural’ outreach

Herman also cited Russian government programs such as the African Initiative and Alabuga, which present themselves as cultural or educational exchange schemes but have been linked to military recruitment.

“On the surface, sometimes it looks like cultural outreach,” he said. “Sometimes Cameroonians are lured, thinking it is for work, not necessarily knowing what is beneath the surfac.,” He added that offers of Russian nationality within six months were a particularly powerful draw.
France has previously described the African Initiative as a front administered by Russian intelligence services, designed to spread propaganda.
Why young men continue to risk their lives
Herman stressed, however, that the economic situation of the men was typically the main motivator.

“Imagine that you are a carpenter in Cameroon who cannot even earn 100,000 CFA francs (€150; $175) a month, but somebody is promising you 3 million CFA francs to come and work,” he explained. “It is very attractive.”

He also highlighted the fact that not all Cameroonians in Russia were the victims of deception: Some had lived there for years, had been absorbed into the military over time and were doing reasonably well.

But he pointed out that it was the promise of financial reward combined with the prospect of gaining Russian citizenship that explained why even people aware of the risks continued to accept recruitment offers to fight in Ukraine.
Ekupe corroborated this, noting a prevailing attitude of fatalism among some youth: “Sometimes people say, ‘If I die, I die.'”
Those left behind often suffer the most

Families left behind, meanwhile, are forced to bear the cost in silence: Ekupe described cases in which mothers only learned of their sons’ deaths years after the fact — in one instance, when a fellow soldier called home to report that a 35-year-old Cameroonian had been killed in combat.
She added that many families had received no financial compensation from the Cameroonian government and that some of the men who died had left behind pregnant wives as well as children.
Contact between recruits and their families is often severed abruptly, Ekupe said.

“When they get there and discover it was not as promised, it is really difficult to inform their family,” she added. “Sometimes they have to take time to adjust to the new environment and the situation, in which they find themselves.”

blocks.caption: According to the Kenyan Ministry of Foreign Affairs, more than 200 Kenyan nationals had crossed into Russia by January 2026, but only 18 had returned Image: Minako Sasako/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Russia ducking from responsibilty
On the question of legal responsibility, Herman noted that international law does not, in principle, prohibit a foreign national from voluntarily enlisting in another state’s armed forces.
Legal liability arises, however, when recruitment involves fraud, coercion, trafficking or mercenary activity.

Herman cited Article 47 of the Additional Protocol to the Geneva Conventions, which defines a mercenary as someone who agrees to take direct part in hostilities with private financial gain as their main motivation.
Under current frameworks, the responsibility for the death of a foreign fighter in another country’s war rests largely with the individual and their family, not the recruiting state.
Cameroon: insufficient campaigns to fight recruitement
Cameroon’s government has stated publicly that it does not deploy troops abroad outside international mandates, and has warned citizens against joining foreign conflicts.
Analysts have nevertheless called on the Cameroonian government, and African governments more broadly, to pursue a three-pronged response to stop more people from risking their lives in Russia.

This approach would include economic reforms to create opportunities and reduce the conditions that make deceptive recruitment attractive; direct diplomatic engagement with Russia to hold recruitment networks accountable; and a public awareness campaign that issues clear, proactive public warnings to citizens about the dangers of following such schemes.

blocks.caption: Relatives of Kenyan nationals conscripted by the Russian army have demanded government action to repatriate their kin Image: Tony Karumba/AFP

blocks.text: Ghana has also formally raised the issue with Russia, demanding an end to the recruitment of its nationals.
However, in Cameroon’s case, the country’s longstanding military ties with Russia, which President Paul Biya moved to renew in 2014 and 2015, could prevent a similar move.

Herman said that the absence of an official Cameroonian policy response to date reflected, at least in part, the government’s awareness that the recruitment is carried out by private actors — limiting the state’s formal grounds and opportunities for intervention.

“For the government to stop this,” he said, “it has to go back to its governance policy and have a policy that is inclusive, transparent, and in which people can find opportunities within the system.” /dl

articles.title: China-Nepal flood toll tops 1,000 as tunnel rescue offers last hope
articles.summary: NUWAKOT, Nepal — The death toll from devastating Himalayan glacial floods crossed the grim 1,000 mark on Tuesday, as Chinese and Nepali teams searched for survivors including dozens feared…

blocks.text: NUWAKOT, Nepal — The death toll from devastating Himalayan glacial floods crossed the grim 1,000 mark on Tuesday, as Chinese and Nepali teams searched for survivors including dozens feared trapped in hydropower tunnels.

Nearly 4,500 people are missing after the gigantic wave of freezing water, rocks and debris from a high-altitude glacial collapse roared downstream on Wednesday, wiping out entire settlements and gouging a path of destruction through Nepal.
Nepali rescue teams are digging, drilling and blasting through debris in a race against time in treacherous conditions to free around 100 hydropower workers believed trapped in multiple tunnels.
So far, only corpses have been pulled out of tunnels blocked with sludge.
“We are focused on search and rescue efforts at the tunnels, our work is continuing,” Raja Ram Basnet, Nepal Army spokesman, told AFP on Tuesday.
“Our soldiers are also deployed to collect bodies and prevent the spread of disease.”

With mortuaries overflowing in Nepal, the authorities have begun burying hundreds of unidentified bodies after DNA sampling. At least 17 bodies have also been pulled from rivers far downstream in India.
Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah has called the catastrophe “unimaginable and heartbreaking”.
‘Find their bodies’
In the capital Kathmandu, crowds lined up to search for their missing relatives, posting photographs on a long wall outside a hospital, in the fading hope of finding them alive.

Debu Sapkota, a 58-year-old driver, came to post photos of his 83-year-old mother-in-law and granddaughter who went missing in the town of Trishuli Bazaar, after being swept away by last week’s surge.
A warning alert sounded, but the elderly woman was “too old to run”, he recounts.
“Her granddaughter was helping her escape but both were swept away.”
Sapkota says he no longer has “any hope that they survived”, after witnesses saw them being carried away by the torrent.
“I am here hoping to find their bodies,” he said, holding up photos of the two missing women dressed in traditional clothes.
In Chitwan district, mourning relatives cremated some of the dead.
Soldiers were seen unloading bodies of victims from helicopters in Nepal’s Nuwakot and Rasuwa districts.
Aid needs are enormous. Entire communities have been swept away, leaving families homeless and using makeshift shelters as heavy rain lashes down.
Roads and dozens of bridges have been smashed, and power plants destroyed.
“There are too many challenges,” said police officer E. Hawadi in badly affected Nuwakot district.
‘Climate change’

In Nuwakot, AFP photographers on Tuesday saw people scouring through mud into the rubble of their homes for usable items, some clearing away dirt and stringing up plastic sheeting for shelter in the ruins.
Foreigners missing among the list include 583 in Nepal and 261 in China, coming more than 30 nations.
They include tourists who had come for trekking in the apparently serene Himalayas, as well as Hindu pilgrims seeking spiritual peace at Tibet’s sacred Mount Kailash.

There is growing anger at the scale of destruction to hit Nepal, a largely rural nation of 30 million people — that has contributed little to the emissions driving global warming churned out by wealthy and industrialised nations, but is suffering its consequences.

“It is now time for us to strongly raise with the international community the issue of the disasters we are experiencing as a result of climate change,” Shah, Nepal’s prime minister, said in a statement late Monday.
Scientists say the Himalayas, the world’s highest mountain range, are melting faster as global temperatures rise.

blocks.caption: This screen grab from a handout video footage released by Nepal’s Prime Minister Secretariat on August 31, 2026 via AFPTV shows Nepali soldiers conducting an operation inside a tunnel to rescue workers after flash floods at Rasuwagadhi Hydropower Project site in Rasuwa district. Agence France-Presse

blocks.text: Nepal’s economy is already under pressure, with limited resources to respond to a disaster of this scale, with Kathmandu warning reconstruction costs could run into the “billions of dollars”.
‘Mourn the victims’
Nepal said 987 bodies had been recovered, and listed 3,916 as missing.
China’s state media reports 16 dead, and 546 people missing.
That takes the overall number of dead to 1,003, and missing to 4,462.
In China, Tibet is largely inaccessible to foreign journalists, and Chinese authorities are the only source of official information.
Emergency workers, officials and residents in Tibet held memorial services on Tuesday.
“Rescuers, local officials and residents stood in silence to mourn the victims,” China’s official news agency Xinhua said.
More than 2,000 people are aiding rescue operations, including soldiers, Xinhua added.
It said on Tuesday that teams were “working around the clock to search for survivors, repair roads, set up communication base stations and restore power lines.”
But Tibetan advocacy groups in exile have questioned China’s account of the disaster.
Tencho Gyatso, president of the International Campaign for Tibet, called for China to disclose “complete and verifiable information about the damage and casualties”.
Beijing’s foreign ministry said Monday that the “release of information has been open, transparent and timely”, and rejected international reports that it was underreporting deaths. /dl

articles.title: After Nepal disaster, Cebu City watches Lusaran River, flood-prone areas
articles.summary: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Following the deadly flash floods in Nepal, disaster officials here are keeping a close watch on the Lusaran River and other flood-prone areas. Councilor Dave Tumulak, head…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Following the deadly flash floods in Nepal, disaster officials here are keeping a close watch on the Lusaran River and other flood-prone areas.

Councilor Dave Tumulak, head of the Cebu City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (CCDRRMC), said on Tuesday that authorities continue to remind communities living near waterways to move to safer areas, particularly when heavy rainfall threatens to swell rivers.
Lusaran River shows risk
Tumulak identified the Lusaran River as a key area of concern.
He said the risk becomes particularly serious during heavy downpours, citing the flooding that struck Cebu City during Typhoon Tino in November 2025.
“Kining Lusaran [River] mao ni delikado, kay same atong nahitabo sa [bagyong] Tino nga heavy downpour nga nag flash flood gyud sila didto,” he said.
(The Lusaran River is particularly dangerous because it could mirror what happened during Tropical Storm Tino, where heavy rainfall triggered severe flash floods in the area.)
Tumulak said the situation along the river has since changed, with residents reportedly leaving riverbanks after experiencing the devastation caused by the storm.

“Ang Lusaran, katong pagkatapusan sa Tino, nahawan na man gyud tong sapa. Wala na gyud nagpuyo kay na-trauma na gyod ang mga tawo,” he said. (In Lusaran, by the end of Tino, the river channel had already cleared. No one was living there anymore because the people had been traumatized by what happened.)
Still, Tumulak said the CCDRRMC would continue monitoring the area, with a possible inspection planned this week.
Clearing efforts
Meanwhile, the disaster head said the city continues its information campaign and clearing efforts involving the legally required 3-meter easement along waterways.
“Ongoing na atong information dissemination sa clearing sa 3-meter easement,” he said. (Our information dissemination on the clearing of the 3-meter easement is ongoing.)

Tumulak said the city has also begun compiling a list of families who could need relocation as authorities clear areas along waterways. The city plans to relocate affected families to safer locations rather than leave them exposed to flooding along rivers and waterways.
The concern over Lusaran comes from its experience with Tino, which brought extreme rainfall to Cebu City on November 3 to 4, 2025.
Tino dumped 183 millimeters of rain on Cebu City within 24 hours, exceeding the city’s normal November rainfall average of 131 millimeters.
The resulting overflow of the Lusaran River triggered powerful flash floods in Barangay Lusaran and nearby communities.

articles.title: Cone on Gilas Asiad team: ‘They will be a lot of fun to watch’
articles.summary: Gilas Pilipinas head coach Tim Cone is optimistic on how the Asian Games team would fare against some of the continent’s powerhouses, noting that the crew led by Adrian Nocum and Robert Bolick should…

blocks.text: Gilas Pilipinas head coach Tim Cone is optimistic on how the Asian Games team would fare against some of the continent’s powerhouses, noting that the crew led by Adrian Nocum and Robert Bolick should be a lot of fun to watch in the Nagoya edition of the quadrennial meet.

The veteran mentor revealed that the Asiad-bound team won’t be using the same triangle offense he has with the Gilas FIBA team and instead will be using an up tempo and fast-paced system that would fit the team’s current all-PBA composition.

“From what I've seen from that team, they are a lot of fun to watch. I think the fans and our countrymen, I think they’ll have a lot of fun watching that team,” said Cone as he turned his focus to the country’s title-retention bid in Asian Games following a successful home stand in the 2027 FIBA World Cup Asian Qualifiers.

“It’s a different system, they are not playing my system. It’s more of an up tempo push the ball (style). They’ll be using their speed and quickness to get up and down the floor,” added the veteran mentor.

Although focused on the preparations of Gilas FIBA window squad, Cone had a glimpse of the quality of the Asiad-bound team, having played against them in two tuneup games — even beating – the Sotto-led Gilas in their first meeting.
The Gilas Asiad crew has been training for two weeks now with Gilas lead deputy Richard del Rosario along with fellow assistants Jong Uichico and Josh Reyes facilitating the training.

“It’s gonna be a pretty much different group of players playing this time. You come up with these windows like this, you are really exhausted with all the preparations you had to do and you got to turn around and get to the Asian Games,” said Cone, recalling the same dilemma the Gilas team under Chot Reyes had in the past.

“I remember the Chot’s team when they went to the World Cup, they played fabulous in the World cup in Spain and then they had to fly all the way to Korea and play the Asian Games and they just didn't have the energy to play after that grueling World Cup that they had,” he recalled.
“So the idea of bringing fresher guys motivated guys to come out and play and play for their country I think it’s a good idea,” he added.

Aside from Nocum and Bolick, who are expected to anchor the attack for Gilas, Sedrick Barefield is also part of the team alongside Don Trollano, Jerrick Ahanmisi, Brandon Ganuelas-Rosser, Brandon Bates, Sean Quitevis, Geo Chiu, and Zav Lucero.
RJ Abarrientos, Justin Arana and Justine Baltazar are also joining the crew.
Gilas is scheduled to fly to Korea for a short training camp before flying to Nagoya for their group stage games against Kazakhstan, Bahrain and China.

articles.title: House panel OKs sharply reduced 2027 budget for Marcos office
articles.summary: The Office of the President's proposed budget for 2027 got the House Committte on Appropriations approval within 25 minutes.

blocks.text: September 1, 2026 | 3:26pm

This screenshot shows Executive Secretary Ralph Recto before the Committee on Appropriations in the House of Representatives on September 1, 2026, while defending the 2027 proposed budget of Office of the President.
Screenshot from HREP

MANILA, Philippines — The Office of the President’s proposed budget for 2027 worth more than P10.15 billion passed the deliberations of the Committee on Appropriations in the House of Representatives on Tuesday, September 1.

With 37 affirmative votes and five negative votes, the committee approved the P10,155,758,000 proposed budget within the first 25 minutes of the deliberations after lawmakers extended “institutional and interbranch courtesy” to the Office of the President.

According to Executive Secretary Ralph Recto, who attended the hearing with other officials from the Office of the President, the proposed budget represents only 0.14% of the P7.2 trillion total budget proposal for 2027.
Recto added that it is also 64% lower than the 2026 budget.
Based on the publicly available General Appropriations Act of 2026 uploaded on the website of the Department of Budget and Management (DBM), the Office of the President was allocated P28,028,733,000.

Recto said the decrease in the proposed budget reflects the lower operating costs of the Office of the President’s delivery units and the completion of activities related to the ASEAN Summit, which the country hosted.
“In short, we are asking for less, while remaining fully prepared to do more,” Recto said.

After Recto’s presentation, House Minority Leader Marcelino Libanan (4Ps Party-list) made the motion to extend interparliamentary courtesy to the Office of the President and terminate further deliberations and discussions of the sought budget.
The motion was seconded by House Senior Deputy Speaker Ferdinand Hernandez (South Cotabato).

Rep. Antonio Tinio (ACT Teachers Party-list), however, objected and argued that Congress should also demand transparency from the Office of the President, the same way that it demanded the Office of the Vice President to be transparent about its budget.
“Lakas maka-demand ng kongresong ito ng transparency para sa Office of the Vice President.

Dapat ganoon din para sa Office of the President,” Tinio said, citing alleged involvement of some Cabinet officials in flood control corruption. “Kailangang magpaliwanag ang Office of the President kung bakit halos kalahati ng kanyang budget ay confidential and intelligence funds.”

(This Congress demanded transparency from the Office of the Vice President. The same should apply to the Office of the President. The Office of the President needs to explain why almost half of its budget goes to confidential and intelligence funds.)
In their manifestations, some lawmakers explained their negative votes and cited the need for transparency and accountability as reasons to oppose the “parliamentary courtesy.”
Among those who opposed were Tinio, Rep. Renee Co (Kabataan Party-list), Rep. Sarah Elago (Gabriela Party-list), Rep. Eli San Fernando (KAMANGGAGAWA Party-list) and Rep. Iris Montes (4K Party-list).

articles.title: OCD seeks more resources as flooding hits areas not previously prone to inundation
articles.summary: The Office of Civil Defense (OCD) on Tuesday, Sept. 1, sought to augment disaster response resources in Central Luzon (Region 3) as prolonged rains due to the impact of enhanced southwest monsoon…

blocks.text: The Office of Civil Defense (OCD) on Tuesday, Sept. 1, sought to augment disaster response resources in Central Luzon (Region 3) as prolonged rains due to the impact of enhanced southwest monsoon (habagat) continue to inundate areas that were previously not known to experience flooding.

Office of Civil Defense (OCD) Deputy Administrator for Administration, Assistant Secretary Rafaelito Bernardo Alejandro IV said Pampanga, in particular, needs additional rescue boats and personnel as some municipalities face flooding despite not being traditionally flood-prone.

“We have to ramp up the issuance of early warnings because in Pampanga alone, the feedback to us is that there are municipalities that were not previously flooded, now experiencing [flood],” Alejandro said.

“We have to increase our manpower and our resources to address this flooding. What Pampanga needs now are additional rubber boats, watercraft, and additional personnel from the Armed Forces to relieve their local resources,” he added.

Pampanga Governor Lilia Pineda earlier identified areas in the more elevated “Upper Pampanga,” including San Fernando City, Angeles City, Floridablanca, and Porac, that were not previously prone to severe flooding but are now inundated.
The OCD said the country has been dealing with the effects of habagat for about a month already. As of Tuesday morning, 178 local government units had declared a state of calamity.

The latest OCD data on the combined effects of habagat and previous tropical cyclones Luis, Maymay, and Neneng showed that about 2.6 million families or 9.1 million people were affected in 6,175 barangays across 10 regions.
There were 1,255 evacuation centers operating, housing 39,386 families or 135,905 individuals.
NLEX traffic; death toll at 34
The disaster has also left 34 people dead, 19 injured, and three missing. Alejandro said two deaths were added to the toll, one in the National Capital Region and another in Pangasinan.
On top of this, the OCD was also validating 14 reported casualties from Zambales, Subic, Tarlac, Pampanga and Olongapo during the second round of habagat’s impacts.
Massive flooding has disrupted major roads and damaged bridges, prompting government agencies and the military to assist local authorities and infrastructure operators.

On the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX), a portion in San Simon, Pampanga remains limited to one lane. Alejandro said the OCD has been assisting NLEX management while the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) and Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) personnel were also providing support for mitigation work.

“We are coordinating with NLEX management to address the lack of resources and with the LGU to provide assistance and relief, not only to those on the highway but also to their families who are affected and cannot get out of that area,” he said.

Two bridges in Tarlac, the Agana Bridge and Aquino Bridge, were also damaged, and the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) was rushing repairs and plans to install a temporary bridge while alternate routes were being used.

“The DPWH is rushing the bridge there in Tarlac. They will use a temporary bridge and alternate roads. The repair continues and hopefully, alternate routes can be used first while these bridges are being repaired,” Alejandro said.

The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), meanwhile, confirmed on Tuesday that it has recovered the remains of one of the five people who were aboard a vehicle that fell into the Tarlac River after part of the Agana Bridge collapsed in Tarlac City last Aug. 29.
The body was found in the waters off Barangay Pugaro in Dagupan City, Pangasinan, on Aug. 31, two days after the bridge incident.
Resources
The OCD said the government still has resources available for continuing response operations despite the scale and duration of the disaster.

Alejandro said the Department of Social Welfare and Development alone has P2.3 billion in standby funds and nearly 900,000 family food packs available. Another 35,000 ready-to-eat food packs are also on hand while quick response funds of agencies such as the OCD remain available.

The latest OCD assessment placed infrastructure damage at P6.27 billion and agricultural losses at P2.32 billion. About 3,700 houses were damaged, including 3,300 partially damaged and 458 totally destroyed.
The government has provided P1.79 billion worth of assistance to affected communities.
PH Navy to the rescue
The Philippine Navy (PN), meanwhile, continued humanitarian assistance and disaster response operations in Metro Manila and Central Luzon.
The Navy said the Tanging Yaman Foundation Inc. provided 50 sacks of rice to support relief operations for families affected by habagat in Metro Manila.

The 3rd Marine Rifle Battalion coordinated with the Malabon City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office, while the 1st Marine Rifle Battalion engaged with the Valenzuela City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council for the inspection of disaster response equipment and support facilities.
The Philippine Marine Ready Force-National Capital Region and the 1st Marine Rifle Battalion also conducted a “Libreng Sakay” operation for stranded commuters in Caloocan, Valenzuela, and Pasay.

In Minalin, Pampanga, the Disaster Response and Rescue Team of Installation Management and Facilities-Northern Luzon conducted house-to-house rescue and evacuation operations in Barangay Sta. Rita amid waist-deep flooding.
The National Capital Region Command also kept its troops and search, rescue and retrieval teams on alert while coordinating with LGUs, DRRM offices, the MMDA and other agencies.
Despite the continuing rains, Alejandro said the OCD is focused on ensuring that assistance reaches communities that are becoming vulnerable to flooding.
He urged residents who need immediate assistance to use the Unified 911 emergency number or contact their local disaster risk reduction and management offices.

“The general number that is being used is the Unified 911. We can call there in case we need help. Also get in touch with your local DRRM offices so we can augment or send additional resources on the ground,” Alejandro said.

articles.title: DOE announces LPG price rollback for September
articles.summary: The Department of Energy (DOE) announced that consumers will see lower cooking fuel prices this month, as liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) rates drop by ₱0.40 per kilogram. This translates to a ₱4.40…

blocks.text: The Department of Energy (DOE) announced that consumers will see lower cooking fuel prices this month, as liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) rates drop by ₱0.40 per kilogram.
This translates to a ₱4.40 reduction for a standard 11-kilogram cylinder.
For September, domestic retail prices for an 11-kilogram LPG cylinder are estimated to range between ₱1,031 and ₱1,536, depending on the brand, location, and specific market factors.
Although the price cut is modest, Energy Secretary Sharon S. Garin noted that every bit of savings matters for families managing everyday household expenses.

"For families who rely on LPG to prepare their meals every day, every peso saved can go toward other household needs," Garin said. "The reduction may be modest, but consumers should benefit whenever market conditions bring costs down."

The DOE noted that international LPG contract prices for September were heavily influenced by higher crude oil prices, geopolitical tensions, Middle East supply constraints, and stronger Asian demand ahead of the winter season.
Garin also stressed the importance of transparency in retail pricing, adding that the agency will continue tracking market movements so consumers can plan accordingly.

“Consumers should be able to understand what drives the prices they pay,” Garin added. “We will continue to provide clear information on LPG price movements so households can make informed decisions and better manage their expenses.”

The price rollback materialized even as the international LPG Contract Price (CP) climbed to $649.50 per metric ton in September from $634.00 in August. That increase was offset by a drop in freight shipping rates—down to $94.41 per metric ton from $120.82—and a slightly stronger peso, which averaged ₱61.40 against the US dollar in August compared to ₱61.59 in July. Together, these lower underlying costs reduced the overall landed import cost of LPG. (Gabriell Christel Galang)

articles.title: Ravelas weighs in on GCash’s landmark ₱92-billion IPO
articles.summary: The upcoming ₱92.3-billion initial public offering (IPO) of Globe Telecom Inc. and Ayala Corp.’s fintech arm, Mynt Inc., is shaping up to become the largest stock debut in the local capital market…

blocks.text: The upcoming ₱92.3-billion initial public offering (IPO) of Globe Telecom Inc. and Ayala Corp.’s fintech arm, Mynt Inc., is shaping up to become the largest stock debut in the local capital market history, with an indicative maximum offer price set at ₱10 per share.

However, veteran market analyst and senior adviser at Reyes Tacandong & Co. Jonathan Ravelas explained that the maximum target price for the IPO of the parent company behind dominant mobile wallet GCash represents a regulatory ceiling rather than a target valuation.

The success of an initial public offering is evaluated through investor demand, the quality of participating institutional shareholders, domestic capital market development, and sustained value creation over time, rather than whether the final offering price matches an initial cap, according to Ravelas.

Historical equity listings in the country support this approach, as several high-profile corporate debuts were finalized below their initial registration ceilings to ensure adequate demand and secondary market stabilization. Transactions including Converge ICT Solutions Inc., Monde Nissin Corp., Puregold Price Club Inc., Wilcon Depot Inc., and MREIT Inc. adjusted their offer pricing during bookbuilding to reflect real-time investor feedback and broader financial conditions.

The maximum price indicated in preliminary filings serves primarily as a regulatory threshold rather than an absolute transaction target. Institutional asset managers perform detailed financial valuation models, with the final offer price emerging through transparent market price discovery. The priority remains aligning company valuation with sustained performance once secondary market trading begins.

For local retail investors, the stock market debut represents an entry point into the broader expansion of the domestic digital financial ecosystem rather than a short-term trading exercise tied strictly to first-day price swings.

Unlike many regional technology startups, GCash stands out by turning expanding user scale into consistent operational profits. The financial technology enterprise has delivered a return-on-equity of about 30 percent over recent reporting periods.

While some market participants have expressed caution regarding potential revenue impacts from fee waivers on certain digital transactions, the strategy aims to deepen user engagement and expand overall network activity.

Lowering entry barriers drives transaction volume across adjacent financial channels, expanding cross-selling opportunities in micro-lending, digital wealth management, insurance distribution, and merchant payment systems. Reducing direct friction costs helps accelerate broader consumer adoption, enlarging the total addressable market for all digital economy players.

articles.title: Shein shares slide on fast-fashion retailer’s stock market debut
articles.summary:
Hong Kong flotation at $26bn by firm once valued at $100bn follows failure to list in US and UK

Shares in the fast-fashion brand Shein slumped by as much as 10% as the China-founded company…

blocks.text: Shares in the fast-fashion brand Shein slumped as much as 10% as the China-founded company made its long-anticipated trading debut on the Hong Kong stock exchange.
The Singapore-headquartered company, once valued at almost $100bn (£74bn), went public on Tuesday pricing shares at HK$48.56, valuing the business at just over $26bn.

However, minutes after the flotation, which raised HK$13.6bn, the stock fell as much as 10%, pushing the online retailer’s valuation below $25bn. Shein’s share price recovered some ground to be 4% below its offer price by the end of trading, at HK$46.62.
“Let global consumers enjoy the sound of fashion,” said Leigh Gui, Shein’s chief financial officer, after a gong was struck to mark the start of trading.

The lacklustre launch as a publicly listed company comes after one of the longest-awaited initial public offerings in recent years, after plans to list in New York were blocked by regulators over forced labour concerns.
Shein also considered a £50bn flotation in London but faced similar questions about its supply chain from campaigners, MPs and investors.

The plunge in value has been driven by regulatory changes around the world that threaten its business model of shipping goods in small packages out of China to take advantage of tax breaks on low-value imported goods.

Shein swung to a loss of $99m in the first three months of this year, compared with a net income of $395m the year before, after the US removed its “de minimis” import duty exemption on small packages, hitting its sales in the country.

The EU is also cracking down on the loophole – introducing a €3 (£2.56) duty on small parcels imported from outside the trading bloc in June – and intends to phase it out, while the UK has said it will do the same by October 2028.

Nevertheless, the company has still become one of the world’s biggest listed fashion groups, with a valuation around the same as the Swedish retailer H&M. The Zara owner, Inditex, has a market capitalisation of about $213bn.
after newsletter promotion
Shein moved its headquarters to Singapore at about the start of 2022, a move viewed by analysts as designed to avoid increasing scrutiny of Chinese companies.

Founded by the entrepreneur Chris Xu, the company runs most of its operations from China but sells all its goods outside the country. It reached a valuation of $100bn in an April 2022 fundraising round, making it the third most valuable startup in the world at the time.

After forced labour concerns were raised, Shein said it had tightened its supplier policies, enforced through regular audits, with any child or forced labour violations becoming grounds for immediate termination of contract.

articles.title: Nigeria rethinks criminalization of suicide
articles.summary: LAGOS — In Nigeria, surviving a suicide attempt can mean facing not only the trauma of the ordeal but also the threat of prosecution. Laws dating back decades, including some inherited from the…

blocks.text: LAGOS — In Nigeria, surviving a suicide attempt can mean facing not only the trauma of the ordeal but also the threat of prosecution.
Laws dating back decades, including some inherited from the colonial era, criminalize attempted suicide — and, advocates say, deter people in crisis from seeking the care they need.
The government now says those laws have run their course and must change.
Africa’s most populous country records about 300,000 suicide attempts annually, with at least 7,000 deaths, according to health minister Mohammed Ali Pate, citing World Health Organization figures.
“Suicide is a major public health concern in Nigeria,” Pate told journalists in August. “The idea is attempted suicide is not a crime.”
Criminalising suicide attempts discourages people from seeking urgent help, said Kingsley Okonoda, a professor of psychiatry at the University of Jos.
“So many people will not present for treatment or will not come out even after the attempted suicide has failed because of fear of being prosecuted,” Okonoda told AFP.
Limited access to treatment
Pate said the government would send a bill to the National Assembly to push forward with the decriminalization plan, with the aim of reducing suicide deaths and attempts by 15 percent by 2030.

Across Nigeria’s 36 states, suicide attempts typically carry a one-year prison term, though in Muslim-majority Jigawa, governed under sharia in parallel to the state and federal justice systems, the penalty can be as high as five years, according to Decriminalize Suicide Worldwide, an advocacy campaign.
Supporters of the reform are calling for the federal government to harmonize the law across the country — and also warn decriminalization alone may not be enough.
Less than 35 percent of Nigerians believe people in their communities can access help for mental or emotional problems, according to a 2024 report from Afrobarometer, a pollster.
Stigma remains a major barrier to treatment, with many Nigerians still viewing mental health problems as spiritual afflictions.

Nigeria also faces a severe shortage of qualified medical professionals, with fewer than 1,000 psychiatrists serving more than 200 million people, according to 2024 figures from the Association of Psychiatrists in Nigeria (APN).
“Decriminalizing suicide must be accompanied by a deliberate expansion of access to quality mental health services. Accessibility must be matched by affordability,” APN said in a statement to AFP.
Economic crisis, insecurity
Along with the proposed amendments, experts said the government must also address factors that predispose people to suicide.
Economic hardship, rising poverty, insecurity and social isolation are among the drivers of mental illness and suicidal behaviour, according to the APN.

The country has endured years of economic strain, with President Bola Tinubu’s major reforms blamed for pushing up the cost of living, even as the government says they are attracting international investment and creating macroeconomic stability.

Inflation reached a record high of 34 percent in mid-2024 before slowing to 15.4 percent in July. Poverty has continued to rise, affecting 63 percent of the population, according to the International Monetary Fund.

The country is also grappling with a 17-year jihadist insurgency in the northeast. Rampant kidnap-for-ransom attacks and farmer-herder violence wrack the north-central region, while secessionist agitation rumbles on in the southeast.

The government “has a crucial role to play beyond the health sector. Every meaningful intervention that makes life safer, more dignified and more economically viable is, in itself, a mental health intervention and suicide prevention,” APN said.
A suicide prevention bill submitted by several NGOs to the National Assembly in 2024, seeking to protect the “rights of persons with suicidal behaviour”, is yet to be passed.
Promoters said the bill would complement proposed amendments to the country’s existing mental health laws.
“The amendment and the National Suicide Prevention Bill are two halves of one reform,” said Taiwo Lateef Sheikh, of the Nigeria Suicide Prevention Advocacy Working Group.
“One removes the punishment, the other builds what should be there instead.” /dl

If you or someone you know is in need of assistance, please reach out to the National Center for Mental Health (NCMH). Their crisis hotlines are available at 1553 (Luzon-wide landline toll-free), 0917-899-USAP (8727), 0966-351-4518, and 0908-639-2672. For more information, visit their website: (https://doh.gov.ph/NCMH-Crisis-Hotline)

Alternatively, you can contact Hopeline PH at the following numbers: 0917-5584673, 0918-8734673, 88044673. Additional resources are available at ngf-mindstrong.org, or connect with them on Facebook at Hopeline PH.

articles.title: Next stop for Myanmar leader’s diplomatic tour: Vietnam
articles.summary: YANGON — Myanmar’s junta-chief turned president, Min Aung Hlaing, will visit Vietnam this weekend, both nations said Tuesday, the latest trip on a regional drive for diplomatic…

blocks.text: YANGON — Myanmar’s junta-chief turned president, Min Aung Hlaing, will visit Vietnam this weekend, both nations said Tuesday, the latest trip on a regional drive for diplomatic recognition.
Min Aung Hlaing triggered Myanmar’s civil war as armed forces chief in 2021 by ousting the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi and detaining her.
In April, he took over as civilian president after staging highly restricted elections, and is now waging a diplomatic offensive to end his country’s pariah status abroad.
The Myanmar foreign ministry said he would meet President To Lam in Vietnam, as well as Prime Minister Le Minh Hung and the president of the national assembly.
“Furthermore, the president will attend the Myanmar-Vietnam Business Forum 2026 and the itinerary includes visits to digital and electronic technology industries,” it said in a statement.
It did not specify the dates of the visit, which it said aims to promote “mutually beneficial cooperation between the two governments”.
Vietnam state media said he would be in the Communist nation from September 4 to 6.
Much of the international community shunned Myanmar’s leadership after the coup, which triggered a civil war that some monitors estimate to have claimed 100,000 lives.
But there has been a shift since the elections.
The vote has been dismissed in many quarters as a charade, as it excluded Suu Kyi’s party and was blocked from huge tracts of rebel-held territory, while dissenters were jailed.
Yet India, Laos and Thailand — neighbouring nations sharing unavoidable border issues with Myanmar — have all welcomed Min Aung Hlaing since he became civilian president.
Defending the decision to host the Myanmar leader in Bangkok last month, Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow told reporters: “It’s not about legitimacy, it’s about reality.”
Min Aung Hlaing was also recently feted during visits to steadfast allies Russia and Belarus.
China — which previously backed him behind the scenes, according to analysts — also granted him a red carpet welcome in Beijing in June. /dl

articles.title: How China buried Tibet flood images after Nepal disaster
articles.summary: When a catastrophic flash flood swept through the rugged China-Nepal border on August 26, the physical devastation was immediate. In Nepal, a black torrent of mud and rock tore through communities,…

blocks.text: When a catastrophic flash flood swept through the rugged China-Nepal border on August 26, the physical devastation was immediate.
In Nepal, a black torrent of mud and rock tore through communities, leaving hundreds dead and thousands more missing along the borderlands.

But across the frontier in Tibet, an autonomous region of China, the physical disaster was almost instantly followed by a digital one: the rapid, high-tech erasure of the catastrophe’s visual evidence.

As survivors tried to upload raw footage of the deluge, China’s state-backed information control apparatus swung into action, executing a sophisticated, precision operation to shape the public narrative and bury inconvenient truths.
The contrasting realities — a tragic humanitarian crisis in Nepal and a tightly sanitized, triumphant rescue narrative in China — reveal the evolving mechanics of Beijing’s modern censorship machine.

Rather than imposing a blunt, blanket blackout, authorities deployed advanced image-recognition technology and “saturated information” tactics to drown out domestic scrutiny while deflecting diplomatic friction abroad.
Collapse of the border gate
In the immediate aftermath of the flood-triggered mudslide, local residents captured dramatic footage of the torrent engulfing Gyirong Port, a critical overland trade hub between China and Nepal.
The most striking video showed a black wall of water and debris crashing into and destroying the “national” border gate.

In an article titled “An Unrecorded Mudslide Rushes into Gyirong Port” on China’s WeChat, a universal app that combines messaging with payment options and social media functions, local blogger “Matou Qingnian” described the chaotic scene.

“The most terrifying moment happened at the Gyirong Port,” the author wrote, describing video footage of crowds, including children, fleeing in panic before a pitch-black torrent swallowed the camera’s view.
Within hours, both the article and the raw video footage had vanished from Chinese social media.

According to China Digital Times (CDT), an independent watchdog that tracks Chinese internet censorship, the video of the collapsing border gate was systematically blocked from being shared on WeChat, even in private messages.

“The footage itself contained no graphic violence, no protests, and no political slogans,” explained Mira, a CDT editor who specializes in tracking sensitive keywords and media. “The target of the censorship was the symbol itself: the National Gate.”

Digital analysts note that this censorship highlights a significant upgrade in China’s internet policing tools. Instead of merely filtering text-based keywords, platforms now rely heavily on video fingerprinting, image hashing and machine-learning models to recognize specific visual scenes.
Once a visual sequence is blacklisted, it is intercepted before it can ever be posted.
Satiety as a shield: The art of ‘saturated’ censorship
The suppression of the Gyirong Port disaster reflects a broader shift in Beijing’s strategy: from mass deletion to “precision surgery” and narrative flooding.
A search for “Tibet mudslide” on Xiaohongshu — China’s popular lifestyle and search platform — reveals the mechanics of this “saturated information environment.”
Rather than showing an empty search page, the platform’s algorithm feeds users a carefully curated stream of state-media reports from China’s state broadcaster CCTV and news agency Xinhua.

The visual landscape is dominated by high-resolution, sterile graphics: “before-and-after” comparisons, maps of high-altitude glacial collapses — the official scientific cause of the disaster — and state-approved aerial drone footage.
The raw, chaotic cellphone videos recorded by eyewitnesses at the border are entirely absent.

By filling the digital space with a high volume of “safe” and visually appealing official content, the state satisfies the public’s immediate curiosity while preemptively suffocating independent reporting or organic discussions, analysts note.

blocks.caption: Rescuers have been carrying out search-and-rescue operations at the mudslide-hit Gyirong Port since last Wednesday Image: Lhasa Fire and Rescue Mobile Detachment/Handout/Xinhua/picture alliance

blocks.text: On Weibo, China’s microblogging giant, the narrative arc was similarly managed. While “Tibet mudslide” briefly trended on August 26, the domestic casualty figures were quickly frozen the next morning at three dead and 558 missing.
Almost immediately, the platform’s trending topics were redirected toward the government’s swift response.

Two heavily publicized, lengthy official reports dominated the news cycle: Chinese President Xi Jinping convening a Central Politburo meeting to coordinate rescue and relief efforts, and Premier Li Qiang arriving in Gyirong to personally direct operations on the ground.
These headlines effectively turned a major human tragedy into a highly orchestrated exhibition of state competence.
Dangerous ‘half-year’ question
Beneath the veneer of efficient state rescue efforts lies a deeper, systemic vulnerability that Beijing was desperate to hide: a history of structural negligence.

On August 27, a hashtag briefly slipped through the censors and trended on Weibo: “Gyirong Port Reopened Only Half a Year Ago.” It amassed over 347,000 views in less than an hour before it was abruptly deleted. The hashtag pointed to a damning timeline of infrastructure failures.

In July 2025, Gyirong Port was completely shut down after being devastated by another severe flash flood. It took nearly six months to rebuild and reopen the port on January 1 of this year. Eight months later, the port has been destroyed again.

As the deleted “Matou Qingnian” article noted, Gyirong Port has now suffered mudslides during the flood seasons of 2024, 2025 and now 2026. In 2025, several Chinese personnel went missing or were killed.
By erasing the “half-year” trend, censors blocked an inevitable and dangerous train of public inquiry.

If the state-of-the-art border facility was destroyed twice in 14 months, it raises critical questions about site selection, shoddy infrastructure construction, and the complete failure of glacial lake monitoring and early-warning systems in Tibet.

These questions are especially sensitive in Tibet, a region under intense security and political control since the 1950s. Foreign journalists are strictly barred from entering the region outside of highly choreographed government-led tours.
According to human rights groups, local Tibetans who attempt to speak with foreign journalists or share independent accounts online face immediate detention or arrest.
High-altitude friction
The informational firewall does not stop at China’s borders; it has also created a diplomatic rift with neighboring Nepal, which has borne the brunt of the disaster’s human toll.
Parshuram Kaphle, a prominent Nepalese foreign policy journalist, publicly accused Beijing on X (formerly Twitter) of failing to share critical trans-boundary data.

“Nepal has been addressing the legitimate security concerns of our neighbors,” Kaphle wrote in a post that has since been deleted. “However, it must be said with sadness that our northern neighbor has significantly undermined us. By failing to provide early warning of such a massive disaster, we suffered immense loss of human life.”

He further wrote: “We have continually faced crises originating from their territory, while we continue to address all their concerns, necessary or unnecessary. Why must Nepal alone pay the price of one-sided love?”

The Chinese government has rejected any accountability. On August 27, the Chinese Embassy in Nepal issued a statement on Facebook, dismissing accusations of failing to issue warnings or causing the disaster through upstream dam failures as “fake news.”
“Accusation helps nothing,” the embassy statement read. “Cooperation saves lives.”
But for families searching for the thousands of missing loved ones along the muddy banks of the Himalayan border, cooperation remains as obscured as the truth behind the digital firewall. /dl

articles.title: SSS targets ₱1.44-trillion investment portfolio as stocks rebound, property earnings surge
articles.summary: State-run Social Security System (SSS) has set its sights on hitting ₱1.44 trillion in investments this year, half of which will be placed in government securities (GS), while stocks and corporate…

blocks.text: State-run Social Security System (SSS) has set its sights on hitting ₱1.44 trillion in investments this year, half of which will be placed in government securities (GS), while stocks and corporate bonds will take up sizable shares.

SSS President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Robert Joseph Montes De Claro reported during the pension fund’s 69th anniversary on Tuesday, Sept. 1 that, as of midyear, SSS’ total investments stood at ₱1.27 trillion, yielding ₱27.2 billion in income.
For the full year, SSS has estimated total investments to grow 13.4 percent to ₱1.44 trillion, with actual income expected to increase nearly threefold to ₱71.4 billion.
SSS Commissioner Victor Alfonso A. Limlingan said during the event that SSS is carefully balancing the security of the fund’s members with the need to improve financial gains.

“It’s a tricky balancing act. We don’t want to be too conservative because then we won’t generate the income necessary to pay for pensions. At the same time, we need to be a little more aggressive,” Limlingan said.

Of SSS’ total investments as of end-June, government debt papers accounted for ₱692.1 billion, taking up more than half of the investment portfolio and yielding actual income of ₱16 billion. Estimates showed this will expand to ₱724.1 billion, yielding ₱2 billion by year-end.

Investments in corporate notes and bonds stood at ₱96.3 billion, generating income of ₱3.2 billion. This segment of the fund’s portfolio posted a return on investment (ROI) of more than seven percent.
Estimates by SSS pointed to an investment total of ₱104.7 billion by year-end, with ₱5.4 billion in income. However, the ROI is expected to ease to 6.63 percent.

SSS also invested ₱31.74 billion in the money market in the first half, generating ₱1.14 billion in actual income and a 6.62-percent ROI. Unlike the capital market, the money market handles short-term borrowing and lending of one year or less.
Investments in the money market are expected to grow by a quarter to ₱39.8 billion by end-2026, generating ₱2 billion in income.
Other capital investments were ₱6.1 billion in mutual funds and ₱10.8 billion in externally managed funds. Combined income from these investments stood at ₱229 million.

By end-2026, mutual funds are expected to inch up to ₱6.3 billion, while SSS will trim externally managed funds to ₱8.6 billion. Combined earnings from these segments are seen growing to ₱650 million.

Notably, SSS incurred an investment loss of ₱998 million from its holdings in the local stock market, which stood at ₱179.4 billion as of end-June. However, SSS is looking at increasing its stock investments to ₱191 billion by end-2026, on a projection that the latest loss will reverse into income of ₱8 billion.
It also bears noting that SSS has already earmarked ₱15 billion for foreign investments in the second half of 2026, which De Claro said could stand at ₱20 billion in 2027.

On the lending front, member loans hit ₱151.9 billion in June, with actual income of ₱6.15 billion. SSS projects these loans to modestly increase to ₱153.7 billion by the end of the year, with the ROI easing to the mid-five-percent range from the end-June level of 8.9 percent.
Pension loans stood at ₱11.4 billion, with actual income of ₱451 million. This is forecast to grow to ₱14.1 billion, bringing in ₱743 million in earnings.
Total capital for the new microloan product stood at ₱4.2 billion, raking in ₱80 million in the first few months after its launch early this year.

Ultimately, the fund invested ₱154.6 billion in property, generating ₱906 million in actual income. SSS expects this to grow to ₱179.4 billion by year-end, with income seen spiking to ₱11.8 billion—soaring by more than 1,200 percent from the end-June figure.
Limlingan said the fund’s investment in real estate assets is among the best-performing investments in its portfolio.

“Many of our members are very young, and they won’t need to draw on their contributions until much later in life,” Limlingan said. “Therefore, our experience has been that our best-performing investment, as many of you have probably confirmed, is real estate, which tends to increase in value over the long term.”
Limlingan further explained that while real estate does not necessarily generate strong returns quickly, it has historically tended to appreciate and generate reliable returns over a longer period.
As of end-July, SSS’ net income grew 15.6 percent to ₱55.5 billion from the end-June level of ₱48 billion.
Member contributions rose 17.5 percent in July to ₱235.3 billion from ₱200.3 billion logged in the first half.

Additionally, the mandatory provident fund (MPF) increased to ₱263.12 billion, covering 9.18 million members, from ₱255.63 billion, covering 9.06 million members. MPF is an automatic retirement savings program for members whose monthly salary credit exceeds ₱20,000.
Meanwhile, SSS has spent ₱7.1 billion as of end-July, which the pension fund said was equivalent to roughly a fourth of the ₱29.2-billion charter limit.

articles.title: Times Square stabbing in NYC leaves 1 dead, assailant killed
articles.summary: A woman armed with two kitchen knives killed one person and wounded another in New York City's Times Square before police fatally shot her. Authorities said the attack was random and unprovoked.

image.caption: The attack was not believed to be terror-related, authorities said Image: Kyle Mazza/Anadolu/picture alliance

blocks.text: A woman with two kitchen knives fatally stabbed one person and wounded another in New York City's popular Times Square on Monday before police shot and killed her, officials said.
The knife attack occurred just before 4:30 pm near a police substation outside One Times Square, the building known for hosting the city's annual New Year's Eve ball drop.
What do we know about the Times Square knife attack?

New York City Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said the 49-year-old suspect from the borough of Queens pulled the knives from a shopping bag and stabbed a 68-year-old man in the abdomen as he exited a subway station with his wife. She then attacked a 32-year-old woman, stabbing her in the abdomen. Both victims were hospitalized, with the young woman dying of her wounds. The older man is currently in stable condition, police said.

blocks.caption: Authorities recovered two knives from the scene of the fatal stabbing incidentImage: Kyle Mazza/Anadolu/picture alliance

blocks.text: Officers surrounded the suspect and attempted to get her to drop the knives before deploying a Taser, which also failed to stop her, according to Tisch.
The suspect reportedly told officers, "I'm not dropping anything, I would rather kill both of you," before advancing toward them with the knives raised.
Multiple officers then opened fire, with bystander video showing her falling to the ground, where officers handcuffed her and administered first aid. She was later pronounced dead.
What did the authorities say?
"This was an extraordinarily dangerous situation unfolding in the heart of Times Square, the crossroads of the world," Tisch said.
She added the attack was random and unprovoked.
Tisch said the suspect had a documented history of mental health contacts with police, including incidents in 2018 and 2019, but no prior arrests.
Investigators do not believe the attack was terrorism-related, and police have not released the victims' identities pending notification of family.

blocks.caption: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch addressed the press in the aftermath of the attackImage: Kyle Mazza/Anadolu/picture alliance

blocks.text: Mayor Zohran Mamdani, told a news conference, "We know that those families' lives have been shattered by what took place today, and we will continue to hold them close as the hours and days and weeks continue from this moment."
Both Mamdani and Tisch credited the responding officers, saying their actions likely prevented further casualties.

The incident marks the second fatal stabbing in Times Square this year, following a similar attack in May, even as the New York City's overall homicide rate has dropped sharply to one of its lowest totals in decades.

articles.title: Metro Pacific’s water unit prepares ₱23-billion expansion push
articles.summary: Metro Pacific Water Inc. (MPW) plans to spend ₱23 billion over the next five years to upgrade infrastructure and expand its presence across local and Southeast Asian markets. In a statement, the…

blocks.text: Metro Pacific Water Inc. (MPW) plans to spend ₱23 billion over the next five years to upgrade infrastructure and expand its presence across local and Southeast Asian markets.

In a statement, the water investment arm of Metro Pacific Investments Corp., siad the capital expenditure program will fund network modernization, raw water source development, pipeline repairs, non-revenue water reduction, and the deployment of modular treatment systems.
MPW said the initiative aims to stabilize systems across the firm’s regional operations. The commitment comes as the company seeks to scale its coverage.

MPW urrently serves roughly 221,000 households in Iloilo, Dumaguete, and San Jose del Monte, Bulacan. Through joint ventures such as Metro Iloilo Bulk Water Supply Corp. and Cagayan de Oro Bulk Water Inc., the company manages bulk water infrastructure in the Philippines. Internationally, it supplies industrial zones in Vietnam’s Nghe An province through subsidiaries Tuan Loc Water Resources and Phu Ninh Water.
Metro Pacific Water President and Chief Executive Officer Andrew B. Pangilinan said the capital deployment is designed to strengthen long-term utility readiness and economic resilience.
“When we started Metro Pacific Water 15 years ago, our goal was to help build a more water-secure future for the communities we serve,” Pangilinan said.

“That mission has only become more urgent today. Water security is economic security, and this ₱23-billion investment is our commitment to building the infrastructure the next generation will depend on,” he added.

The company’s combined water production capacity reached 798 million liters per day in 2026, a 20 percent increase from 667 million liters per day in 2025 following asset rehabilitation and facility optimizations.

To address shortfalls in water-scarce areas, the firm deployed modular technologies, including brackish water and seawater reverse osmosis systems, to offer immediate supply relief while longer-term projects progress.

Operational gains were recorded across several key domestic markets. In Iloilo, daily available water supply reached 80 million liters per day, supported by the ongoing construction of a 66.5-million-liter desalination facility and the 86-million-liter Jalaur Water Treatment Project.

Production in Dumaguete City rose to 48.2 million liters per day, while the Cagayan de Oro unit maintained an output of 80 million liters per day, backed by infrastructure capable of delivering up to 100 million liters per day.
In Bulacan, Metro Pacific Water assumed interim operations of the San Jose del Monte water system through Metro Pacific Bulacan Water in 2026 to stabilize a grid affected by deferred maintenance.
Within three months, operating teams repaired more than 600 pipeline leaks and restored Water Treatment Plant 2 to its design capacity of 30 million liters per day.
Unit Metro Pacific Water Solutions has also completed more than 700 sewage treatment plant projects nationwide, expanding its footprint in municipal and industrial wastewater management.

Looking ahead, Pangilinan said the group plans to leverage its cross-border operational experience in Southeast Asia to deploy scalable technologies as demand for reliable utility infrastructure grows. (Gabriell Christel Galang)

articles.title: Zambia's president to be sworn in for second term while opponent detained
articles.summary: Hakainde Hichilema swept to victory, but his main rival is now in detention charged with treason.

blocks.text: Zambia's President Hakainde Hichilema is due to be sworn in for a second five-year term on Tuesday following a disputed election and the arrest of his main opponent on treason charges.

Hichilema – credited with stabilising the economy – swept to victory on 13 August with 60% of the vote, according to official results. Runner-up Brian Mundubile, who received 38%, alleged that the outcome had been tampered with.
He was unable to mount a legal challenge to the result as the courts were sealed off last week on the final day a case could be filed.
Election observers said that while polling day was largely peaceful, some have raised questions about the vote tallying process.

European Union observers said staff in many tallying centres did not record results on tally sheets as soon as they were announced, and cited weak verification between digital entries and paper records. It added that returning officers frequently paused proceedings while awaiting instructions from headquarters.
The day after the poll, security forces raided a property in the capital, Lusaka, linked to Mundubile, killing a former cabinet minister and arresting a number of opposition politicians.
The authorities accused the opposition of planning an armed insurrection, which they denied.
Mundubile and his running mate, Makebi Zulu, had gone into hiding. They were detained by police last week and charged at the weekend.
When Hichilema, 64, came into office in 2021 after a landslide victory, Zambia had recently defaulted on its international debt and had an annual inflation rate of more than 24%.
"We inherited a broken-down country… the economy was declining," Hichilema told the BBC in Lusaka before the election.

The former businessman negotiated a restructuring of the debt and rebuilt relations with foreign creditors. Inflation has also come down, but prices are still rising and many continue to struggle with the cost of living.
Hichilema now wants to build on the foundations he said he laid over the past five years.
Botswana President Duma Boko and Tanzania's President Samia Suluhu Hassan are among several African leaders expected to attend the inauguration ceremony at the National Heroes Stadium in Lusaka.
Hichilema will be sworn in alongside his running mate, Mutale Nalumango.

articles.title: ‘The mountains are changing’: What the floods tell us about the future of India’s Himalayas
articles.summary: As families await news of missing loved ones, the disaster is a stark reminder of how the climate crisis is creating a fast-growing threat. Plus, the town considered India’s ‘Jurassic…

blocks.text: It has been hard not to despair while watching the ruinous floods swallow parts of Nepal, and harder, still knowing that the agony compounds each passing day for dozens of Indian families whose members remain unaccounted for.

Social media is awash with desperate pleas, photos and details of the young and old, men and women, from Mumbai to Kolkata, posted by families searching for traces of life. The disaster unfolded when a melting glacier slammed into the valley below, unleashing a deadly cascade of rock and ice down the Bhote Kashi River, which flows from Tibet into Nepal.

Among the 275 Indians missing at the time of writing are workers of a hydropower project and people undertaking the Hindu pilgrimage to Mount Kailash in Tibet. Another 128 people of Indian origin, including a large group of Sadhguru’s Isha Foundation spiritual group, are also missing; 149 Indian people have been rescued as of Monday.

For Gauri Joshi, whose five relatives remained unaccounted for over the weekend, the last few days have been a blur of calling their numbers in vain, watching news of rescue operations and trying to reach Indian officials – over and over again. What she has pieced together so far is that her relatives, part of a pilgrim tour group from Maharashtra, cleared immigration at the Gyirong border between Nepal and Tibet and boarded buses shortly before the flood waters destroyed the crossing.
“Chances appear very bleak now. But maybe a miracle will happen,” Joshi said.

The tragedy has reignited the question of how vulnerable the Himalayas are to climate change, and what its implications are for India. To understand the risks of glacier collapse and thawing permafrost leading to sudden floods and debris flows, I spoke to Dr Ashim Sattar, a professor at Indian Institute of Technology Bhubaneswar and an expert on glacial lake outburst floods. The conversation has been edited and condensed.
What are the climate- or glacier-related risks emerging across the Himalayas?

“There are different forms of cryosphere and how they pose a hazard. In a layperson’s terms, the cryosphere is where water exists in solid form, for example a glacier. When it melts, it forms glacial lakes. If they have an outburst, they can cause damage downstream.

Another cryospheric component is glacier ice. This is what we’ve seen in Nepal, where a glacier detachment happened. The frontal part of the glacier detached from the main glacier and eventually led to a debris flow.

The third component is permafrost. They exist widely in the Himalayas, but there has not been much monitoring because it’s very difficult. Everything – these lakes, glaciers and permafrost – are all hazards. Unless they’re triggered, they would not cause damage.

With climate change, these grounds will go above zero degrees and will start to degrade. These would need very little … to mobilise debris. We might expect a higher frequency of debris flows in the future. We won’t know how they are getting conditioned, unless we have some monitoring stations and scientific investigation.

And given the Himalayas are very vast, monitoring every part of it becomes tricky. It can be the mountain ranges within India, or maybe outside India, eventually, which drains into the Indian subcontinent. That needs to be well studied.”

blocks.caption: ‘[Floods] might happen any time’ … a Devighat resident retrieves some of his belongings. Photograph: Ahmer Khan/The Guardian

blocks.text: How big are the downstream risks for India?

“Right now, this is a gap in scientific studies; nothing [is] quantified yet. There is direct evidence of climate impacts, even in the Indian part of the Himalayas. The number of glacial lakes is increasing, the size of glacial lakes is increasing, the volume of glacial lakes is increasing, and glaciers are retreating. The risk exists because it might happen any time.”
Which parts of India are the most vulnerable?

“Everyone in the Himalayas, every Himalayan state has hazards. We can’t deny it. If you look at the eastern side, they have a lot of glacial lakes. They have already reached their maximum extent. Most full-grown lakes are about to reach their limits, like maximum extent. In the western Himalayas or even the central Himalayas, there’s a lot of scope for the lakes because they have not reached their full extent. As the glaciers would retreat, they would keep on growing.

We are still unsure when the status is going to change for any of these states. That’s a very, very difficult question, and I don’t think anyone [can] answer it at this moment without any scientific investigation.”

How would you describe India’s early warning systems and disaster preparedness?“The National Disaster Management Authority is taking proactive steps now with the glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) Risk Mitigation Programme to install early-warning systems.

Maybe an early warning system should be community-based. It should be for the people and by the people. It’s not always the scientist or the policymakers who can actually make this work at its full potential. We need to have local knowledge, involve the communities to make them more effective.”
How long will it take to have these systems in place?

“I have no idea because each of these organisations are working at their own pace. They have their own style of working. I’m sure it is going to happen soon. I can just comment on the areas where I know, and I’ve been in touch.”
Is prevention possible, or can it only minimise the damage?

“Prevention is possible, but it is very expensive: computationally, financially and manpower-wise. Minimising is also possible. It would require a lot of intervention in the high mountains, which is very difficult in those terrains.

We know that the mountains are changing and the hazard levels are increasing, so the only way forward is to minimise the exposure to the risk below. That means how much of the hazard is going to interact with the downstream. If something is in the path, we remove them.”

blocks.text: Photographer Aashim Tyagi (@aashim), who once documented Art Deco architecture in Gujarat’s Balasinor, suggests a prehistoric side quest: “I was intrigued by the town’s reputation as the ‘Jurassic Park of India’ and a little digging led me to a dinosaur museum in neighbouring Raiyoli. It’s set amid open fields near one of Asia’s largest fossil beds where Rajasaurus narmadensis and a dozen other species once roamed. Much of the museum and the village’s paleontological preservation is owed to Aaliya Babi of Balasinor’s erstwhile royal family, earning her the nickname ‘Dinosaur Princess’. Balasinor and its dinosaur museum are a worthwhile detour from Ahmedabad or Baroda.”

articles.title: Putin proposes permanent Russia-China visa-free scheme in talks with Xi
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Monday expressed readiness to make the visa-free scheme with China permanent if Beijing considers it useful, as he held talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping in…

blocks.text: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Monday expressed readiness to make the visa-free scheme with China permanent if Beijing considers it useful, as he held talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Kyrgyzstan, Tass news agency reported.
The two countries have introduced an arrangement allowing each other’s nationals to stay for 30 days without a visa, with the measure effective until the end of 2027.

In the meeting held on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Bishkek, Putin noted that the visa-free travel had helped increase tourist flows between the two countries by 43 percent in the first half of 2026, according to Tass.

Putin also expressed his condolences to the families of the victims of catastrophic flash floods and mudslides along the Nepal-China border and wished for a “speedy recovery to all those affected,” the news agency said.

The two leaders, who last met in person in Beijing in May, briefly touched upon the Ukraine crisis, but it was not the main issue at their meeting, Tass quoted Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov as saying.
China and Russia have been strengthening their ties in recent years, with Beijing opposing Western sanctions on Moscow over its war against Ukraine. /dl
